This strategy is complementary to traditional model-dependent searches and can be integrated into the LHC trigger system to capture events that might otherwise be missed, thus enhancing the discovery potential for new physics phenomena.

title: Herbal medicine use in pregnancy: results of a multinational study
abstract: This multinational, cross-sectional, internet-based study investigated the prevalence and determinants of herbal medicine use during pregnancy among 9,459 women from 23 countries across Europe, North and South America, and Australia. The findings revealed that 28.9% of participants reported using herbal medicines during pregnancy, with significant regional variation—highest in Russia (69%), Eastern Europe (51.8%), and Australia (43.8%). Herbal medicines were most commonly used to manage pregnancy-related ailments such as colds and nausea, with ginger, cranberry, valerian, and raspberry being the most frequently reported herbs. Women more likely to use herbal medicines tended to be first-time mothers, non-smokers, users of folic acid, occasional alcohol consumers, students, or those with education beyond high school. While one in five women received a physician’s recommendation for herbal use, most initiated use independently. The study highlights widespread self-medication with herbal products during pregnancy and underscores the need for further research on their safety and efficacy in this population.

title: WikiPathways: Pathway Editing for the People
abstract: WikiPathways provides a collaborative platform for creating, updating, and sharing pathway diagrams and serves as an example of content curation by the biology community.

title: The EANM practice guidelines for bone scintigraphy
abstract: These EANM practice guidelines provide comprehensive recommendations for the performance, interpretation, and reporting of bone scintigraphy, a highly sensitive nuclear medicine imaging technique essential for evaluating skeletal pathology. The guidelines address the use of technetium-99m-labeled phosphate analogues, describe standard imaging protocols including planar, SPECT, and SPECT/CT acquisitions, and outline multiphase imaging approaches. They emphasize the importance of bone scintigraphy in detecting metabolic changes associated with malignant and benign bone diseases, often before radiological alterations become apparent. The document discusses clinical indications, technical considerations, and the complementary role of bone scintigraphy alongside other imaging modalities. Developed through consensus by EANM committees and informed by international standards, these guidelines aim to support practitioners in delivering high-quality, standardized care while acknowledging variability in resources and clinical scenarios.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

title: Small data machine learning in materials science
abstract: This review discussed the dilemma of small data faced by materials machine learning. First, we analyzed the limitations brought by small data. Then, the workflow of materials machine learning has been introduced. Next, the methods of dealing with small data were introduced, including data extraction from publications, materials database construction, high-throughput computations and experiments from the data source level; modeling algorithms for small data and imbalanced learning from the algorithm level; active learning and transfer learning from the machine learning strategy level. Finally, the future directions for small data machine learning in materials science were proposed.

title: The evolution and future of logistics and supply chain management
abstract: This article will be divided into three sections: past, present, and future. The past section will trace major events that created business logistics as it is practiced today. In particular, do the events portend the future of business logistics and supply chain management? The present section will attempt to summarize the state of business logistics. How business logistics relates to supply chain management will be addressed. The future section will make some predictions as to the issues that need to be addressed and the events that will likely take place in the near term.

title: Multimodal Emotion Recognition using Deep Learning
abstract: New research into human-computer interaction seeks to consider the consumer's emotional status to provide a seamless human-computer interface. This would make it possible for people to survive and be used in widespread fields, including education and medicine. Multiple techniques can be defined through human feelings, including expressions, facial images, physiological signs, and neuroimaging strategies. This paper presents a review of emotional recognition of multimodal signals using deep learning and comparing their applications based on current studies. Multimodal affective computing systems are studied alongside unimodal solutions as they offer higher accuracy of classification. Accuracy varies according to the number of emotions observed, features extracted, classification system and database consistency. Numerous theories on the methodology of emotional detection and recent emotional science address the following topics. This would encourage studies to understand better physiological signals of the current state of the science and its emotional awareness problems.
venue: Journal of Applied Science and Technology Trends

title: Stem cell paracrine actions and tissue regeneration.
abstract: Stem cells are central to regenerative medicine due to their ability to differentiate into diverse cell types, but emerging evidence highlights the significance of their paracrine actions—secretion of bioactive factors that influence the tissue microenvironment and modulate resident cell behavior. This review synthesizes current understanding of stem and progenitor cell trophic factor production, emphasizing their roles in promoting cell proliferation, cytoprotection, angiogenesis, immunomodulation, and extracellular matrix remodeling. The paracrine mechanisms of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), in particular, are explored with respect to immune modulation and support of hematopoiesis, as well as implications for tissue repair and cancer therapy. Advances in genomic and proteomic profiling have elucidated the spectrum of cytokines, growth factors, and other molecules secreted by various stem cell populations, informing strategies to harness these effects for therapeutic purposes. The article discusses methods to augment and direct stem cell paracrine actions, positioning stem/progenitor cells as complex biological delivery vehicles for regenerative applications. Understanding and manipulating these paracrine pathways hold promise for enhancing tissue regeneration and developing novel treatments for degenerative diseases and immune-related disorders.

title: Reported Subjective Well-Being: A Challenge for Economic Theory and Economic Policy
abstract: Over the past few years, there has been a steadily increasing interest from economists in happiness research. This paper argues that reported subjective well-being is a satisfactory empirical approximation to individual utility and endeavors to provide an impression of this new, and challenging, development. We study data from the German Socio-Economic Panel to understand (i) the role of aspirations in the relationship between income and happiness better and (ii) the effect of unemployment on people’s satisfaction with life. We discuss some of the consequences for economic policy and for economic theory.
venue: Journal of Contextual Economics – Schmollers Jahrbuch

title: Handbook of the Sociology of Gender
abstract: The Handbook of the Sociology of Gender offers a comprehensive and critical overview of contemporary sociological theories and research on gender as a pervasive social construct shaping all aspects of human life. Edited by Janet Saltzman Chafetz and featuring contributions from leading scholars, the volume addresses gender across micro, meso, and macro levels, examining its influence within social processes, structures, and major institutions such as the economy, family, polity, legal systems, health care, education, science, sport, and religion. Emphasizing comparative cross-national and historical perspectives, the handbook also highlights within-gender differences related to class, race/ethnicity, sexuality, and age. Rejecting a singular focus on women or men, it instead explores the dynamic relationships between genders and their roles in both dominant and subordinate positions. Divided into four sections—covering foundational issues, macrolevel structures and processes, microlevel interactions, and institutional contexts—the book aims to provide in-depth analyses for professional sociologists, graduate students, and interdisciplinary feminist scholars seeking an authoritative synthesis of current knowledge in gender sociology.

title: Business Practices in Small Firms in Developing Countries
abstract: This paper investigates the role of business practices in micro and small firms across seven developing countries by introducing a standardized set of 26 survey questions covering marketing, stock-keeping, record-keeping, and financial planning. Analysis reveals that variation in these business practices explains a significant share of differences in firm performance—measured by sales, profits, labor productivity, and total factor productivity—comparable to effects observed in larger firms. Panel data from three countries further show that better business practices predict higher firm survival rates and faster sales growth over time. The relationship between business practices and outcomes remains robust after controlling for owner human capital, with evidence that higher human capital, entrepreneurial family background, and having employees are associated with better practices. Competition shows weaker associations. Auditing exercises confirm the reliability of self-reported data. The findings suggest that improving business practices can substantially enhance performance even among the smallest firms in developing countries, challenging the view that formal management is less relevant in this context.

title: Technological Change and the Environment
abstract: Environmental policy discussions increasingly focus on issues related to technological change. This is partly because the environmental consequences of social activity are frequently affected by the rate and direction of technological change, and partly because environmental policy interventions can themselves create constraints and incentives that have significant effects on the path of technological progress. This paper, prepared as a chapter draft for the forthcoming Handbook of Environmental Economics (North-Holland/Elsevier Science), summarizes for environmental economists current thinking on technological change in the broader economics literature, surveys the growing economic literature on the interaction between technology and the environment, and explores the normative implications of these analyses. We begin with a brief overview of the economics of technological change, and then examine three important areas where technology and the environment intersect: the theory and empirical evidence of induced innovation and the related literature on the effects of environmental policy on the creation of new, environmentally friendly technology; the theory and empirics of environmental issues related to technology diffusion; and analyses of the comparative technological impacts of alternative environmental policy instruments. We conclude with suggestions for further research on technological change and the environment.

title: 18F labeled nanoparticles for in vivo PET-CT imaging.
abstract: We report the synthesis and in vivo characterization of an 18F modified trimodal nanoparticle (18F-CLIO). This particle consists of cross-linked dextran held together in core-shell formation by a superparamagnetic iron oxide core and functionalized with the radionuclide 18F in high yield via 'click' chemistry. The particle can be detected with positron emission tomography, fluorescence molecular tomography, and magnetic resonance imaging. The presence of 18F dramatically lowers the detection threshold of the nanoparticles, while the facile conjugation chemistry provides a simple platform for rapid and efficient nanoparticle labeling.

title: Herbal medicine research and global health: an ethical analysis.
abstract: Governments, international agencies and corporations are increasingly investing in traditional herbal medicine research. Yet little literature addresses ethical challenges in this research. In this paper, we apply concepts in a comprehensive ethical framework for clinical research to international traditional herbal medicine research. We examine in detail three key, underappreciated dimensions of the ethical framework in which particularly difficult questions arise for international herbal medicine research: social value, scientific validity and favourable risk-benefit ratio. Significant challenges exist in determining shared concepts of social value, scientific validity and favourable risk-benefit ratio across international research collaborations. However, we argue that collaborative partnership, including democratic deliberation, offers the context and process by which many of the ethical challenges in international herbal medicine research can, and should be, resolved. By 'cross-training' investigators, and investing in safety-monitoring infrastructure, the issues identified by this comprehensive framework can promote ethically sound international herbal medicine research that contributes to global health.
venue: Bulletin of the World Health Organization

title: Bayesian reasoning and machine learning
abstract: Machine learning methods extract value from vast data sets quickly and with modest resources. They are established tools in a wide range of industrial applications, including search engines, DNA sequencing, stock market analysis, and robot locomotion, and their use is spreading rapidly. People who know the methods have their choice of rewarding jobs. This hands-on text opens these opportunities to computer science students with modest mathematical backgrounds. It is designed for final-year undergraduates and master's students with limited background in linear algebra and calculus. Comprehensive and coherent, it develops everything from basic reasoning to advanced techniques within the framework of graphical models. Students learn more than a menu of techniques, they develop analytical and problem-solving skills that equip them for the real world. Numerous examples and exercises, both computer based and theoretical, are included in every chapter. Resources for students and instructors, including a MATLAB toolbox, are available online.

title: Post-Covid-19 Education and Education Technology ‘Solutionism’: a Seller’s Market
abstract: The Covid-19 pandemic and the social distancing that followed have affected all walks of society, also education. In order to keep education running, educational institutions have had to quickly adapt to the situation. This has resulted in an unprecedented push to online learning. Many, including commercial digital learning platform providers, have rushed to provide their support and ‘solutions’, sometimes for free. The Covid-19 pandemic has therefore also created a sellers’ market in ed-tech. This paper employs a critical lens to reflect on the possible problems arising from hasty adoption of commercial digital learning solutions whose design might not always be driven by best pedagogical practices but their business model that leverages user data for profit-making. Moreover, already before Covid-19, there has been increasing critique of how ed-tech is redefining and reducing concepts of teaching and learning. The paper also challenges the narrative that claims, ‘education is broken, and it should and can be fixed with technology’. Such technologization, often seen as neutral, is closely related to educationalization, i.e. imposing growing societal problems for education to resolve. Therefore, this is a critical moment to reflect how the current choices educational institutions are making might affect with Covid-19 education and online learning: Will they reinforce capitalist instrumental view of education or promote holistic human growth? This paper urges educational leaders to think carefully about the decisions they are currently making and if they indeed pave the way to a desirable future of education.

title: Magnetite and Green Rust: Synthesis, Properties, and Environmental Applications of Mixed-Valent Iron Minerals.
abstract: Mixed-valent iron minerals, particularly magnetite and green rust, play pivotal roles in environmental processes due to their unique structural, redox, and magnetic properties. This comprehensive review synthesizes current knowledge on the synthesis pathways—both abiotic and biotic—of these minerals, elucidates their structural characteristics, Fe(II):Fe(III) ratios, redox potentials, and magnetic behaviors, and examines their occurrence in natural and engineered environments. Advanced characterization techniques for identification and quantification are discussed in detail. The review further highlights the environmental applications of magnetite and green rust, focusing on their capacity for contaminant sorption, reductive transformation of pollutants, and facilitation of advanced oxidation processes for remediation purposes. By integrating findings across geochemistry, mineralogy, geomicrobiology, materials science, and environmental engineering, this article provides an authoritative resource for researchers investigating the reactivity and application potential of mixed-valent iron minerals in near-surface environments.

title: Techniques for extraction and isolation of natural products: a comprehensive review
abstract: Natural medicines were the only option for the prevention and treatment of human diseases for thousands of years. Natural products are important sources for drug development. The amounts of bioactive natural products in natural medicines are always fairly low. Today, it is very crucial to develop effective and selective methods for the extraction and isolation of those bioactive natural products. This paper intends to provide a comprehensive view of a variety of methods used in the extraction and isolation of natural products. This paper also presents the advantage, disadvantage and practical examples of conventional and modern techniques involved in natural products research.

title: A Reconsideration of Environmental Federalism
abstract: This paper critically examines the theory and practice of environmental federalism, focusing on the allocation of responsibilities for environmental standard-setting and regulation among different levels of government. Through the development of three benchmark cases—pure public goods, local public goods, and cases with interjurisdictional spillovers—the analysis provides a conceptual framework for evaluating when centralization or decentralization is most appropriate. The paper reviews both theoretical arguments and recent empirical evidence, particularly regarding concerns about a 'race to the bottom' in environmental standards under decentralized governance. Findings suggest that while central governments play a crucial role in addressing national or global pollutants and supporting research and information dissemination, there remain significant circumstances where decentralized standard-setting yields efficiency gains and better matches local preferences. The study concludes with reflections on the need for flexible, context-dependent approaches to environmental policymaking that balance the benefits of both centralized and decentralized governance structures.

title: More than tools? Making sense of the ongoing digitizations of higher education
abstract: This editorial introduces a special issue that critically examines the ongoing digitization of higher education, challenging the prevailing tendency to view digital technologies merely as neutral tools for learning. Drawing on diverse scholarly contributions, the issue interrogates the assumptions underpinning educational technology, highlighting the need for deeper engagement with questions of learning, pedagogy, and the broader social, political, and economic contexts in which digital technologies are deployed. The authors argue that current discourse often reduces education to learning processes, neglects robust pedagogical analysis, and overlooks the complex human dimensions of technology use. By foregrounding these neglected areas, the editorial calls for more nuanced and theoretically informed approaches to understanding and shaping the digital transformation of higher education.
venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education

title: Advanced Materials
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in the field of advanced materials, with a particular focus on nanostructured systems and their technological applications. Drawing on data from over 1000 literature references and updates to previous monographs, it highlights the development of correlating equations for the temperature dependence of heat capacities in liquids and reviews progress in agricultural formulation science, emphasizing the critical role of surfactants. The report also summarizes key outcomes from major international conferences, including the IUPAC Workshop on Nanostructured Advanced Materials and the International Conference on Solution Chemistry, which showcased interdisciplinary research spanning quantum structures, biological templating of nanomaterials, and solution chemistry. The paper underscores the importance of international collaboration, the integration of theoretical and experimental approaches, and the promotion of young scientists in advancing the field of advanced materials.

title: Self-assembling amphiphilic peptides
abstract: The self‐assembly of several classes of amphiphilic peptides is reviewed, and selected applications are discussed. We discuss recent work on the self‐assembly of lipopeptides, surfactant‐like peptides and amyloid peptides derived from the amyloid‐β peptide. The influence of environmental variables such as pH and temperature on aggregate nanostructure is discussed. Enzyme‐induced remodelling due to peptide cleavage and nanostructure control through photocleavage or photo‐cross‐linking are also considered. Lastly, selected applications of amphiphilic peptides in biomedicine and materials science are outlined. © 2014 The Authors. Journal of Peptide Science published by European Peptide Society and John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.

title: Systematic review approaches for climate change adaptation research
abstract: This paper examines the application of systematic review approaches to climate change adaptation research, addressing the growing need for methodological transparency and rigor in synthesizing evidence on adaptation policy and practice. While systematic reviews and realist review methods are well-established in the health sciences, their uptake in social and environmental sciences, particularly within adaptation research, remains limited. The paper analyzes existing research synthesis methodologies, discusses their relevance and adaptability to the complex and heterogeneous literature on climate change adaptation, and highlights the challenges of integrating diverse data sources and formats. Emphasizing the importance of clearly defined eligibility criteria, reproducible methods, and critical appraisal of study quality, the authors propose customized systematic review frameworks suited to the unique demands of adaptation research. The review offers practical guidelines and recommendations for conducting systematic reviews in this context, ultimately calling for further conceptual and methodological development to enhance the synthesis and tracking of adaptation actions across regions and sectors.

title: Evolutionary biology of aging
abstract: The evolutionary theory of aging Observation of aging Experimental tests of the evolutionary theory of aging Genetic mechanisms form the evolution of aging Comparative biology of aging An evolutionary perspective on organismal theories of aging An evolutionary perspective on cellular and molecular theories of aging The future of gerontology.

title: Telocytes in regenerative medicine
abstract: Telocytes (TCs) are a recently identified type of interstitial cell distinguished by their small cell bodies and extremely long, thin telopodes, with a presence documented across numerous tissues and organs. Characterized by unique ultrastructural and immunohistochemical features, TCs form extensive three-dimensional networks through homo- and heterocellular junctions, facilitating intercellular communication and the maintenance of tissue homeostasis. TCs interact closely with stem and progenitor cells within tissue niches, supporting their role in tissue repair and regeneration. This review summarizes current knowledge on the identification, distribution, and functional implications of TCs, highlighting their involvement in regenerative processes in organs such as the heart, lungs, skeletal muscle, skin, meninges, eye, liver, uterus, and urinary system. The therapeutic potential of targeting TCs—either alone or in combination with stem cells—is discussed as a novel strategy to enhance tissue regeneration and prevent irreversible damage. Further exploration of methods to promote TC growth may offer innovative approaches in regenerative medicine beyond traditional stem cell transplantation.
venue: Journal of Cellular and Molecular Medicine

title: Euclid. I. Overview of the Euclid mission
abstract: The current standard model of cosmology successfully describes a variety of measurements, but the nature of its main ingredients, dark matter and dark energy, remains unknown. is a medium-class mission in the Cosmic Vision 2015--2025 programme of the European Space Agency (ESA) that will provide high-resolution optical imaging, as well as near-infrared imaging and spectroscopy, over about 14\,000\,deg$^2$ of extragalactic sky. In addition to accurate weak lensing and clustering measurements that probe structure formation over half of the age of the Universe, its primary probes for cosmology, these exquisite data will enable a wide range of science. This paper provides a high-level overview of the mission, summarising the survey characteristics, the various data-processing steps, and data products. We also highlight the main science objectives and expected performance.

title: Pollution Comes Home and Gets Personal: Women's Experience of Household Chemical Exposure∗
abstract: We report on interviews conducted with participants in a novel study about environmental chemicals in body fluids and household air and dust. Interviews reveal how personal and collective environmental history influence the interpretation of exposure data, and how participants fashion an emergent understanding of environmental health problems from the articulation of science and experience. To the illness experience literature, we contribute a framework for analyzing a new category of embodied narratives—“exposure experience”—that examines the mediating role of science. We update social scientific knowledge about social responses to toxic chemicals during a period in which science alters public understanding of chemical pollution. This article is among the first published accounts of participants' responses to learning personal exposure data, research identified as critical to environmental science and public health. Our findings raise the importance of reporting even uncertain science and underscore the value of a community-based reporting strategy.
venue: Journal of Health and Social Behavior

title: A review of imaging techniques for systems biology
abstract: This review examines the diverse imaging techniques that have become integral to systems biology, a field focused on modeling the dynamics and structure of complete biological systems through interdisciplinary approaches. The paper discusses the roles, principles, and applications of microscopy, ultrasound, computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), positron emission tomography (PET), and molecular probes such as quantum dots and nanoshells. Emphasis is placed on how these modalities enable visualization and quantification of biological processes across multiple spatial and temporal scales, facilitating both experimental investigation and mathematical modeling. The review highlights the iterative interplay between imaging data and computational models, which is central to systems biology’s methodology, and underscores the importance of digital image processing techniques like segmentation and registration for model creation and validation. Cancer research is presented as a key application area, where advances in molecular imaging are accelerating understanding of complex signaling pathways and informing targeted therapeutic strategies. The paper concludes that ongoing improvements in imaging resolution, acquisition speed, and molecular specificity will further enhance the predictive power of systems biology models and drive progress in biomedical research.

title: Advances in the biology and chemistry of sialic acids.
abstract: Sialic acids are a subset of nonulosonic acids, which are nine-carbon alpha-keto aldonic acids. Natural existing sialic acid-containing structures are presented in different sialic acid forms, various sialyl linkages, and on diverse underlying glycans. They play important roles in biological, pathological, and immunological processes. Sialobiology has been a challenging and yet attractive research area. Recent advances in chemical and chemoenzymatic synthesis, as well as large-scale E. coli cell-based production, have provided a large library of sialoside standards and derivatives in amounts sufficient for structure-activity relationship studies. Sialoglycan microarrays provide an efficient platform for quick identification of preferred ligands for sialic acid-binding proteins. Future research on sialic acid will continue to be at the interface of chemistry and biology. Research efforts not only will lead to a better understanding of the biological and pathological importance of sialic acids and their diversity but also could lead to the development of therapeutics.

title: Defect Engineering: Tuning the Porosity and Composition of the Metal–Organic Framework UiO-66 via Modulated Synthesis
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive investigation into the defect chemistry of the metal–organic framework UiO-66 synthesized using various monocarboxylic acid modulators under standard conditions. By systematically varying the concentration and acidity of the modulators across 15 syntheses, we demonstrate that missing cluster defects are predominant and that their concentration—and thus the porosity and composition of UiO-66—can be precisely tuned. Characterization by PXRD, nitrogen sorption, dissolution/NMR, and TGA reveals clear trends: increasing modulator concentration or acidity leads to higher defect concentrations and enhanced porosity, with BET surface areas ranging from 1175 to 1777 m2g-1. Comparison of experimental nitrogen adsorption isotherms with simulated models further validates these findings. The results highlight the critical role of modulator properties in defect engineering, offering a rational approach to tailor UiO-66’s structure and properties for targeted applications.

title: Chemical markers for the quality control of herbal medicines: an overview
abstract: Selection of chemical markers is crucial for the quality control of herbal medicines, including authentication of genuine species, harvesting the best quality raw materials, evaluation of post-harvesting handling, assessment of intermediates and finished products, and detection of harmful or toxic ingredients. Ideal chemical markers should be the therapeutic components of herbal medicines. However, for most herbal medicines, the therapeutic components have not been fully elucidated or easily monitored. Bioactive, characteristic, main, synergistic, correlative, toxic and general components may be selected. This article reviews the effective use of chemical markers in the quality control of herbal medicines including the selection criteria considering the roles and physicochemical factors which may affect the effective use of chemical markers.

title: Expander Graphs and their Applications
abstract: A major consideration we had in writing this survey was to make it accessible to mathematicians as well as to computer scientists, since expander graphs, the protagonists of our story, come up in numerous and often surprising contexts in both fields. But, perhaps, we should start with a few words about graphs in general. They are, of course, one of the prime objects of study in Discrete Mathematics. However, graphs are among the most ubiquitous models of both natural and human-made structures. In the natural and social sciences they model relations among species, societies, companies, etc. In computer science, they represent networks of communication, data organization, computational devices as well as the flow of computation, and more. In mathematics, Cayley graphs are useful in Group Theory. Graphs carry a natural metric and are therefore useful in Geometry, and though they are “just” one-dimensional complexes, they are useful in certain parts of Topology, e.g. Knot Theory. In statistical physics, graphs can represent local connections between interacting parts of a system, as well as the dynamics of a physical process on such systems. The study of these models calls, then, for the comprehension of the significant structural properties of the relevant graphs. But are there nontrivial structural properties which are universally important? Expansion of a graph requires that it is simultaneously sparse and highly connected. Expander graphs were first defined by Bassalygo and Pinsker, and their existence first proved by Pinsker in the early ’70s. The property of being an expander seems significant in many of these mathematical, computational and physical contexts. It is not surprising that expanders are useful in the design and analysis of communication networks. What is less obvious is that expanders have surprising utility in other computational settings such as in the theory of error correcting codes and the theory of pseudorandomness. In mathematics, we will encounter e.g. their role in the study of metric embeddings, and in particular in work around the Baum-Connes Conjecture. Expansion is closely related to the convergence rates of Markov Chains, and so they play a key role in the study of Monte-Carlo algorithms in statistical mechanics and in a host of practical computational applications. The list of such interesting and fruitful connections goes on and on with so many applications we will not even

title: Atmospheric chemistry and global change
abstract: Atmospheric chemistry plays a central role in driving global environmental change by influencing climate, air quality, and the composition of the atmosphere. This paper reviews the complex interactions among chemical species in the atmosphere, examines the impact of human activities on atmospheric composition, and explores the consequences for climate change and ecosystem health. Key processes such as ozone depletion, greenhouse gas accumulation, and the formation of secondary pollutants are discussed in the context of both natural variability and anthropogenic forcing. The paper highlights advances in observational techniques and modeling that have improved our understanding of atmospheric processes, while emphasizing the need for continued research to predict future changes and inform policy decisions aimed at mitigating adverse impacts on the environment and society.

title: Science friction: Data, metadata, and collaboration
abstract: As scientific research becomes increasingly data-driven and interdisciplinary, collaboration across fields often encounters “science friction”—the challenges arising from the movement of data and metadata between diverse domains. This paper examines how metadata, typically conceived as stable descriptors facilitating data interoperability, can instead become sources of friction that impede data sharing and collaborative work. Drawing on ethnographic studies of large environmental science projects, the authors argue that metadata should be understood not only as products but also as dynamic processes embedded in scientific communication. The findings reveal that ad hoc, incomplete, and mutable metadata practices are integral to everyday scientific work, highlighting the limitations of standardized metadata frameworks. The paper advocates for a process-oriented approach to metadata that acknowledges the essential role of informal and evolving practices in enabling effective interdisciplinary collaboration and data exchange.

title: Herbal medicine use in pregnancy: results of a multinational study
abstract: The use of complementary and alternative medicines (CAM) is growing in the general population. Herbal medicines are used in all countries of the world and are included in the top CAM therapies used.MethodsA multinational study on how women treat disease and pregnancy-related health ailments was conducted between October 2011 and February 2012 in Europe, North and South America and Australia. In this study, the primary aim was to determine the prevalence of herbal medicine use in pregnancy and factors related to such use across participating countries and regions. The secondary aim was to investigate who recommended the use of herbal medication in pregnancy.ResultsThere were 9,459 women from 23 countries participating in the study. Of these, 28.9% reported the use of herbal medicines in pregnancy. Most herbal medicines were used for pregnancy-related health ailments such as cold and nausea. Ginger, cranberry, valerian and raspberry were the most commonly used herbs in pregnancy. The highest reported rate of herbal use medicines was in Russia (69%). Women from Eastern Europe (51.8%) and Australia (43.8%) were twice as likely to use an herbal medicine versus other regions. Women using herbal medicines were characteristically having their first child, non-smokers, using folic acid and consuming some alcohol in pregnancy. Also, women who were currently students and women with an education other than a high school degree were more likely to use herbal medicines than other women. Although 1 out of 5 women stated that a physician had recommended the herbal use, most women used herbal medicine in pregnancy on their own initiative.ConclusionsIn this multinational study herbal medicine use in pregnancy was high although there were distinct differences in the herbs and users of herbal medicines across regions. Most commonly the women self-medicated with herbal medicine to treat pregnancy-related health ailments. More knowledge regarding the efficacy and safety of herbal medicines in pregnancy is warranted.

title: Interacting topological insulators: a review
abstract: This review provides a comprehensive overview of interacting topological insulators, focusing on the interplay between topological band structures and electron-electron interactions in condensed matter systems. While non-interacting topological insulators such as quantum spin Hall and Chern insulators are well described by band theory, the inclusion of interactions leads to a rich variety of novel phases and phenomena. The article discusses the stability of topological phases against correlations, the emergence of correlated topological insulators in various lattice models, and interaction-induced phases such as topological Kondo insulators. It further explores exotic states like topological Mott insulators and fractional Chern insulators, which arise solely due to strong correlations and have no non-interacting analogs. The review also addresses the impact of interactions on surface states and highlights connections between topological band structures and frustrated magnetism in transition metal oxides. By surveying theoretical models, experimental realizations, and recent advances in quantum simulation platforms, this work elucidates the manifold directions and open questions at the intersection of topology and strong correlations in quantum materials.
venue: Reports on progress in physics. Physical Society

title: Frameworks for ICT Integration in Mathematics Education - A Teacher’s Perspective
abstract: Technology holds pedagogical affordances that can help address low performance in mathematics education. This research study investigated which factors significantly contributed to technology usage by Mathematics teachers. The 155 teachers surveyed were found to be regular users of computers, demonstrating a high opinion of the pedagogical worth of technology and perceiving the tool as being useful for enhancing Mathematic education. However, only a minority was really using technology in their teaching practices. Teachers reiterated the need to be adequately trained in the pedagogical integration of Information and Communication Technology (ICT), insisted on the provision of better computer services in schools, including access to the Internet and solicited the support of parents to accompany their children in their studies. A revised theoretical model was drawn based on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and unified theory of acceptance and use of technology (UTAUT) models, and the two ICT related variables that caused significant variances in technology usage were perceived ease of use and facilitating conditions.
venue: Eurasia Journal of Mathematics, Science and Technology Education

title: Regression Discontinuity Designs in Economics
abstract: This paper provides an introduction and “user guide” to Regression Discontinuity (RD) designs for empirical researchers. It presents the basic theory behind the research design, details when RD is likely to be valid or invalid given economic incentives, explains why it is considered a “quasi-experimental” design, and summarizes different ways (with their advantages and disadvantages) of estimating RD designs and the limitations of interpreting these estimates. Concepts are discussed using examples drawn from the growing body of empirical research using RD. ( JEL C21, C31)

title: The promise of andragogy, heutagogy and academagogy to enterprise and entrepreneurship education pedagogy
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to address the recent development of heutagogy in the domain of enterprise and entrepreneurship education (EE). Responding to recent thinking within our domain of education, this paper discusses the origins of heutagogy, its adoption within enterprise and EE and offers suggestions as to the further development of such thinking in this domain. Design/methodology/approach This conceptual paper revisits the original thinking that developed the process of heutagogy, or self-determined learning. Revisiting the conceptual foundations of heutagogy, comparing it to andragogy and to the idea of academagogy enables the process of academagogical process knowledge (APK) to be outlined. Through this process, the authors argue it is possible to envisage the real potential value of heutagogy to enterprise and EE. Findings In advocating for the development of APK, the authors highlight the importance of six specific knowledge bases; knowledge of self, knowledge of entrepreneurship theories, knowledge of transformational learning approaches, knowledge of authentic assessment processes, knowledge of student engagement and knowledge of how to scholarly lead. The authors argue that the development of scholarship of teaching and learning for enterprise and EE can be advanced through these six knowledge bases. Practical implications There are important implications that arise for all enterprise and entrepreneurship educators in the discussions presented here, especially if we consider entrepreneurial approaches within disciplines and interests that anchor the studies, as opposed to more generic approaches found in entrepreneurship courses. Most importantly, that heutagogy must be evaluated alongside the blended contributions of pedagogy, andragogy and academagogy. Originality/value This paper advances the readers’ understanding of the potential role of heutagogy in enterprise and EE. In doing so, differing opinions related to the use of heutagogy in the domain have been addressed, and a developmental pathway outlined.
