abstract: Prediction models are developed to aid health care providers in estimating the probability or risk that a specific disease or condition is present (diagnostic models) or that a specific event will occur in the future (prognostic models), to inform their decision making. However, the overwhelming evidence shows that the quality of reporting of prediction model studies is poor. Only with full and clear reporting of information on all aspects of a prediction model can risk of bias and potential usefulness of prediction models be adequately assessed. The Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis Or Diagnosis (TRIPOD) Initiative developed a set of recommendations for the reporting of studies developing, validating, or updating a prediction model, whether for diagnostic or prognostic purposes. This article describes how the TRIPOD Statement was developed. An extensive list of items based on a review of the literature was created, which was reduced after a Web-based survey and revised during a 3-day meeting in June 2011 with methodologists, health care professionals, and journal editors. The list was refined during several meetings of the steering group and in e-mail discussions with the wider group of TRIPOD contributors. The resulting TRIPOD Statement is a checklist of 22 items, deemed essential for transparent reporting of a prediction model study. The TRIPOD Statement aims to improve the transparency of the reporting of a prediction model study regardless of the study methods used. The TRIPOD Statement is best used in conjunction with the TRIPOD explanation and elaboration document. To aid the editorial process and readers of prediction model studies, it is recommended that authors include a completed checklist in their submission (also available at www.tripod-statement.org). Editors’ note: In order to encourage dissemination of the TRIPOD Statement, this article is freely accessible on the Annals of Internal Medicine Web site (www.annals.org) and will be also published in BJOG, British Journal of Cancer, British Journal of Surgery, BMC Medicine, British Medical Journal, Circulation, Diabetic Medicine, European Journal of Clinical Investigation, European Urology, and Journal of Clinical Epidemiology. The authors jointly hold the copyright of this article. An accompanying Explanation and Elaboration article is freely available only on www.annals.org; Annals of Internal Medicine holds copyright for that article.

title: The Physics of Neutron Stars
abstract: Neutron stars are some of the densest manifestations of massive objects in the universe. They are ideal astrophysical laboratories for testing theories of dense matter physics and provide connections among nuclear physics, particle physics, and astrophysics. Neutron stars may exhibit conditions and phenomena not observed elsewhere, such as hyperon-dominated matter, deconfined quark matter, superfluidity and superconductivity with critical temperatures near 1010 kelvin, opaqueness to neutrinos, and magnetic fields in excess of 1013 Gauss. Here, we describe the formation, structure, internal composition, and evolution of neutron stars. Observations that include studies of pulsars in binary systems, thermal emission from isolated neutron stars, glitches from pulsars, and quasi-periodic oscillations from accreting neutron stars provide information about neutron star masses, radii, temperatures, ages, and internal compositions.

title: WikiPathways: Pathway Editing for the People
abstract: The rapid expansion of biological data presents significant challenges for the curation and integration of pathway information, which is essential for understanding complex biological systems. Traditional pathway databases rely on small, specialized teams and static representations, limiting community participation and the ability to keep pace with new discoveries. WikiPathways addresses these limitations by providing an open, collaborative platform that enables the broader scientific community to contribute, edit, and maintain biological pathways using a user-friendly web interface and an embedded graphical editing tool. By leveraging the familiar wiki model and integrating pathway-specific features such as direct annotation with public databases and literature references, WikiPathways lowers barriers to participation and facilitates continuous updating and peer review. This community-driven approach enhances the accessibility, accuracy, and relevance of pathway information, offering a scalable solution to the challenges posed by the ongoing growth of biological data.

title: The Learning Platform in Distance Higher Education: Student’s Perceptions
abstract: This study investigates the perceptions of students from the School of Education at the Spanish National University of Distance Education (UNED) regarding the use of learning platforms in distance higher education. Employing a mixed-methods descriptive approach, data were collected through a validated semi-structured questionnaire completed by 111 students enrolled in social education, pedagogy, and master's programs. The findings reveal generally positive student evaluations across four key dimensions: the role of the learning platform in distance education, instructional design, didactic interaction, and its impact on professional practice. Qualitative analysis highlights strengths such as enhanced peer exchange and support for independent learning, while identifying weaknesses including delayed feedback and limitations as a content repository. The results provide actionable insights for improving the integration and effectiveness of learning platforms in distance education, emphasizing the need for timely feedback mechanisms and enriched interactive features to better support student learning and engagement.
venue: The Turkish Online Journal of Distance Education

title: Malignant astrocytic glioma: genetics, biology, and paths to treatment.
abstract: Malignant astrocytic gliomas such as glioblastoma are the most common and lethal intracranial tumors. These cancers exhibit a relentless malignant progression characterized by widespread invasion throughout the brain, resistance to traditional and newer targeted therapeutic approaches, destruction of normal brain tissue, and certain death. The recent confluence of advances in stem cell biology, cell signaling, genome and computational science and genetic model systems have revolutionized our understanding of the mechanisms underlying the genetics, biology and clinical behavior of glioblastoma. This progress is fueling new opportunities for understanding the fundamental basis for development of this devastating disease and also novel therapies that, for the first time, portend meaningful clinical responses.

title: Soft Computing
abstract: Soft computing is a computational paradigm inspired by the human ability to make approximate decisions and solve problems under imprecise or uncertain conditions, without requiring high precision or accuracy. Unlike traditional AI approaches that rely on symbolic processing and precise reasoning, soft computing aims to develop methodologies that tolerate imprecision and uncertainty, enabling simpler and more effective inference and problem-solving in real-world scenarios. Key technologies supporting soft computing include fuzzy theory, neural networks, probabilistic reasoning, genetic algorithms, chaos theory, and knowledge engineering. The concept of toll sets, introduced by Dubois and Prade, extends fuzzy set theory by associating a cost or penalty with membership, providing a new perspective for modeling uncertainty. Ongoing research, such as the Berkeley Initiative for Soft Computing (BISC), continues to advance the field by fostering collaboration and innovation in these methodologies.

title: Human Brain Organoids on a Chip Reveal the Physics of Folding
abstract: Human brain wrinkling has been implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders and yet its origins remain unknown. Polymer gel models suggest that wrinkling emerges spontaneously due to compression forces arising during differential swelling, but these ideas have not been tested in a living system. Here, we report the appearance of surface wrinkles during the in vitro development and self-organization of human brain organoids in a microfabricated compartment that supports in situ imaging over a timescale of weeks. We observe the emergence of convolutions at a critical cell density and maximal nuclear strain, which are indicative of a mechanical instability. We identify two opposing forces contributing to differential growth: cytoskeletal contraction at the organoid core and cell-cycle-dependent nuclear expansion at the organoid perimeter. The wrinkling wavelength exhibits linear scaling with tissue thickness, consistent with balanced bending and stretching energies. Lissencephalic (smooth brain) organoids display reduced convolutions, modified scaling and a reduced elastic modulus. Although the mechanism here does not include the neuronal migration seen in vivo, it models the physics of the folding brain remarkably well. Our on-chip approach offers a means for studying the emergent properties of organoid development, with implications for the embryonic human brain. Wrinkling in human brain organoids suggests that brain development may be mechanically driven, a notion supported only by model gels so far. Evidence in this simple living system highlights roles for cytoskeletal contraction and nuclear expansion.

title: Perspectives on Mechanism Design in Economic Theory
abstract: Roger B. Myerson delivered his Prize Lecture on 8 December 2007 at Aula Magna, Stockholm University. He was introduced by Professor Jorgen Weibull, Chairman of the Economics Prize Committee.

title: A decade of systems biology.
abstract: Over the past decade, systems biology has emerged as a transformative approach for modeling and understanding complex biological systems through the integration of systematic, genome-scale measurements and computational analyses. This review traces the evolution of the field, highlighting technological advances in high-throughput data generation and the development of analytical frameworks that enable predictive, hypothesis-driven research. Systems biology has expanded from its origins in model organisms to address fundamental questions in human development and disease, influencing areas such as molecular diagnostics, genetic interaction mapping, disease gene identification, and stem cell biology. We discuss the challenges posed by exponential data growth, cellular and genetic heterogeneity, and the need for integrative models that encompass both physical and functional system properties. The review also examines emerging applications—such as pathway-based biomarkers and global genetic interaction maps—and recent progress in software tools that facilitate interactive exploration of system-wide models. Collectively, these advances underscore the increasing relevance of systems approaches for cell and developmental biologists seeking to apply network-based methods to diverse biomedical problems.
venue: Annual Review of Cell and Developmental Biology

title: The synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) using continuous flow chemistry
abstract: Continuous flow chemistry has emerged as a transformative technology in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), offering enhanced control, safety, and scalability compared to traditional batch processes. This review highlights the evolution and current state of continuous flow methodologies for API production, emphasizing their holistic integration from synthesis through in-line analysis and purification to final formulation. Key examples from both academia and industry demonstrate how flow chemistry enables efficient, reproducible, and safer multi-step syntheses, including challenging or hazardous transformations. The modularity and automation potential of flow systems facilitate rapid process optimization and real-time monitoring, while also addressing issues of heat and mass transfer. Despite notable successes in scaling up API manufacture using flow reactors, challenges such as reactor fouling, high initial investment, and the need for specialized training persist. By critically examining both the achievements and limitations of continuous flow approaches, this review underscores their growing impact on pharmaceutical manufacturing and the collaborative efforts required to realize fully continuous drug production.

title: Improving Health Care Globally: A Critical Review of the Necessity of Family Medicine Research and Recommendations to Build Research Capacity
abstract: An invitational conference led by the World Organization of Family Doctors (Wonca) involving selected delegates from 34 countries was held in Kingston, Ontario, Canada, March 8 to12, 2003. The conference theme was “Improving Health Globally: The Necessity of Family Medicine Research.” Guiding conference discussions was the value that to improve health care worldwide, strong, evidence-based primary care is indispensable. Eight papers reviewed before the meeting formed the basic material from which the conference developed 9 recommendations. Wonca, as an international body of family medicine, was regarded as particularly suited to pursue these conference recommendations: Research achievements in family medicine should be displayed to policy makers, health (insurance) authorities, and academic leaders in a systematic way. In all countries, sentinel practice systems should be developed to provide surveillance reports on illness and diseases that have the greatest impact on the population’s health and wellness in the community. A clearinghouse should be organized to provide a central repository of knowledge about family medicine research expertise, training, and mentoring. National research institutes and university departments of family medicine with a research mission should be developed. Practice-based research networks should be developed around the world. Family medicine research journals, conferences, and Web sites should be strengthened to disseminate research findings internationally, and their use coordinated. Improved representation of family medicine research journals in databases, such as Index Medicus, should be pursued. Funding of international collaborative research in family medicine should be facilitated. International ethical guidelines, with an international ethical review process, should be developed in particular for participatory (action) research, where researchers work in partnership with communities. When implementing these recommendations, the specific needs and implications for developing countries should be addressed. The Wonca executive committee has reviewed these recommendations and the supporting rationale for each. They plan to follow the recommendations, but to do so will require the support and cooperation of many individuals, organizations, and national governments around the world.

title: Genome Sequence of the Pea Aphid Acyrthosiphon pisum
abstract: The genome of the pea aphid shows remarkable levels of gene duplication and equally remarkable gene absences that shed light on aspects of aphid biology, most especially its symbiosis with Buchnera.

title: Role of AI chatbots in education: systematic literature review
abstract: AI chatbots shook the world not long ago with their potential to revolutionize education systems in a myriad of ways. AI chatbots can provide immediate support by answering questions, offering explanations, and providing additional resources. Chatbots can also act as virtual teaching assistants, supporting educators through various means. In this paper, we try to understand the full benefits of AI chatbots in education, their opportunities, challenges, potential limitations, concerns, and prospects of using AI chatbots in educational settings. We conducted an extensive search across various academic databases, and after applying specific predefined criteria, we selected a final set of 67 relevant studies for review. The research findings emphasize the numerous benefits of integrating AI chatbots in education, as seen from both students' and educators' perspectives. We found that students primarily gain from AI-powered chatbots in three key areas: homework and study assistance, a personalized learning experience, and the development of various skills. For educators, the main advantages are the time-saving assistance and improved pedagogy. However, our research also emphasizes significant challenges and critical factors that educators need to handle diligently. These include concerns related to AI applications such as reliability, accuracy, and ethical considerations.
venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education

title: Recent advances in 3D printing of biomaterials
abstract: 3D Printing promises to produce complex biomedical devices according to computer design using patient-specific anatomical data. Since its initial use as pre-surgical visualization models and tooling molds, 3D Printing has slowly evolved to create one-of-a-kind devices, implants, scaffolds for tissue engineering, diagnostic platforms, and drug delivery systems. Fueled by the recent explosion in public interest and access to affordable printers, there is renewed interest to combine stem cells with custom 3D scaffolds for personalized regenerative medicine. Before 3D Printing can be used routinely for the regeneration of complex tissues (e.g. bone, cartilage, muscles, vessels, nerves in the craniomaxillofacial complex), and complex organs with intricate 3D microarchitecture (e.g. liver, lymphoid organs), several technological limitations must be addressed. In this review, the major materials and technology advances within the last five years for each of the common 3D Printing technologies (Three Dimensional Printing, Fused Deposition Modeling, Selective Laser Sintering, Stereolithography, and 3D Plotting/Direct-Write/Bioprinting) are described. Examples are highlighted to illustrate progress of each technology in tissue engineering, and key limitations are identified to motivate future research and advance this fascinating field of advanced manufacturing.

title: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for fluid mechanics: a review
abstract: Despite the significant progress over the last 50 years in simulating flow problems using numerical discretization of the Navier–Stokes equations (NSE), we still cannot incorporate seamlessly noisy data into existing algorithms, mesh-generation is complex, and we cannot tackle high-dimensional problems governed by parametrized NSE. Moreover, solving inverse flow problems is often prohibitively expensive and requires complex and expensive formulations and new computer codes. Here, we review flow physics-informed learning, integrating seamlessly data and mathematical models, and implement them using physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). We demonstrate the effectiveness of PINNs for inverse problems related to three-dimensional wake flows, supersonic flows, and biomedical flows.

title: A strategy to apply machine learning to small datasets in materials science
abstract: There is growing interest in applying machine learning techniques in the research of materials science. However, although it is recognized that materials datasets are typically smaller and sometimes more diverse compared to other fields, the influence of availability of materials data on training machine learning models has not yet been studied, which prevents the possibility to establish accurate predictive rules using small materials datasets. Here we analyzed the fundamental interplay between the availability of materials data and the predictive capability of machine learning models. Instead of affecting the model precision directly, the effect of data size is mediated by the degree of freedom (DoF) of model, resulting in the phenomenon of association between precision and DoF. The appearance of precision–DoF association signals the issue of underfitting and is characterized by large bias of prediction, which consequently restricts the accurate prediction in unknown domains. We proposed to incorporate the crude estimation of property in the feature space to establish ML models using small sized materials data, which increases the accuracy of prediction without the cost of higher DoF. In three case studies of predicting the band gap of binary semiconductors, lattice thermal conductivity, and elastic properties of zeolites, the integration of crude estimation effectively boosted the predictive capability of machine learning models to state-of-art levels, demonstrating the generality of the proposed strategy to construct accurate machine learning models using small materials dataset.MACHINE LEARNING: Dealing with small datasetsMachine learning can be useful for materials prediction if crude estimations of the outcome are integrated in the code. Machine learning has been attracting tremendous attention lately due to its predictive power; evidence suggests it is directly proportional to the size of the available datasets. Machine learning can be useful in predicting new materials and novel properties, but materials sets tend to be smaller and more diverse than other fields. Ying Zhang and Chen Ling from the Toyota Research Institute of North America report that these small datasets affect the freedom of the algorithms and thus limit their predictive capabilities. In order to counterbalance the effect, they suggest introducing in the code crude estimations of the targeted property, obtained by other means.

title: Julia: A Fresh Approach to Numerical Computing
abstract: Bridging cultures that have often been distant, Julia combines expertise from the diverse fields of computer science and computational science to create a new approach to numerical computing. Julia is designed to be easy and fast and questions notions generally held to be “laws of nature' by practitioners of numerical computing: \beginlist \item High-level dynamic programs have to be slow. \item One must prototype in one language and then rewrite in another language for speed or deployment. \item There are parts of a system appropriate for the programmer, and other parts that are best left untouched as they have been built by the experts. \endlist We introduce the Julia programming language and its design---a dance between specialization and abstraction. Specialization allows for custom treatment. Multiple dispatch, a technique from computer science, picks the right algorithm for the right circumstance. Abstraction, which is what good computation is really about, recognizes what remains the same after dif...

title: The chemistry of isoindole natural products
abstract: This review highlights the chemical and biological aspects of natural products containing an oxidized or reduced isoindole skeleton. This motif is found in its intact or modified form in indolocarbazoles, macrocyclic polyketides (cytochalasan alkaloids), the aporhoeadane alkaloids, meroterpenoids from Stachybotrys species and anthraquinone-type alkaloids. Concerning their biological activity, molecular structure and synthesis, we have limited this review to the most inspiring examples. Within different congeners, we have selected a few members and discussed the synthetic routes in more detail. The putative biosynthetic pathways of the presented isoindole alkaloids are described as well.

title: Towards a general theory of implementation
abstract: Understanding and evaluating the implementation of complex interventions in practice is an important problem for healthcare managers and policy makers, and for patients and others who must operationalize them beyond formal clinical settings. It has been argued that this work should be founded on theory that provides a foundation for understanding, designing, predicting, and evaluating dynamic implementation processes. This paper sets out core constituents of a general theory of implementation, building on Normalization Process Theory and linking it to key constructs from recent work in sociology and psychology. These are informed by ideas about agency and its expression within social systems and fields, social and cognitive mechanisms, and collective action. This approach unites a number of contending perspectives in a way that makes possible a more comprehensive explanation of the implementation and embedding of new ways of thinking, enacting and organizing practice.

title: A Primer on Sediment-Trace Element Chemistry
abstract: This book provides a basic introduction to sediment-heavy metal interactions and how sediment chemical data can be used to address environmental questions and issues. It is designed to promote self-teaching and is written so that students and professionals with a minimum of formal training in the environmental sciences can understand it. The book addresses all of the major physical and chemical factors that control sediment-trace element chemistry, as well as sampling and sampling design, data manipulation, and data interpretation. Following in the steps of the successful first edition, which was used as a text for a three day short course for U.S. Geological Survey professionals interested in sediment trace chemistry and its application to water quality issues, A Primer on Sediment-Trace Element Chemistry, 2nd Edition is ideal for academics, geochemists, chemists, hydrologists, environmental lawyers, and water quality professionals needing a comprehensive introduction to this field.

title: Biostimulants in Plant Science: A Global Perspective
abstract: This review presents a comprehensive and systematic study of the field of plant biostimulants and considers the fundamental and innovative principles underlying this technology. The elucidation of the biological basis of biostimulant function is a prerequisite for the development of science-based biostimulant industry and sound regulations governing these compounds. The task of defining the biological basis of biostimulants as a class of compounds, however, is made more complex by the diverse sources of biostimulants present in the market, which include bacteria, fungi, seaweeds, higher plants, animals and humate-containing raw materials, and the wide diversity of industrial processes utilized in their preparation. To distinguish biostimulants from the existing legislative product categories we propose the following definition of a biostimulant as “a formulated product of biological origin that improves plant productivity as a consequence of the novel or emergent properties of the complex of constituents, and not as a sole consequence of the presence of known essential plant nutrients, plant growth regulators, or plant protective compounds.” The definition provided here is important as it emphasizes the principle that biological function can be positively modulated through application of molecules, or mixtures of molecules, for which an explicit mode of action has not been defined. Given the difficulty in determining a “mode of action” for a biostimulant, and recognizing the need for the market in biostimulants to attain legitimacy, we suggest that the focus of biostimulant research and validation should be upon proof of efficacy and safety and the determination of a broad mechanism of action, without a requirement for the determination of a specific mode of action. While there is a clear commercial imperative to rationalize biostimulants as a discrete class of products, there is also a compelling biological case for the science-based development of, and experimentation with biostimulants in the expectation that this may lead to the identification of novel biological molecules and phenomenon, pathways and processes, that would not have been discovered if the category of biostimulants did not exist, or was not considered legitimate.

title: Clinical Medicine
abstract: Integrated care systems join up health and care services, so that people have the support they need, in the right place, at the right time. The aims include improving outcomes in healthcare, tackling inequalities in access and enhancing productivity and value for money. This is needed for neuroscience care as the traditional delivery of neuroscience care is inefficient, outdated and expensive, and can involve complex referral pathways and long waiting times. In preparation for the formation of the integrated care system (ICS), a novel innovative collaboration across multiple NHS trusts developed across North Central London in 2021. We developed a model where neuroscience specialists engage in collaborative care with clinicians outside the specialist hospital setting. Pivotal to the pathway is a multidisciplinary meeting, and collaborative working enables joint clinical reviews, diagnostics and medication initiation. This innovative collaboration has already significantly improved access, addressed inequalities due to borough variation and enhanced the delivery and quality of neuroscience care in our ICS. It is a translatable model that can be adapted to suit other regions in the UK. It fulfils many of the objectives of the integrated care system and these benefits are seen without the need for significantly more resource.

title: Biology in bloom: implementing Bloom's Taxonomy to enhance student learning in biology.
abstract: This study presents the development and implementation of the Blooming Biology Tool (BBT), an assessment instrument grounded in Bloom’s Taxonomy, designed to enhance alignment between biology instruction and assessment in postsecondary education. By categorizing and analyzing nearly 600 biology exam questions from diverse sources, the BBT enables faculty to evaluate the cognitive demands of their assessments and adjust teaching strategies accordingly. The tool was implemented across multiple collegiate settings, facilitating the creation of exam questions and learning activities that target higher-order cognitive skills. Results indicate that the BBT supports both instructors in diagnosing student learning and designing more effective assessments, and students in developing metacognitive awareness and advanced study strategies. The paper also introduces complementary resources to further assist biology educators in fostering critical thinking and deeper conceptual understanding through discipline-specific application of Bloom’s Taxonomy.

title: Clinical Medicine
abstract: Clinical medicine is defined as the practice of medicine grounded in the direct observation and treatment of patients. This paper explores the foundational principles of clinical medicine, emphasizing its distinction from laboratory-based or theoretical approaches. Drawing on definitions from authoritative sources such as the National Cancer Institute Thesaurus, the discussion highlights the centrality of patient interaction, physical examination, and clinical judgment in diagnosis and management. The paper also considers the evolving landscape of clinical medicine in light of technological advancements and changing healthcare paradigms. Ultimately, it underscores the enduring importance of clinician-patient engagement as a cornerstone of effective medical practice.

title: Introduction to Many-Body Physics
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive introduction to many-body physics, emphasizing the fundamental concepts and methodologies that underpin the field. Beginning with a discussion of scales and complexity in many-body systems, it explores the role of quantum fields and collective excitations, as well as the significance of conserved particles. The text introduces second quantization through simple examples and develops the formalism of Green's functions. Key theoretical frameworks such as Landau Fermi liquid theory and Feynman diagrams at zero temperature are presented, followed by an examination of finite temperature effects in many-body systems. The paper further addresses fluctuation dissipation relations, linear response theory, and electron transport phenomena. It discusses the physics of phase transitions, broken symmetry, and utilizes path integral methods to analyze critical phenomena. Advanced topics include superconductivity within the BCS framework and the behavior of heavy electrons and local moments. This work serves as a foundational resource for understanding both the basic principles and advanced topics in many-body physics.

title: Doping a Mott insulator: Physics of high-temperature superconductivity
abstract: This paper reviews the physics of high-temperature superconductivity in cuprate materials from the perspective of doping a Mott insulator, emphasizing the role of strong electron correlations. The authors discuss the basic electronic structure of cuprates and analyze experimental observations, particularly in the underdoped regime where anomalous phenomena such as the pseudogap emerge. The resonating valence bond (RVB) theory is introduced as a qualitative framework for understanding these features, with attention given to phase fluctuations and their limitations in explaining the full pseudogap phenomenology. Numerical approaches using projected wavefunctions are presented, yielding results consistent with experiments. Theoretical developments are explored through analytic treatments of the t-J model using slave-boson methods, leading to gauge theory descriptions that capture spin-charge separation and fractionalization. Both U(1) and SU(2) gauge formulations are examined, with the latter providing a more complete account of the spin liquid phase and its evolution upon doping. The implications of these theories for the phase diagram, vortex structure, and topological aspects of the pseudogap phase are discussed, offering insights into the mechanisms underlying high-Tc superconductivity and highlighting directions for future research.

title: Physics of thin films
abstract: This comprehensive work provides an in-depth exploration of the physics of thin films, encompassing their preparation methods, measurement techniques, formation mechanisms, and structural characterization. It systematically reviews chemical, electrochemical, sputtering, and vacuum evaporation techniques for thin film deposition, followed by detailed discussions on methods for measuring film thickness and deposition rates. The book examines the stages of film formation, nucleation theories, growth processes, and the influence of various factors on film structure and crystallography, including epitaxial growth. Advanced analytical techniques such as electron microscopy, electron diffraction, X-ray methods, and Auger spectroscopy are presented for the assessment of composition, morphology, and structure. The physical properties of thin films—including mechanical, electrical, magnetic, and optical characteristics—are analyzed with attention to experimental methods and underlying mechanisms. Finally, the applications of thin films in optics and electronics are surveyed, highlighting their roles in contacts, resistors, capacitors, inductors, ferromagnetic and superconducting devices, microacoustic elements, integrated circuits, optoelectronics, and integrated optics. This text serves as a foundational reference for researchers and practitioners engaged in thin film science and technology.

title: Ten quick tips for machine learning in computational biology
abstract: Machine learning has become a pivotal tool for many projects in computational biology, bioinformatics, and health informatics. Nevertheless, beginners and biomedical researchers often do not have enough experience to run a data mining project effectively, and therefore can follow incorrect practices, that may lead to common mistakes or over-optimistic results. With this review, we present ten quick tips to take advantage of machine learning in any computational biology context, by avoiding some common errors that we observed hundreds of times in multiple bioinformatics projects. We believe our ten suggestions can strongly help any machine learning practitioner to carry on a successful project in computational biology and related sciences.

title: Conductivity engineering of graphene by defect formation
abstract: This study demonstrates that the electrical conductivity of graphene can be significantly enhanced through the controlled introduction of vacancy defects. Contrary to conventional expectations that defects reduce conductivity, both quantum mechanical transport calculations and experimental measurements on carbon nanosheets reveal an increase in conductivity by more than an order of magnitude with rising defect concentration. Theoretical modeling shows that vacancy defects induce mid-gap states, resulting in localized regions of metallic behavior around the vacancies. Ab-initio density functional theory and tight-binding calculations, supported by coherent potential approximation, confirm that these mid-gap states increase carrier density and shift the Fermi level away from the Dirac point, thereby enhancing conductivity. Experimental verification using chemically treated carbon nanosheets corroborates the theoretical predictions. These findings highlight defect engineering as a viable strategy for tailoring graphene’s electronic properties and enabling the fabrication of electronic junctions in graphene-based devices.

title: Engineering organoids
abstract: Organoids are in vitro miniaturized and simplified model systems of organs that have gained enormous interest for modelling tissue development and disease, and for personalized medicine, drug screening and cell therapy. Despite considerable success in culturing physiologically relevant organoids, challenges remain to achieve real-life applications. In particular, the high variability of self-organizing growth and restricted experimental and analytical access hamper the translatability of organoid systems. In this Review, we argue that many limitations of traditional organoid culture can be addressed by engineering approaches at all levels of organoid systems. We investigate cell surface and genetic engineering approaches, and discuss stem cell niche engineering based on the design of matrices that allow spatiotemporal control of organoid growth and shape-guided morphogenesis. We examine how microfluidic approaches and lessons learnt from organs-on-a-chip enable the integration of mechano-physiological parameters and increase accessibility of organoids to improve functional readouts. Applying engineering principles to organoids increases reproducibility and provides experimental control, which will, ultimately, be required to enable clinical translation. Organoids are cellular 3D models of organs, which provide powerful in vitro platforms for the investigation of tissue and disease biology. In this Review, the authors investigate engineering approaches, including cellular engineering, designer matrices and microfluidics, to improve the reproducibility and physiological relevance of organoids.

title: Strategic issues in customer relationship management (CRM) implementation
abstract: This paper examines the strategic issues involved in implementing customer relationship management (CRM) systems, drawing on a case study of a UK-based manufacturing company. The study highlights the complexity and holistic nature of CRM, emphasizing its integration with business processes and information technologies. Key findings indicate that successful CRM implementation requires strong leadership, clear sourcing strategies, effective customer targeting, and robust evaluation mechanisms. The research underscores the importance of aligning technological and business objectives, managing organizational change, and adopting a customer-centric approach. The paper concludes by identifying gaps in existing literature and recommending further empirical research to better understand the critical factors influencing CRM success.

title: Exit, Voice, and Loyalty
abstract: This paper explores the interplay between exit, voice, and loyalty as mechanisms through which individuals and groups respond to decline in firms, organizations, and states. By introducing the concepts of exit (the act of leaving or withdrawing) and voice (the act of expressing dissatisfaction), the study examines how these responses reflect economic and political dynamics. The analysis considers the latitude for deterioration within organizations, highlighting how slack can persist due to insufficient feedback mechanisms. The paper investigates the limitations of exit as a corrective tool, especially in contexts where competition is imperfect or collusive, and discusses how voice emerges as a crucial alternative or complement to exit. Special attention is given to the challenges of combining exit and voice, particularly under monopoly conditions or in spatial duopolies such as two-party political systems. The role of loyalty is theorized as a moderating factor that influences the choice between exit and voice, shaping organizational resilience and adaptability. Overall, the study provides a framework for understanding how economic and political actors navigate decline and change through their available options.

title: Machine learning and the physical sciences
abstract: Machine learning (ML) has rapidly emerged as a transformative tool across the physical sciences, offering new approaches for data analysis, model development, and simulation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the interplay between ML and physics, highlighting both conceptual advances and practical applications. We discuss how insights from statistical physics have deepened understanding of machine learning algorithms, including neural networks and generative models, and how ML techniques are being leveraged to address complex problems in particle physics, cosmology, quantum many-body systems, quantum computing, chemistry, and materials science. The review also examines the development of specialized hardware architectures designed to accelerate ML computations. Throughout, we emphasize recent successes, domain-specific methodologies, and the unique challenges encountered at the intersection of ML and physical sciences. The paper concludes with an outlook on future research directions and the potential for continued cross-fertilization between these fields.

title: The Effectiveness of Business Codes: A Critical Examination of Existing Studies and the Development of an Integrated Research Model
abstract: Business codes are a widely used management instrument. Research into the effectiveness of business codes has, however, produced conflicting results. The main reasons for the divergent findings are: varying definitions of key terms; deficiencies in the empirical data and methodologies used; and a lack of theory. In this paper, we propose an integrated research model and suggest directions for future research.

title: Molecular biology of microbial hydrogenases.
abstract: Microbial hydrogenases are diverse metalloproteins that catalyze the reversible oxidation of molecular hydrogen, playing essential roles in microbial energy metabolism, including fermentation, respiration, and redox balancing. The major classes—[NiFe]-hydrogenases, [FeFe]-hydrogenases, and iron-sulfur cluster-free Hmd hydrogenases—differ in active site composition, structure, and phylogeny. Advances in molecular biology, X-ray crystallography, and spectroscopy have elucidated the structure and function of these enzymes, revealing mechanisms of metallocenter assembly and regulation by environmental signals. Some hydrogenases also function as H2 sensors, influencing gene expression and energy conservation via protonmotive force generation. Understanding the molecular biology and diversity of microbial hydrogenases not only provides insights into microbial physiology but also underpins efforts to harness these enzymes for sustainable biological hydrogen production.

title: Soft Computing
abstract: Soft Computing is dedicated to system solutions based on soft computing techniques. It provides rapid dissemination of important results in soft computing technologies, a fusion of research in evolutionary algorithms and genetic programming, neural science and neural net systems, fuzzy set theory and fuzzy systems, and chaos theory and chaotic systems. Soft Computing encourages the integration of soft computing techniques and tools into both everyday and advanced applications. By linking the ideas and techniques of soft computing with other disciplines, the journal serves as a unifying platform that fosters comparisons, extensions, and new applications. As a result, the journal is an international forum for all scientists and engineers engaged in research and development in this fast growing field. Indexed by Science Citation Index, Inspec, Compendex, DBLP, Computer Science Index, Current Abstracts, Current

title: Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials as Emerging Tools for Materials Science
abstract: Atomic‐scale modeling and understanding of materials have made remarkable progress, but they are still fundamentally limited by the large computational cost of explicit electronic‐structure methods such as density‐functional theory. This Progress Report shows how machine learning (ML) is currently enabling a new degree of realism in materials modeling: by “learning” electronic‐structure data, ML‐based interatomic potentials give access to atomistic simulations that reach similar accuracy levels but are orders of magnitude faster. A brief introduction to the new tools is given, and then, applications to some select problems in materials science are highlighted: phase‐change materials for memory devices; nanoparticle catalysts; and carbon‐based electrodes for chemical sensing, supercapacitors, and batteries. It is hoped that the present work will inspire the development and wider use of ML‐based interatomic potentials in diverse areas of materials research.

title: Student Centric Curriculum Design and Implementation – Challenges & Opportunities in Business Management & IT Education
abstract: This paper examines the growing significance of student-centric curriculum design and implementation in higher education, with a focus on business management and information technology disciplines. Rapid changes in these fields, driven by globalization and technological advancement, necessitate curricula that are responsive to industry needs and foster both knowledge acquisition and research skills among students. The study analyzes the challenges faced by autonomous and affiliated institutions in planning, designing, and executing such curricula, including aligning course content with industry requirements, integrating research components, and adopting innovative pedagogical approaches. Opportunities arising from student-centric models are explored, particularly their potential to enhance employability, adaptability, and leadership capabilities among graduates. The paper also presents an ABCD (Advantages, Benefits, Constraints, Disadvantages) analysis of student-centric curriculum models, highlighting that while implementation poses significant challenges—such as resource constraints and resistance to change—the overall benefits outweigh the drawbacks. The findings underscore the importance of continuous curriculum development to keep pace with evolving industry standards and advocate for collaborative efforts between academia and industry to ensure relevance and effectiveness in business management and IT education.

title: Norbert Elias and Modern Sociology: Knowledge, Interdependence, Power, Process
abstract: This book explores the interplay between the making of Elias as a sociologist and the development of his core ideas relating to figurations, interdependence, and civilising processes. Focusing on the relevance of Elias's work for current debates within sociology, the authors centrally consider his contributions to the sociology of knowledge and methodology. Dunning and Hughes locate the work of Elias within a discussion of the crisis of sociology as a subject, and compare his figurational approach with the approaches of three major figures in modern sociology: Anthony Giddens, Michel Foucault and Pierre Bourdieu. This highly readable and engaging book will be essential reading for students and scholars of sociological theory and methods.

title: Nanoparticles and their applications in cell and molecular biology.
abstract: Nanoparticles, with their tunable compositions, sizes, shapes, and surface chemistries, offer unique physical and chemical properties that have revolutionized cell and molecular biology research. This review provides an overview of the major classes of nanoparticles—including liposomes, albumin-bound nanoparticles, polymeric nanoparticles, dendrimers, iron oxide nanoparticles, quantum dots, and gold nanoparticles—highlighting their structural features and functionalities relevant to biological applications. The paper discusses how these platforms enable advancements in drug delivery, imaging, biosensing, and the elucidation of fundamental biological processes. Special emphasis is placed on strategies for nanoparticle targeting, including both passive and active approaches, which enhance specificity and efficacy in biomedical applications. The integration of nanoparticles into cell and molecular biology has not only improved the sensitivity and precision of experimental techniques but has also facilitated the development of novel therapeutics and diagnostics. Collectively, these advances underscore the transformative potential of nanotechnology in addressing complex biological questions and improving human health.

title: Enablers and Inhibitors of Business-IT Alignment
abstract: This study investigates the key enablers and inhibitors of business-IT alignment through a multi-year empirical analysis involving over 1,000 executives from more than 500 firms across 15 industries. Drawing on survey data, interviews, and consulting observations collected between 1992 and 1997 at IBM’s Advanced Business Institute, the research identifies senior executive support, IT involvement in strategy development, mutual understanding between IT and business, strong partnerships, well-prioritized IT projects, and IT leadership as primary enablers of alignment. Conversely, lack of close IT-business relationships, poor prioritization, unmet commitments, insufficient business understanding by IT, lack of executive support for IT, and weak IT leadership are found to be major inhibitors. The findings reveal that these factors are consistent across industries, time periods, and executive roles, underscoring the evolutionary and dynamic nature of alignment. The study validates prior anecdotal evidence and emphasizes that maximizing enablers while minimizing inhibitors is essential for achieving effective business-IT alignment.
venue: Communications of the Association for Information Systems

title: Keldysh field theory for driven open quantum systems
abstract: This review presents a comprehensive account of recent theoretical advances in the study of driven open quantum systems, where coherent and dissipative dynamics interplay to produce genuinely non-equilibrium phenomena with no direct analog in equilibrium condensed matter physics. Motivated by experimental progress in platforms such as cold atomic gases, exciton-polariton condensates, and microcavity arrays, the paper systematically develops the Keldysh functional integral framework as a versatile tool for analyzing both stationary states and dynamical evolution in these systems. Key topics include the emergence of non-thermal stationary states, novel macroscopic many-body phenomena uniquely tied to microscopic drive and dissipation, and the breakdown of conventional equilibrium concepts such as detailed balance. The review details the construction of the Keldysh action from quantum master equations, explores its symmetries and semiclassical limits, and applies functional renormalization group techniques to characterize critical behavior in driven-dissipative spin and bosonic models. Universal features of heating dynamics in one-dimensional systems are also discussed. By bridging concepts from quantum optics, many-body theory, and statistical mechanics, this work highlights the rich landscape of phases and dynamical regimes accessible in driven open quantum systems and underscores the power of field-theoretical methods for their analysis.
venue: Reports on progress in physics. Physical Society

title: Quantum Theory of Angular Momentum: Irreducible Tensors, Spherical Harmonics, Vector Coupling Coefficients, 3nj Symbols
abstract: This monograph presents a comprehensive and systematic treatment of the quantum theory of angular momentum, emphasizing irreducible tensors, spherical harmonics, vector coupling coefficients, and 3nj symbols. Addressing the needs of both specialists and students, it compiles essential formulas, relationships, and theoretical results within a unified framework of phase conventions and definitions. The text covers foundational aspects such as vector and tensor theory, angular momentum operators, Wigner D-functions, spin functions, tensor spherical harmonics, Clebsch-Gordan coefficients, and higher-order coupling symbols. Designed as both a reference and a practical handbook, the material is organized for ease of use in calculations relevant to atomic, molecular, nuclear, and particle physics, as well as applications in quantum chemistry, optics, plasma physics, radiophysics, and astrophysics. By consolidating widely scattered results and providing concise presentations without proofs but with extensive references, this work facilitates the evaluation of structures, transition probabilities, cross sections, and angular distributions in diverse quantum systems.

title: Quantum Hamiltonian Complexity
abstract: Quantum Hamiltonian Complexity (QHC) is an interdisciplinary field at the intersection of quantum physics, computer science, and mathematics, focused on the computational study of quantum constraint satisfaction problems through the lens of local Hamiltonians. This survey provides a comprehensive introduction to QHC, tracing its historical development from both computer science and physics perspectives, and highlighting key breakthroughs such as the quantum analogue of the Cook-Levin Theorem and area laws for one-dimensional quantum systems. It aims to bridge disciplinary gaps by offering accessible explanations of foundational concepts in quantum information, a glossary of condensed matter physics terminology, and overviews of central techniques including mean-field theory, tensor networks, and renormalization methods. The survey also reviews pivotal results in the field, such as the QMA-completeness of k-local Hamiltonian problems and efficient algorithms for special cases like Quantum 2-SAT, presented with novel information-theoretic insights. By synthesizing motivations, methods, and results, this work serves as a foundational resource for researchers seeking to understand the computational complexity inherent in quantum many-body systems.
venue: Foundations and Trends® in Theoretical Computer Science

title: Electrostatic correlations: from plasma to biology
abstract: Electrostatic correlations play an important role in physics, chemistry and biology. In plasmas they result in thermodynamic instability similar to the liquid–gas phase transition of simple molecular fluids. For charged colloidal suspensions the electrostatic correlations are responsible for screening and colloidal charge renormalization. In aqueous solutions containing multivalent counterions they can lead to charge inversion and flocculation. In biological systems the correlations account for the organization of cytoskeleton and the compaction of genetic material. In spite of their ubiquity, the true importance of electrostatic correlations has come to be fully appreciated only quite recently. In this paper, we will review the thermodynamic consequences of electrostatic correlations in a variety of systems ranging from classical plasmas to molecular biology.

title: Sustainable Development (1987-2005) - An Oxymoron Comes of Age
abstract: This paper critically examines the evolution of the concept of sustainable development from its emergence in the Brundtland Commission’s 1987 report to 2005, interrogating its status as an oxymoron and its proliferation across diverse policy, academic, and activist discourses. The analysis highlights the inherent contradictions and ambiguities in defining and operationalizing sustainable development, particularly regarding the shifting and culturally contingent nature of “needs,” the tension between economic growth and environmental sustainability, and the challenges posed by distributive politics and ownership of natural resources. The essay argues that while sustainable development has become a dominant framework in global policy debates, its effectiveness is undermined by unresolved questions about what is to be sustained, for whom, and by what means. The paper concludes that advancing meaningful sustainability requires confronting these discursive complexities, integrating new scientific and technological realities, and recognizing the centrality of political economy and cultural diversity in shaping environmental futures.

title: Strategic issues in customer relationship management (CRM) implementation
abstract: The number of customer relationship management (CRM) implementations has grown dramatically in recent years. However, few academic studies of the issues associated with the implementation of the concept are available. This paper offers a modest contribution through the analysis of a case study of a CRM implementation at a UK‐based manufacturing company. The case study illustrates that CRM is a complex and holistic concept, organised around business processes and the integration of information technologies. The study also highlights that implementing CRM requires effective leadership, sourcing, targeting and evaluation strategies.

title: THE EMERGENCE OF MULTISPECIES ETHNOGRAPHY
abstract: This paper traces the emergence of multispecies ethnography as a new anthropological approach that foregrounds the entanglements of humans with animals, plants, fungi, and microbes. Moving beyond traditional anthropocentric frameworks, multispecies ethnography examines how diverse organisms participate in shaping political, economic, and cultural worlds, challenging established boundaries between nature and culture. Drawing on theoretical influences such as Agamben, Haraway, and Deleuze and Guattari, the authors situate this genre within broader debates about the definition of “culture” and “species,” as well as the shifting concept of anthropos in the Anthropocene. Through case studies and collaborative projects like the Multispecies Salon, the paper demonstrates how multispecies ethnography reveals new forms of biocultural hope and ethical engagement amid environmental crises. Ultimately, it argues that this approach not only reconfigures anthropological methods and objects of study but also prompts critical reflection on the stakes of human-nonhuman relations in a rapidly changing world.

title: Techniques for extraction and isolation of natural products: a comprehensive review
abstract: Natural products have long served as a foundation for drug discovery, yet their low abundance in natural sources poses significant challenges for their extraction and isolation. This comprehensive review examines both conventional and modern techniques employed in the extraction and isolation of bioactive compounds from natural medicines, including methods such as maceration, percolation, decoction, reflux extraction, Soxhlet extraction, pressurized liquid extraction, supercritical fluid extraction, ultrasound-assisted extraction, and microwave-assisted extraction. The review discusses the principles, advantages, disadvantages, and practical applications of each method, highlighting factors that influence extraction efficiency such as solvent selection, particle size, temperature, duration, and solvent-to-solid ratio. Emphasis is placed on the growing adoption of greener and more selective techniques to improve yield and purity while reducing time and solvent consumption. By providing a critical evaluation of these methodologies, this review aims to guide researchers in selecting appropriate strategies for phytochemical investigation and drug development from natural products.

title: Challenges in cardiac tissue engineering.
abstract: Cardiac tissue engineering aims to create functional tissue constructs that can reestablish the structure and function of injured myocardium. Engineered constructs can also serve as high-fidelity models for studies of cardiac development and disease. In a general case, the biological potential of the cell-the actual 'tissue engineer'-is mobilized by providing highly controllable three-dimensional environments that can mediate cell differentiation and functional assembly. For cardiac regeneration, some of the key requirements that need to be met are the selection of a human cell source, establishment of cardiac tissue matrix, electromechanical cell coupling, robust and stable contractile function, and functional vascularization. We review here the potential and challenges of cardiac tissue engineering for developing therapies that could prevent or reverse heart failure.

title: Climate change and society : sociological perspectives
abstract: This paper examines the multifaceted impacts of climate change on society through a sociological lens, focusing on critical sectors such as water resources, food production, energy use, coastal communities, and broader economic and social systems. It highlights how shifting weather patterns and rising temperatures are altering water availability and quality, threatening agricultural productivity, and increasing energy demands for cooling while reducing heating needs. The vulnerability of coastal regions to sea level rise and intensified storms is discussed, alongside the heightened risks faced by developing countries and marginalized populations. The analysis underscores that while some short-term benefits may arise in certain regions, the long-term consequences of climate change are likely to exacerbate social inequalities, disrupt infrastructure, and pose significant challenges to public health, national security, and economic stability. The paper calls for comprehensive adaptation strategies that address both environmental changes and their societal ramifications.

title: Biopython: freely available Python tools for computational molecular biology and bioinformatics
abstract: Biopython is a comprehensive open-source collection of Python libraries designed to facilitate computational molecular biology and bioinformatics. Developed through international collaboration, Biopython provides modules for reading and writing a wide range of sequence and alignment file formats, manipulating biological sequences and annotations, parsing macromolecular structures, and interfacing with widely used tools such as BLAST, ClustalW, and EMBOSS. The toolkit also supports access to key online databases, statistical learning methods, population genetics analyses, and graphical visualization of genomic data. With its extensible object-oriented framework and integration with other open bioinformatics projects, Biopython serves both as an application programming interface for software development and as a resource for routine bioinformatics scripting tasks. Freely available under an open license, Biopython is supported by extensive documentation and an active user community.

title: Life Cycle Assessment as Entrepreneurial Tool for Business Management and Green Innovations
abstract: This paper explores the role of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) as an entrepreneurial tool for business management and the advancement of green innovations. Through a theoretical analysis supported by recent studies, the research demonstrates how LCA facilitates sustainable decision-making and enhances competitiveness by integrating environmental considerations across product, process, and service life cycles. The study highlights LCA’s applications in strategic planning, product development, operations management, and corporate social responsibility, emphasizing its value in fostering internal corporate entrepreneurship and driving green innovation. By adopting LCA, firms can better identify opportunities for environmental improvement, support sustainable business practices, and create value through innovation, positioning themselves for success in a transitioning green economy.

title: Ultrafast laser processing of materials: from science to industry
abstract: Ultrafast laser processing, utilizing tightly focused femtosecond and picosecond pulses, has rapidly advanced from fundamental research to industrial applications, enabling precise three-dimensional structuring of materials at sub-100-nanometer scales. This review highlights the unique capabilities of ultrashort laser pulses for localized photomodification through nonlinear light–matter interactions, offering high spatial resolution and flexible control over fabrication parameters such as pulse duration and polarization. Recent technological developments have significantly increased processing speeds and throughput, facilitating the transition from laboratory demonstrations to scalable manufacturing. Key achievements include the fabrication of complex micro- and nano-scale devices, high-density optical memories, photonic structures, and biomedical scaffolds with micrometer precision. The interplay between spatial resolution and fabrication efficiency is examined, along with emerging industrial and biomedical applications that leverage the unrestricted 3D structuring potential of ultrafast lasers. These advances position ultrafast laser processing as a transformative tool for next-generation nanotechnologies and industrial manufacturing.

title: The EANM practice guidelines for bone scintigraphy
abstract: PurposeThe radionuclide bone scan is the cornerstone of skeletal nuclear medicine imaging. Bone scintigraphy is a highly sensitive diagnostic nuclear medicine imaging technique that uses a radiotracer to evaluate the distribution of active bone formation in the skeleton related to malignant and benign disease, as well as physiological processes.MethodsThe European Association of Nuclear Medicine (EANM) has written and approved these guidelines to promote the use of nuclear medicine procedures of high quality.ConclusionThe present guidelines offer assistance to nuclear medicine practitioners in optimizing the diagnostic procedure and interpreting bone scintigraphy. These guidelines describe the protocols that are currently accepted and used routinely, but do not include all existing procedures. They should therefore not be taken as exclusive of other nuclear medicine modalities that can be used to obtain comparable results. It is important to remember that the resources and facilities available for patient care may vary.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

title: All biology is computational biology
abstract: This paper argues that computational thinking and methods are now fundamental to all of biology, making computational biology central to the discipline. Computational approaches have transformed biological research by organizing knowledge through databases and ontologies, enabling large-scale data analysis, and providing statistical tools to uncover patterns and correlations invisible to traditional methods. These advances have produced a reference map of life that guides experimental research and turns conceptual ideas into testable hypotheses. Despite persistent skepticism from some in the biological community, the integration of mathematical, statistical, and computational techniques is reshaping biology into a quantitative science. The next modern synthesis in biology will be driven by these methods becoming core components of mainstream biological training, ultimately dissolving distinctions between computational and experimental biologists.

title: Lateral flow assays
abstract: Lateral flow assays (LFAs) are widely used, low-cost, and rapid diagnostic devices with significant applications in biomedicine, agriculture, food safety, and environmental monitoring. This review outlines the fundamental principles and key components of LFAs, with a particular focus on lateral flow immunoassays (LFIAs) that utilize antibodies as recognition elements. The structure and operation of LFIAs are described, including sample migration by capillary action through layered membranes containing immobilized reagents and the use of visual or instrument-based detection methods. The review discusses assay formats such as direct and competitive tests, highlights the importance of component quality—especially antibodies and nanoparticle labels—and addresses challenges in device manufacturing. The advantages of LFAs, including simplicity, portability, and suitability for point-of-care testing in diverse settings, are contrasted with limitations such as sensitivity and multiplexing capability. Recent advances and future directions for improving LFA performance and expanding their diagnostic applications are also explored.

title: Sustainable development (1987–2005): an oxymoron comes of age
abstract: The paper examines the conceptual history of 'sustainable development', from the Brundtland Commission's definition in 1987 to the present day. It argues that the superficial consensus that has characterized much of the early debate has given way to a series of parallel but distinct discourses around sustainability. The underlying assumptions behind much of the discussion are assessed, as is the move, after the first Earth Summit (1992), to focus on rights, rather than needs, as the principal line of enquiry. This analytical attention to rights is linked to the neo-liberal economic agendas of the 1990s, and the growth of interest in congruent areas, including human security and the environment, social capital, critical natural capital and intellectual property rights. The paper argues that increasing attention to questions of biology and science studies has strengthened this 'rights-based' approach, as well as interest in the linkages between 'natural' and 'human' systems, including attention to questions of environmental justice. It is clear that issues of global environmental justice are as important as they were when the concept of 'sustainable development' was in its infancy, but the new material realities of science and the environment in the 21st century demand a re-engagement with their social consequences, something which is largely ignored by the (market) liberal consensus. title: Coupled spin and valley physics in monolayers of MoS2 and other group-VI dichalcogenides.
abstract: We demonstrate that monolayers of MoS2 and related group-VI dichalcogenides exhibit coupled spin and valley physics arising from the interplay of inversion symmetry breaking and strong spin-orbit coupling. Using symmetry analysis and effective Hamiltonian models supported by first-principles calculations, we show that the valence band edges near the K points are described by massive Dirac fermions with pronounced spin-valley coupling, leading to robust suppression of spin and valley relaxation. This coupling results in the coexistence of valley Hall and spin Hall effects in both electron- and hole-doped regimes, with valley-contrasting spin splitting forbidding independent flips of spin or valley indices. Additionally, frequency-dependent optical selection rules enable selective photoexcitation of carriers with specific combinations of spin and valley indices, allowing for photo-induced spin Hall and valley Hall effects that generate long-lived accumulations at sample boundaries. Our findings reveal a pathway for integrating valleytronics and spintronics in two-dimensional materials with strong spin-orbit coupling and broken inversion symmetry, offering new opportunities for information processing in next-generation electronic and optoelectronic devices.

title: The Impact of Entrepreneurship Education in Higher Education: A Systematic Review and Research Agenda
abstract: This paper systematically reviews 159 empirical studies published between 2004 and 2016 to assess the impact of entrepreneurship education (EE) in higher education, employing an integrated teaching model framework to analyze the relationship between pedagogical methods and entrepreneurial outcomes. The review reveals that most EE impact research continues to focus on short-term, subjective measures such as attitudes and intentions, with limited attention to long-term outcomes like venture creation and business performance. Furthermore, studies often lack detailed descriptions of the pedagogies employed, hindering understanding of how specific teaching approaches influence results. The findings highlight persistent methodological limitations and contradictory evidence regarding EE’s effectiveness, which may be attributed to variations in pedagogical models, contextual factors, and individual differences. The paper calls for future research to adopt novel impact indicators—including those related to emotion, mindset, and the intention-to-behavior transition—and to explore the moderating effects of person-, context-, and pedagogy-specific variables. By providing a comprehensive synthesis and proposing a research agenda, this review advances the theoretical and practical understanding of how university-based EE can be designed and evaluated for greater impact.

title: Lie Algebras in Particle Physics
abstract: Howard Georgi is the co-inventor (with Sheldon Glashow) of the SU(5) theory. This extensively revised and updated edition of his classic text makes the theory of Lie groups accessible to graduate students, while offering a perspective on the way in which knowledge of such groups can provide an insight into the development of unified theories of strong, weak, and electromagnetic interactions.

title: Nanobubble Technology in Environmental Engineering: Revolutionization Potential and Challenges.
abstract: Nanobubble Technology in Environmental Engineering: Revolutionization Potential & Challenges Tao Lyu, Shubiao Wu*, Robert J. G. Mortimer, Gang Pan* School of Animal, Rural and Environmental Sciences, Nottingham Trent University, Brackenhurst Campus, Nottinghamshire NG25 0QF, United Kingdom Centre of Integrated Water-Energy-Food studies (iWEF), Nottingham Trent University, Nottinghamshire NG25 0QF, United Kingdom Aarhus Institute of Advanced Studies, Aarhus University, Høegh-Guldbergs Gade 6B, DK-8000 Aarhus C, Denmark Research Center for Eco-Environmental Sciences, Chinese Academy of Sciences, 18 Shuangqing Road, Beijing 100085, China

title: The role of representative design in an ecological approach to cognition.
abstract: Egon Brunswik argued that psychological processes are adapted to environmental properties. He proposed the method of representative design to capture these processes and advocated that psychology be a science of organism-environment relations. Representative design involves randomly sampling stimuli from the environment or creating stimuli in which environmental properties are preserved. This departs from systematic design. The authors review the development of representative design, examine its use in judgment and decision-making research, and demonstrate the effect of design on research findings. They suggest that some of the practical difficulties associated with representative design may be overcome with modern technologies. The importance of representative design in psychology and the implications of this method for ecological approaches to cognition are discussed.

title: Digital Transformation in Materials Science: A Paradigm Change in Material's Development
abstract: Digital transformation is fundamentally reshaping materials science by integrating automation, artificial intelligence, and data-driven methodologies throughout the material development process. This review examines current advancements in the digitalization of materials research, emphasizing the automation of synthesis, characterization, and data analysis across diverse material classes. Key technologies such as robotic synthesis, flow chemistry, and high-throughput characterization are highlighted for their ability to increase experimental efficiency, reproducibility, and data quality while reducing human bias. The paper discusses the challenges of adapting automated systems to accommodate varied reaction conditions and material types, as well as the need for standardized data management and interoperability among analytical tools. The authors outline future perspectives for a fully digitalized materials research ecosystem, where integrated workflows enable accelerated discovery and optimization of new materials. Ultimately, this paradigm shift promises to transform traditional research approaches, fostering innovation and collaboration in the field of materials science.

title: ‘You have to find your slant, your groove:’ one physical education teacher's efforts to employ transformative pedagogy
abstract: This digital ethnographic study explores the efforts of an elementary school physical education teacher, Harry, to implement transformative pedagogy (TP) aimed at promoting social justice within his teaching practice. Guided by Cochran-Smith’s pedagogical principles for social justice education, the research employed seven qualitative methods—including interviews, observations, document analysis, and digital artifacts—to examine Harry’s pedagogical approaches, curricular content, and organizational structures. The findings reveal five central themes: fostering communities of learners through restorative practices; leveraging students’ backgrounds for a democratic curriculum; integrating skill development with affective learning; navigating challenges related to social justice literacy; and employing diverse assessment strategies. The study highlights both the facilitators and barriers Harry encountered in enacting TP, emphasizing that transformative approaches must be individualized and context-specific rather than prescriptive. Implications are discussed for teacher educators seeking to support both preservice and inservice physical education teachers in adopting pedagogies that foreground equity and social justice.

title: Social limits to economic theory
abstract: This dissertation effects a complete re-orientation of economic theory. It shows how the economic cannot be analysed separately from the political and the social, and lays the foundation for an integrated political economy. The work examines the philosophical difficulties faced by economists, and re-draws the history of economic thought as a response to methodological dilemmas. The traditional History of Economics textbooks re-write the history in terms of the contemporary paradigm. This dissertation, by contrast, shows how the philosophical debates have shaped the trajectory of economics, and how the orientations of the schools undergo major changes so as to attempt to deal with the fundamental dilemmas of a 'policy science’.
