The roles played by the laser frequency, the pulse duration, and the system temperature are illustrated numerically and experimentally. Alignment is extended to three-dimensional orientational control, a method of hindering the rotation about all three axes of polyatomic molecules. We conclude with a discussion of potential applications of intense laser alignment.

title: ABC of Learning and Teaching in Medicine
abstract: This review evaluates the second edition of 'ABC of Learning and Teaching in Medicine' by Peter Cantillon and Diana Wood, highlighting its value as an accessible introductory text for new medical educators. The book’s concise format, with 17 chapters spanning just over 80 pages, makes it approachable for beginners while covering essential topics such as curriculum design, collaborative learning, assessment methods, feedback skills, clinical education, professionalism, and support for struggling students. The inclusion of visuals and practical tools enhances comprehension and retention. Each chapter offers further reading to supplement information, addressing potential gaps due to brevity. The reviewer recommends this book as a foundational resource for faculty development and anticipates the publication of a Korean edition to further support local medical educators.

title: The Marine Microbial Eukaryote Transcriptome Sequencing Project (MMETSP): Illuminating the Functional Diversity of Eukaryotic Life in the Oceans through Transcriptome Sequencing
abstract: Current sampling of genomic sequence data from eukaryotes is relatively poor, biased, and inadequate to address important questions about their biology, evolution, and ecology; this Community Page describes a resource of 700 transcriptomes from marine microbial eukaryotes to help understand their role in the world's oceans.

title: A strategy to apply machine learning to small datasets in materials science
abstract: The application of machine learning (ML) in materials science is often constrained by the limited size and diversity of available datasets, impeding the development of accurate predictive models. This study systematically investigates the relationship between dataset size, model degree of freedom (DoF), and predictive precision in ML models for materials properties. We demonstrate that the effect of data size on prediction accuracy is mediated through model DoF, with increased precision typically requiring higher DoF, which can lead to underfitting and large prediction bias when data are scarce. To address this challenge, we propose incorporating crude estimations of target properties into the feature space, enabling more accurate predictions without increasing model complexity. Through case studies on band gap prediction in binary semiconductors, lattice thermal conductivity, and elastic properties of zeolites, we show that this strategy significantly enhances ML model performance using small datasets, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy. Our findings provide a generalizable approach for constructing robust ML models in materials science where data availability is limited.

title: Physics of the rhythmic applause.
abstract: This study investigates the collective phenomenon of rhythmic applause observed in concert halls, analyzing its emergence and dynamics through experimental recordings and theoretical modeling. The research reveals that while rhythmic applause shares features with other synchronization systems, it exhibits unique behaviors, notably the sudden onset of synchronization following a period of incoherence and the intermittent loss and reappearance of synchrony. Experimental data from both natural and controlled settings demonstrate that synchronization arises via period doubling of individual clapping rhythms, leading to alternating synchronized and unsynchronized phases. These findings are interpreted within the framework of the Kuramoto model for coupled non-identical oscillators, highlighting the role of memory effects and frustration in the system. The results provide new insights into social self-organization and extend the applicability of synchronization models to human collective behavior.
venue: Physical review. E, Statistical physics, plasmas, fluids, and related interdisciplinary topics

title: Traditional Ecological Knowledge in Environmental Assessment and Management
abstract: It is now a policy requirement that 'traditional ecological knowledge' (TEK) be incorporated into environmental assessment and resource management in the North. However, there is little common understanding about what TEK is, and no guidance on how to implement the policy in public arenas where knowledge claims must be tested. The problems are inconsistent and unclear definitions of TEK, and insufficient attention to appropriate methods of organizing and presenting it for assessment and management purposes. TEK can be classified as knowledge about the environment, knowledge about the use of the environment, values about the environment, and the knowledge system itself. All categories are required for environmental assessment, but each must be presented and examined differently. TEK and 'Western' science provide partially different information, based on different sets of observations and procedures, and sometimes on different knowledge claims. It is important that TEK be comprehensible and testable as a knowledge claim in public reviews, and usable for ongoing public monitoring and co-management processes. To this end, certain procedures are recommended for recording, organizing, and presenting TEK, with particular emphasis on the need to differentiate between observation and inference or association. Documenting TEK as recommended usually requires trained intermediaries, but they in turn require the support and cooperation of those who have TEK. One consequence is that it is often both impractical and inappropriate to require development proponents to incorporate TEK into their environmental impact statements. However, the environmental assessment process must facilitate the use of TEK in the public review phase.

title: Practical Physiological Chemistry
abstract: THIS is really the second edition of Dr. Aders Plimmer's excellent manual. The first appearance of the book was privately printed for use in the practical classes of physiological chemistry at University College, London, but a good many copies were distributed to other teachers, and to the Press. A favourable notice of this preliminary edition appeared in the pages of NATURE at the time. The publication of the book for general sale is an indication of the way in which the teachers of the subject welcomed the new departure in the presentation of the subject. For it Is a new departure; hitherto works on the subject have been written by physiologists; the present book is written by a chemist; it is physiological chemistry as opposed to chemical physiology.Practical Physiological Chemistry.By Dr. R. H. Aders Plimmer. Pp. viii + 270. (London: Longmans, Green and Co., 1910.) Price 6s. net.

title: Plasma physics of liquids—A focused review
abstract: This focused review examines the rapidly evolving field of plasma physics of liquids, encompassing both the initiation of plasma within liquids and the complex interactions at plasma–liquid interfaces. The review highlights the broad spectrum of established and emerging applications, from high-voltage switching and nanomaterial synthesis to plasma medicine and agriculture, while emphasizing the fundamental knowledge gaps that hinder further technological progress. Key challenges include elucidating the mechanisms of plasma initiation in liquids—where debates persist regarding electronic, bubble, and interfacial processes—and understanding the electrical phenomena at liquid surfaces. The authors advocate for interdisciplinary research, integrating insights from fields such as solid-state physics, analytical chemistry, electrochemistry, and molecular dynamics simulations, to address these challenges. By providing a comprehensive overview of reactor types, experimental complexities, and unresolved questions—including the roles of nanobubbles and phenomena like the floating water bridge—this review aims to foster collaboration across disciplines and proposes strategic directions for future experimental and computational studies in plasma–liquid systems.

title: The CompTox Chemistry Dashboard: a community data resource for environmental chemistry
abstract: The CompTox Chemistry Dashboard is a publicly accessible, web-based resource developed by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency to address the growing need for high-quality, structure-curated chemical data in environmental chemistry and computational toxicology. Integrating diverse data types—including physicochemical properties, environmental fate and transport, exposure, usage, in vivo toxicity, and in vitro bioassay data—the Dashboard serves as a central hub for researchers and regulators. Built on the rigorously curated DSSTox database, which now encompasses approximately 760,000 substances, the platform offers advanced search capabilities, batch processing, and direct access to multiple data streams in various formats. The Dashboard supports non-targeted chemical analysis and identification using mass spectrometry and links to additional EPA and public domain resources. Continuous expansion and quality control ensure that the Dashboard remains a dynamic and reliable tool for integrating, processing, visualizing, and delivering chemical information. Since its public launch in 2016, it has become an essential resource supporting research and regulatory programs worldwide in environmental science and toxicology.

title: Introducing Procedural Utility: Not Only What, But Also How Matters
abstract: People not only care about outcomes, they also value the procedures which lead to the outcomes. Procedural utility is a potentially important source of human well-being. This paper aims at introducing the concept of procedural utility into economics, and argues that it should be incorporated more widely into economic theory and empirical research. Three building blocks of a concept of procedural utility are outlined and it is suggested how procedural utility can be fruitfully integrated. Evidence from a broad range of social sciences is reviewed in order to show that procedural utility is a relevant concept for economics.

title: Economic Empowerment of Small Businesses Through Zakat Funds at the Amil Zakat Infaq Shadaqah Institute in Surakarta
abstract: This study examines the management and impact of zakat fund distribution on the economic empowerment of small business communities by the Amil Zakat Infaq Shadaqah Institute (LazisMu) in Surakarta. Employing a qualitative field research approach, data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation involving LazisMu administrators and small business recipients. The findings reveal that zakat funds are allocated to underprivileged individuals with entrepreneurial potential, based on recommendations and thorough assessments. LazisMu implements various empowerment programs, including direct business capital assistance, entrepreneurship training, mentoring, and provision of equipment or financial support tailored to the needs of mustahiq. Notable initiatives such as the By Friend and By Request programs at LazisMu UMS and the Economic Empowerment Program at LazisMu PDM Surakarta City have contributed to increased business capacity and sustainability among beneficiaries. The study concludes that effective zakat fund management and targeted empowerment strategies play a significant role in enhancing the welfare and independence of small business actors, thereby fostering broader community economic development in Surakarta.
venue: Demak Universal Journal of Islam and Sharia

title: Handbook of Public Communication of Science and Technology
abstract: Comprehensive yet accessible, this key Handbook provides an up-to-date overview of the fast growing and increasingly important area of ‘public communication of science and technology’, from both research and practical perspectives. As well as introducing the main issues, arenas and professional perspectives involved, it presents the findings of earlier research and the conclusions previously drawn. Unlike most existing books on this topic, this unique volume couples an overview of the practical problems faced by practitioners with a thorough review of relevant literature and research.  The practical Handbook format ensures it is a student-friendly resource, but its breadth of scope and impressive contributors means that it is also ideal for practitioners and professionals working in the field. Combining the contributions of different disciplines (media and journalism studies, sociology and history of science), the perspectives of different geographical and cultural contexts, and by selecting key contributions from appropriate and well-respected authors, this original text provides an interdisciplinary as well as a global approach to public communication of science and technology.

title: Metabolic engineering for the production of natural products.
abstract: Natural products and their derivatives play an important role in modern healthcare as frontline treatments for many diseases and as inspiration for chemically synthesized therapeutics. With advances in sequencing and recombinant DNA technology, many of the biosynthetic pathways responsible for the production of these chemically complex yet valuable compounds have been elucidated. With an ever-expanding toolkit of biosynthetic components, metabolic engineering is an increasingly powerful method to improve natural product titers and generate novel compounds. Heterologous production platforms have enabled access to pathways from difficult to culture strains, systems biology and metabolic modeling tools have resulted in increasing predictive and analytic capabilities, advances in expression systems and regulation have enabled the fine-tuning of pathways for increased efficiency, and characterization of individual pathway components has facilitated the construction of hybrid pathways for the production of new compounds. These advances in the many aspects of metabolic engineering not only have yielded fascinating scientific discoveries but also make it an increasingly viable approach for the optimization of natural product biosynthesis.
venue: Annual Review of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering

title: A History of Archaeological Thought
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive examination of the development of archaeological thought from its origins in antiquarianism to contemporary theoretical debates. It traces the evolution of the discipline through key historical periods, including the influence of classical and text-based approaches, the rise of scientific and prehistoric archaeology, and the impact of evolutionary, culture-historical, and processual paradigms. The analysis highlights how social, political, and intellectual contexts have shaped archaeological interpretation and methodology, with particular attention to issues such as nationalism, colonialism, racism, and the integration of social sciences. The paper also explores the emergence of postprocessualism and alternative theoretical frameworks, culminating in a discussion of current challenges related to subjectivity, relativism, and archaeology’s relevance in broader academic and public spheres. Through this historical overview, the paper underscores the dynamic and contested nature of archaeological inquiry and its ongoing negotiation between scientific rigor and interpretive flexibility.

title: Systems biology of the structural proteome
abstract: The integration of protein structural data into genome-scale models (GEMs) has advanced systems biology by enabling multi-scale analyses that connect genotype to phenotype through detailed molecular mechanisms. This study presents the development and application of GEMs with protein structures (GEM-PRO) for Escherichia coli and Thermotoga maritima, utilizing a systematic pipeline to map genes to high-quality experimental and homology-modeled protein structures. Comparative analyses demonstrate the utility of GEM-PRO in exploring temperature-dependent growth, protein fold family distributions, substrate specificity, and proteome characteristics. The expanded structural coverage enhances the predictive power of systems biology models, facilitating insights into metabolic specificity, protein complex stoichiometry, and adaptive strategies across organisms. To support dissemination and training, the GEM-PRO knowledgebase and tutorials are made publicly available, empowering researchers to apply this framework to their own studies. Overall, GEM-PRO bridges molecular and systems-level data, providing a comprehensive platform for investigating the structural basis of cellular functions and enabling new directions in comparative and structural systems biology.

title: Molecular Biology, Nucleic Acids, and the Future of Medicine
abstract: It seems particularly fitting, in this symposium, to try to assess the prob able and possible impact of molecular biology and its important com ponent, the structure and function of nucleic acids, on the future of medicine. Although I attempt specific predictions with considerable trepi dation, not being qualified in either fortunetelling or medicine, I do so in the firm belief that the findings and concepts of molecular biology will play a leading role in the future of medicine. Medicine, after all, primarily involves the application of biological concepts and understanding to the health and welfare of man.

title: Theory of neutrinos: a white paper
abstract: This paper is a review of the present status of neutrino mass physics, which grew out of an APS sponsored study of neutrinos in 2004. After a discussion of the present knowledge of neutrino masses and mixing and some popular ways to probe the new physics implied by recent data, it summarizes what can be learned about neutrino interactions as well as the nature of new physics beyond the Standard Model from the various proposed neutrino experiments. The intriguing possibility that neutrino mass physics may be at the heart of our understanding of a long standing puzzle of cosmology, i.e. the origin of matter–antimatter asymmetry is also discussed.

title: Synthetic biology - putting engineering into biology
abstract: Synthetic biology represents the application of engineering principles to biological systems, aiming to systematically design and construct novel or improved biological entities for diverse applications. This review explores how foundational engineering concepts—such as modularity, abstraction hierarchies, standardization, and the separation of design from fabrication—are being integrated into biology. Advances in artificial gene networks, de novo DNA synthesis, and protein engineering have enabled the creation of engineered biological functions at multiple levels, including genetic circuits, protein domains, and metabolic pathways. The paper highlights key achievements such as toggle switches, oscillators, spatial pattern formation, and rational enzyme redesign, demonstrating the potential for modular recombination and computational design in synthetic biology. The increasing accessibility of DNA synthesis technologies further supports the realization of complex synthetic systems. While challenges remain due to biological complexity and evolutionary dynamics, the adoption of engineering frameworks is driving progress toward predictable and scalable bioengineering. The review concludes by discussing the implications for bioinformatics and emphasizing the need for continued development of standards and tools to support the systematic engineering of living systems.

title: Pedagogic partnership in higher education: encountering emotion in learning and enhancing student wellbeing
abstract: Despite emotion being recognized as fundamental to learning, the affective aspects of learning have often been side-lined in higher education. In the context of rising student wellbeing challenges, exploring ways of supporting students and their emotions in learning is increasingly significant. Pedagogic partnerships have the potential to help students to recognize and work with their emotions in their learning in a positive manner. As such, pedagogic partnerships offer opportunities to promote resilience and enhance student wellbeing. In this paper, we develop partnership research in three ways by: 1) considering the ways in which pedagogic partnership may support students to encounter emotions and empower them to develop resilience, leading to positive wellbeing; 2) exploring how this process might be achieved in the disciplinary context of geography; and 3) developing an evidence-based model to summarize the potential effect of pedagogic partnership in enhancing student wellbeing. We draw upon two case studies of student-faculty and student-student pedagogic partnership within geography curricula in order to evidence that emotional awareness in learning comes through the joys and struggles of working in partnership. We argue that pedagogic partnership may be developed to support the wellbeing of modern-day higher education communities.
venue: Journal of Geography in Higher Education

title: Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics
abstract: European scale harmonized monitoring of atmospheric composition was initiated in the early 1970s, and the activity has generated a comprehensive dataset (available at http://www.emep.int) which allows the evaluation of regional and spatial trends of air pollution during a period of nearly 40 years. Results from the monitoring made within EMEP, the European Monitoring and Evaluation Programme, show large reductions in ambient concentrations and deposition of sulphur species during the last decades. Reductions are in the order of 70–90% since the year 1980, and correspond well with reported emission changes. Also reduction in emissions of nitrogen oxides (NOx) are reflected in the measurements, with an average decrease of nitrogen dioxide and nitrate in precipitation by about 23% and 25% respectively since 1990. Only minor reductions are however seen since the late 1990s. The concentrations of total nitrate in air have decreased on average only by 8% since 1990, and fewer sites show a significant trend. A majority of the EMEP sites show a decreasing trend in reduced nitrogen both in air and precipitation on the order of 25% since 1990. Deposition of base cations has decreased during the past 30 years, and the pH in precipitation has increased across Europe. Large inter annual variations in the particulate matter mass concentrations reflect meteorological variability, but still there is a relatively clear overall decrease at several sites during the last decade. With few observations going back to the 1990s, the observed chemical composition is applied to document a change in particulate matter (PM) mass even since 1980. These data indicate an overall reduction of about 5 μg/m3 from sulphate alone. Despite the significant reductions in sulphur emissions, sulphate still remains one of the single most important compounds contributing to regional scale aerosol mass concentration. Long-term ozone trends at EMEP sites show a mixed pattern. The year-to-year variability in ozone due to varying meteorological conditions is substantial, making it hard to separate the trends caused by emission change from other effects. For the Nordic countries the data indicate a reduced occurrence of very low concentrations. The most pronounced change in the frequency distribution is seen at sites in the UK and the Netherlands, showing a reduction in the higher values. Smaller changes are seen in Germany, while in Switzerland and Austria, no change is seen in the frequency distribution of ozone. The lack of long-term data series is a major obstacle for studying trends in volatile organic compounds (VOC). The scatter in the data is large, and significant changes are only found for certain components and stations. Concentrations of the heavy metals lead and cadmium have decreased in both air and precipitation during the last 20 years, with reductions in the order of 80–90% for Pb and 64–84% for Cd (precipitation and air respectively). The measurements of total gaseous mercury indicate a dramatic decrease in concentrations during 1980 to about 1993. Trends in hexachlorocyclohexanes (HCHs) show a significant decrease in annual average air concentrations. For other persistent organic pollutants (POPs) the patterns is mixed, and differs between sites and between measurements in air versus precipitation.

title: Biology and biotechnology of Trichoderma
abstract: Trichoderma species are globally distributed soilborne ascomycetes renowned for their ecological versatility, efficient substrate colonization, and potent degradative enzyme systems. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the biodiversity, phylogeny, and distinguishing characteristics of Trichoderma, highlighting advances in molecular identification and genome sequencing that have clarified species boundaries and evolutionary relationships. The genus exhibits diverse interactions with plant hosts, ranging from beneficial biocontrol to occasional pathogenicity, underpinned by sophisticated defense mechanisms and secondary metabolite production. Trichoderma reesei, in particular, is a cornerstone of industrial biotechnology due to its prolific cellulase production for biofuel generation, with genetic engineering and the recent discovery of a sexual cycle further enhancing its utility in research and industry. The availability of genomic resources for multiple Trichoderma species has facilitated functional studies on environmental response, enzyme regulation, and metabolic adaptation. Collectively, these insights underscore the genus’s significance as both a model organism in fungal biology and a valuable resource for sustainable agricultural and biotechnological applications.

title: Rhetorical Variation across Research Article Abstracts in Environmental Science and Applied Linguistics
abstract: Abstract is of a pivotal genre in scientific communication, assisting not only highly selective readers with judgment of the pertinent articles but also researchers in disseminating new knowledge and intellectual discoveries. Difficult yet challenging, however, is the task of writing effective abstracts particularly among non-English speaking scholars. This study reports on the identification of moves and co-existing linguistic features commonly used in environmental science and applied linguistics research article abstracts. 200 research article abstracts published during the years of 2010-2013 were analyzed with reference to Hyland’s analytical framework. The two-tier analysis reveals a typical rhetorical structure including a cluster of linguistic features associated with certain pieces of information presented in each particular move, elucidating how research article abstracts in both fields are conventionally constructed. With the presence of all five moves, the structures of I-P-M-Pr-C and P-M-Pr-C were most prevalent among the corpus of environmental science and applied linguistics, respectively. All of the moves, except for Introduction move, were conventional across the two disciplines. Pedagogical implications of the findings are useful particularly for academic reading and writing instruction, enabling language teachers to empower their learners with strategies that contribute to the enhancement of success for publishing in scholarly leading publication.

title: Life Cycle Assessment as Entrepreneurial Tool for Business Management and Green Innovations
abstract: A transition for a green economy has encouraged companies to use new tools which promote internal corporate entrepreneurship, increase the competitiveness and achieve sustainable results. This article presented a theoretical discussion of how the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) can presents as an entrepreneurial tool for modern business management and green innovation. Studies of LCA were analyzed showing benefits and applications in the areas of strategic planning, production, process of development of products, search and development, social and environmental responsibility, and marketing. As for green innovations, there were analyzed studies of innovations in products, processes and services. The tool assists in making sustainable decisions, fortifies the management of the business processes, the management of operations and the promotion of greener innovations.

title: Machine learning in medicine: Addressing ethical challenges
abstract: Machine learning (ML) is rapidly transforming the field of medicine, offering unprecedented opportunities for improved diagnostics, personalized treatment, and healthcare efficiency. However, the integration of ML technologies into clinical practice raises significant ethical challenges that must be addressed to ensure responsible and equitable use. This paper examines key ethical issues associated with ML in medicine, including concerns about data privacy, algorithmic bias, transparency, accountability, and informed consent. We analyze how these challenges can impact patient trust, exacerbate health disparities, and complicate clinical decision-making. The paper also explores current frameworks and guidelines aimed at mitigating ethical risks and highlights the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration among clinicians, data scientists, ethicists, and policymakers. By critically evaluating existing approaches and proposing strategies for ethical oversight, we underscore the need for ongoing vigilance and adaptive governance as ML becomes increasingly embedded in healthcare systems. Our findings emphasize that addressing ethical challenges is essential not only for safeguarding patient rights but also for realizing the full potential of machine learning to advance medical care.

title: A reflection on lithium-ion battery cathode chemistry
abstract: This review examines the evolution of lithium-ion battery cathode chemistry, tracing its origins from early intercalation compounds to the development of high-energy-density oxide cathodes that underpin modern lithium-ion technology. Emphasizing the critical role of fundamental solid-state chemistry and physics, the article reflects on how advances in understanding structure-composition-property relationships enabled the rational design and optimization of three major classes of oxide cathodes: layered, spinel, and polyanion families. The review highlights the pivotal contributions of John Goodenough’s group in pioneering these chemistries, which have facilitated significant increases in cell voltage, energy density, and safety. By contextualizing these scientific milestones within broader societal impacts—such as portable electronics, electric vehicles, and renewable energy integration—the article underscores the importance of continued basic research for future innovations in battery materials.

title: The Number of Scholarly Documents on the Public Web
abstract: This study estimates the number of English-language scholarly documents accessible on the public web by applying capture-recapture statistical methods to the coverage of Google Scholar and Microsoft Academic Search. Through systematic sampling and overlap analysis of citation data across fifteen academic fields, the research finds that at least 114 million scholarly documents are available online, with Google Scholar indexing nearly 100 million of these. Approximately 24% (27 million) of the documents are freely accessible without subscription or payment, though this proportion varies widely by discipline, ranging from 12% to 50%. The findings highlight both the vast scale and disciplinary variation in the accessibility of scholarly literature on the public web, providing a quantitative foundation for understanding the reach and limitations of major academic search engines.

title: Sisvar: a computer statistical analysis system
abstract: Sisvar is a statistical analysis system, first released in 1996 although its development began in 1994. The first version was done in the programming language Pascal and compiled with Borland Turbo Pascal 3. Sisvar was developed to achieve some specific goals. The first objective was to obtain software that could be used directly on the statistical experimental course of the Department of Exact Science at the Federal University of Lavras. The second objective was to initiate the development of a genuinely Brazilian free software program that met the demands and peculiarities of research conducted in the country. The third goal was to present statistical analysis software for the Brazilian scientific community that would allow research results to be analyzed efficiently and reliably. All of the initial goals were achieved. Sisvar gained acceptance by the scientific community because it provides reliable, accurate, precise, simple and robust results, and allows users a greater degree of interactivity.

title: Testing the nature of dark compact objects: a status report
abstract: Dark compact objects, such as black holes, offer a unique window into the most extreme gravitational environments and are central to addressing fundamental questions in physics, including the nature of dark matter, the resolution of spacetime singularities, and the fate of information in black hole evaporation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the current theoretical and observational status of dark compact objects, emphasizing both standard black holes and a wide range of exotic alternatives motivated by extensions to general relativity and quantum gravity. We discuss the taxonomy, structure, dynamics, and stability of these objects, highlighting key physical parameters that distinguish them from classical black holes. Recent advances in gravitational-wave astronomy and high-resolution electromagnetic observations have enabled unprecedented tests of the Kerr black hole paradigm, offering new constraints on event horizons, tidal effects, multipole moments, and potential signatures such as gravitational-wave echoes. While current evidence strongly supports the existence of astrophysical black holes as described by general relativity, ongoing and future observations promise to further probe the possible existence of exotic compact objects and refine our understanding of strong gravity in the universe.

title: Conductivity engineering of graphene by defect formation
abstract: Transport measurements have revealed several exotic electronic properties of graphene. The possibility to influence the electronic structure and hence control the conductivity by adsorption or doping with adatoms is crucial in view of electronics applications. Here, we show that in contrast to expectation, the conductivity of graphene increases with increasing concentration of vacancy defects, by more than one order of magnitude. We obtain a pronounced enhancement of the conductivity after insertion of defects by both quantum mechanical transport calculations as well as experimental studies of carbon nano-sheets. Our finding is attributed to the defect induced mid-gap states, which create a region exhibiting metallic behaviour around the vacancy defects. The modification of the conductivity of graphene by the implementation of stable defects is crucial for the creation of electronic junctions in graphene-based electronics devices.

title: Lie Algebras in Particle Physics
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive introduction to the role of Lie algebras in particle physics, emphasizing their foundational importance in understanding symmetries and group structures underlying the Standard Model and beyond. The work systematically develops the mathematical framework of Lie algebras and their representations, illustrating how these concepts are applied to classify particles, describe gauge theories, and construct unified models. Key topics include isospin, flavor symmetries, and the embedding of symmetry groups relevant to strong, weak, and electromagnetic interactions. The exposition balances mathematical rigor with physical insight, making advanced algebraic methods accessible to physicists and highlighting their practical relevance in modern theoretical physics.

title: Asian management in the 21st century
abstract: Contrary to popular opinion, the crucial elements of the management process show strong continuity over time, but differ from one country to another, as a function of the local culture. Recent research reveals fundamental differences in the goals of business leaders from different societies. The article explores general characteristics of Asian management as opposed to management elsewhere, and what the study of Asian management and its cultural origins mean for the emerging Asian multinationals and for the state of the art in management research worldwide in the twenty-first century.

title: Strategy and Human Resource Management
abstract: How is human resource management (HRM) strategic to a firm's viability and how might it help to lay a basis for sustained competitive advantage? How can managers pursue their goals for labour productivity and organisational flexibility in socially acceptable ways? This book explores such questions. The authors develop a conceptual framework to provide an exploration of the growing field of strategic HRM. This text should be of interest to MBA students and advanced undergraduate and postgraduate students of HRM. It should also be an valuable resource for anyone interested in the role of HRM in business success.

title: Materials science aspects of zinc–air batteries: a review
abstract: Metal–air batteries are becoming of particular interest, from both fundamental and industrial viewpoints, for their high specific energy density compared to other energy storage devices, in particular the Li-ion systems. Among metal–air batteries, the zinc–air option represents a safe, environmentally friendly and potentially cheap and simple way to store and deliver electrical energy for both portable and stationary devices as well as for electric vehicles. Zinc–air batteries can be classified into primary (including also the mechanically rechargeable), electrically rechargeable (secondary), and fuel cells. Research on primary zinc–air batteries is well consolidated since many years. On the contrary, research on the electrically rechargeable ones still requires further efforts to overcome materials science and electrochemical issues related to charge and discharge processes. In addition, zinc–air fuel cells are also of great potential interest for smart grid energy storage and production. This review aims to report on the latest progresses and state-of-the-art of primary, secondary and mechanically rechargeable zinc–air batteries, and zinc–air fuel cells. In particular, this review focuses on the critical aspects of materials science, engineering, electrochemistry and mathematical modeling related to all zinc–air systems.
venue: Materials for Renewable and Sustainable Energy

title: Spin Ice State in Frustrated Magnetic Pyrochlore Materials
abstract: A frustrated system is one whose symmetry precludes the possibility that every pairwise interaction (“bond”) in the system can be satisfied at the same time. Such systems are common in all areas of physical and biological science. In the most extreme cases, they can have a disordered ground state with “macroscopic” degeneracy; that is, one that comprises a huge number of equivalent states of the same energy. Pauling's description of the low-temperature proton disorder in water ice was perhaps the first recognition of this phenomenon and remains the paradigm. In recent years, a new class of magnetic substance has been characterized, in which the disorder of the magnetic moments at low temperatures is precisely analogous to the proton disorder in water ice. These substances, known as spin ice materials, are perhaps the “cleanest” examples of such highly frustrated systems yet discovered. They offer an unparalleled opportunity for the study of frustration in magnetic systems at both an experimental and a theoretical level. This article describes the essential physics of spin ice, as it is currently understood, and identifies new avenues for future research on related materials and models.

title: Mathematical models in biology
abstract: Mathematical Models in Biology is an introductory book for readers interested in biological applications of mathematics and modeling in biology. A favorite in the mathematical biology community, it shows how relatively simple mathematics can be applied to a variety of models to draw interesting conclusions. Connections are made between diverse biological examples linked by common mathematical themes. A variety of discrete and continuous ordinary and partial differential equation models are explored. Although great advances have taken place in many of the topics covered, the simple lessons contained in Mathematical Models in Biology are still important and informative.  Shortly after the publication of Mathematical Models in Biology, the genomics revolution turned Mathematical Biology into a prominent area of interdisciplinary research. With this new millennium, biologists have discovered that mathematics is not only useful, but indispensable! As a result, there has been much resurgent interest in, and a huge expansion of, the fields collectively called mathematical biology. This book serves as a basic introduction to concepts in deterministic biological modeling.

title: The economics of animal health and production.
abstract: This study evaluates the potential of mass drug administration (MDA) with moxidectin to accelerate the elimination of onchocerciasis in Africa compared to the current standard of ivermectin. Using the stochastic, individual-based EPIONCHO-IBM model, the research simulates various scenarios across a range of endemicity levels, treatment frequencies, and coverage/adherence rates. Results indicate that biannual moxidectin MDA could halve the time required to achieve elimination of transmission (EoT) in mesoendemic areas and may be essential for achieving EoT in hyperendemic regions. The findings highlight significant limitations of annual ivermectin MDA in high-transmission settings and underscore the need for improved data on repeated moxidectin efficacy, individual response variability, effects on parasite development, and adherence patterns to refine projections. The study supports consideration of moxidectin as a key strategy to meet World Health Organization 2030 targets for onchocerciasis elimination, particularly where current interventions are insufficient.

title: Particle Physics and Inflationary Cosmology
abstract: With the invention of unified theories of strong, weak, electromagnetic and gravitational interactions, elementaryparticle physics has entered a very interesting and unusual stage of its development. The end of the 1960s saw the introduction of the Glashow‐Weinberg‐Salam unification of the weak and electromagnetic interactions. In 1974 came the grand unified theories of the strong, weak and electromagnetic interactions. Two years later we had supergravity, giving us the first hope of unifying all fundamental interactions, including gravitation. The beginning of the 1980s witnessed a renewal of interest in the Kaluza‐Klein theories and supergravity in higher‐dimensional space‐time. Nowadays superstring theory is the leading candidate for the role of “theory of everything.”

title: Mathematical models in biology
abstract: This dissertation explores the development and analysis of mathematical models to describe key biological processes, focusing on aerotaxis in bacteria, growth cone guidance in neurons, and endothelial cell deformation. For aerotaxis, the work presents a detailed comparison between conventional chemotaxis and oxygen-driven movement in Azospirillum brasilense, including experimental observations and the derivation of new mathematical models that incorporate turning frequencies and non-dimensional scaling. Numerical simulations and analytical results are used to investigate band formation and steady-state distributions. In the context of neuronal growth cone guidance, the dissertation reviews biological mechanisms of gradient sensing and constructs theoretical models, such as the cAMP-adenylate cyclase switch and adaptation-diffusion frameworks, to elucidate signal transduction pathways and cellular responses to external cues. The study further extends to modeling the viscoelastic properties of endothelial cells using networks of Kelvin bodies arranged in series and parallel, with parameter sensitivity analyses and network simulations revealing how mechanical forces influence cellular deformation under various flow conditions. Together, these investigations demonstrate the power of mathematical modeling in providing quantitative insights into complex biological phenomena and highlight directions for future research at the interface of mathematics and biology.

title: Environmental Policy Attitudes: Issues, Geographical Scale, and Political Trust
abstract: This article examines environmental policy attitudes, focusing on the differences in preferences across issue type (i.e., pollution, resource preservation) and geographical scale (i.e., local, national, global). In addition, we study whether an individual's trust in government influences environmental policy attitudes. Copyright (c) 2008 by the Southwestern Social Science Association.

title: Magnetic skyrmions: advances in physics and potential applications
abstract: Magnetic skyrmions are small swirling topological defects in the magnetization texture. Their stabilization and dynamics depend strongly on their topological properties. In most cases, they are induced by chiral interactions between atomic spins in non-centrosymmetric magnetic compounds or in thin films with broken inversion symmetry. Skyrmions can be extremely small, with diameters in the nanometre range, and behave as particles that can be moved, created and annihilated, which makes them suitable for ‘abacus’-type applications in information storage and logic technologies. Until recently, skyrmions had been observed only at low temperature and, in most cases, under large applied magnetic fields. An intense research effort has led to the identification of thin-film and multilayer structures in which skyrmions are now stable at room temperature and can be manipulated by electrical currents. The development of skyrmion-based topological spintronics holds promise for applications in the mid-term furure, even though many challenges, such as the achievement of writing, processing and reading functionalities at room temperature and in all-electrical manipulation schemes, still lie ahead. Magnetic skyrmions are topologically protected spin whirls that hold promise for applications because they can be controllably moved, created and annihilated. In this Review, the underlying physics of the stabilization of skyrmions at room temperature and their prospective use for spintronic applications are discussed.

title: The Limits of Reductionism in Medicine: Could Systems Biology Offer an Alternative?
abstract: Reductionism has long dominated medical science, shaping diagnosis, treatment, and prevention through the analysis of isolated components and singular causal factors. While this approach has yielded significant advances, it often overlooks the complex interactions and contextual factors inherent in human health. This essay critically examines four key manifestations of reductionism in medicine: the focus on singular factors, the emphasis on homeostasis as static stability, the limitations of inexact risk modification, and the additive treatment of coexisting conditions. Each practice illustrates how reductionist thinking can miss dynamic system behaviors, multifactorial risk profiles, and nonlinear treatment effects. The emerging field of systems biology offers a complementary perspective by emphasizing holistic analysis and computational modeling of biological networks. By recognizing the limitations of reductionism and integrating systems-oriented approaches, medicine may better account for complexity and improve patient care. This article lays the groundwork for further exploration of how systems biology could reshape clinical practice.

title: The Evolutionary synthesis : perspectives on the unification of biology
abstract: This paper examines the role of active information in evolutionary search algorithms by analyzing the Avida digital organism platform, which evolves logic functions using only nand gates. Drawing on conservation of information and no free lunch theorems, we demonstrate that successful search performance in Avida depends critically on domain-specific prior knowledge, such as reward stair steps that guide the synthesis of increasingly complex logic functions. Empirical evaluation reveals that removing these sources of active information significantly impairs search efficiency, while eliminating deleterious instructions enhances it. We further show that alternative evolutionary strategies leveraging the same prior knowledge can outperform Avida in generating target logic functions with fewer instructions. These findings highlight the necessity of external information for effective search in complex spaces and provide a quantitative framework for measuring the contribution of such information to algorithmic performance in digital evolution systems.

title: THE PHYSICS OF TRAFFIC
abstract: This monograph presents a comprehensive investigation into the complex dynamics of freeway traffic, emphasizing empirical spatiotemporal patterns and their theoretical interpretation. Challenging traditional traffic flow models, the author introduces the three-phase traffic theory to explain observed discrepancies between empirical data and earlier theories. The book systematically reviews historical developments in traffic research, details key features of free and congested traffic, and identifies fundamental empirical patterns such as wide moving jams, synchronized flow, and spontaneous breakdown phenomena. Through qualitative analysis accessible to a broad audience, the work elucidates the mechanisms underlying traffic pattern formation and transitions between distinct traffic phases. Subsequent sections develop a microscopic perspective on these patterns and explore practical engineering applications informed by the new theory. By integrating empirical evidence with innovative theoretical frameworks, this study advances understanding of traffic as a paradigmatic complex system and provides actionable insights for traffic management and infrastructure design.

title: Bone tissue engineering: recent advances and challenges.
abstract: Bone tissue engineering (BTE) has emerged as a promising alternative to traditional bone grafting techniques, addressing the increasing global demand for effective bone repair driven by aging populations and rising incidence of bone disorders. This review examines the fundamental principles of BTE, including the integration of biomaterials, cells, and bioactive factors to promote functional bone regeneration. Recent advances in scaffold design, particularly at the micro- and nanoscale, and the incorporation of biomimetic properties and growth factors are discussed. The review also evaluates various cellular strategies, such as the use of mesenchymal stem cells, embryonic stem cells, induced pluripotent stem cells, and platelet-rich plasma, highlighting their respective advantages and limitations for clinical translation. Despite significant progress, major challenges remain, notably the achievement of adequate vascularization at defect sites and the development of constructs that fully recapitulate native bone function. Addressing these obstacles is essential for advancing BTE toward widespread clinical application and will shape future research directions in the field.

title: Dynamics of Structures: Theory and Applications to Earthquake Engineering
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive exploration of structural dynamics with a focus on applications to earthquake engineering. It systematically develops the theoretical foundations and analytical methods for both single-degree-of-freedom (SDF) and multi-degree-of-freedom (MDF) systems, covering equations of motion, free and forced vibration, damping mechanisms, and numerical evaluation of dynamic response. The work details the response of linear and inelastic systems to various excitations, including harmonic, periodic, arbitrary, and seismic inputs, and introduces advanced topics such as generalized SDF systems, distributed mass and elasticity, and the finite element method. Special emphasis is placed on the earthquake response and design of multistory buildings, including linearly elastic, inelastic, and base-isolated structures, as well as the integration of structural dynamics principles into building codes and evaluation guidelines. Through rigorous analysis and practical examples, this study provides essential methodologies for predicting and mitigating earthquake-induced structural responses, supporting resilient design in civil engineering practice.

title: Tracking materials science data lineage to manage millions of materials experiments and analyses
abstract: In an era of rapid advancement of algorithms that extract knowledge from data, data and metadata management are increasingly critical to research success. In materials science, there are few examples of experimental databases that contain many different types of information, and compared with other disciplines, the database sizes are relatively small. Underlying these issues are the challenges in managing and linking data across disparate synthesis and characterization experiments, which we address with the development of a lightweight data management framework that is generally applicable for experimental science and beyond. Five years of managing experiments with this system has yielded the Materials Experiment and Analysis Database (MEAD) that contains raw data and metadata from millions of materials synthesis and characterization experiments, as well as the analysis and distillation of that data into property and performance metrics via software in an accompanying open source repository. The unprecedented quantity and diversity of experimental data are searchable by experiment and analysis attributes generated by both researchers and data processing software. The search web interface allows users to visualize their search results and download zipped packages of data with full annotations of their lineage. The enormity of the data provides substantial challenges and opportunities for incorporating data science in the physical sciences, and MEAD’s data and algorithm management framework will foster increased incorporation of automation and autonomous discovery in materials and chemistry research.

title: Developing employability in engineering education: a systematic review of the literature
abstract: This systematic review examines the international research literature from 2007 to 2017 to identify curricular and pedagogical arrangements that promote employability among engineering graduates. Guided by a theoretical framework distinguishing between engineering knowledge and professional skills, the review synthesizes evidence on how these elements are prioritized and integrated within engineering education. Findings reveal an interdependent relationship between technical expertise and professional competencies such as communication, teamwork, and project management, highlighting the necessity of both for addressing complex real-world engineering challenges. The review underscores the importance of curricular reforms that balance disciplinary knowledge with the development of soft skills, offering principled recommendations for educators seeking to enhance graduate employability in a rapidly evolving global context.

title: The Economics and Politics of Women's Rights
abstract: This paper surveys the relationship between women’s legal rights, economic development, and political change, emphasizing both historical and contemporary perspectives. The authors document a strong correlation between women’s rights and economic development across countries, noting that legal gender equality lags in developing nations. They review evidence showing that expanded rights for women—particularly in property ownership, political participation, and bodily autonomy—lead to increased investments in health, education, and children’s welfare, which in turn foster economic growth. The paper also examines the political economy of women’s rights, highlighting how technological change and shifts in the demand for human capital have altered men’s incentives to support gender equality. Theoretical models suggest a feedback loop wherein economic development and the expansion of women’s rights mutually reinforce each other. The analysis concludes that causality runs in both directions: development can promote gender equality, while women’s rights can accelerate development.

title: A hybrid learning pedagogy for surmounting the challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic in the performing arts education
abstract: For performing arts education, Sage on the stage and Learn from the Masters were halted by the COVID-19 pandemic, and so did everything else. All lectures, tutorials and other face-to-face skill-based training sections were cancelled and were replaced by the online model. Such a model was only seen as one of the supplementary components for performing arts education in the past. From January 2020, this online pedagogy was inevitably placed to surmount the challenges caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. The social distancing measures demanded the blended pedagogy into a new online approach, in which the traditional face-to-face teaching to be replaced by synchronous online learning (facilitated by technologies such as Zoom, Cisco Webex, Google Class, Panopto etc.). Meanwhile, to offer opportunities for cognitive participation which allows students to process the learning and be reflective, webinar and innovative performance projects were launched from the concept of ‘flipped classroom and outcome-based education.’ This mixed approach (blended learning, flipped classroom, and outcome-based education) is described as ‘hybrid learning’ in this study. The ‘hybrid learning’ pedagogy is implemented at the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts (HKAPA) for all teaching activities in the 2nd semester 2020/2021 to overcome the challenges caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. A questionnaire survey about how it affected the performing arts education, and how the new pedagogy was implemented took place in July 2020. The survey results from both the teachers (76) and students (163) share lessons, insights, and new understandings on teaching and learning online. Hybrid learning has been widely investigated and researched, yet study on hybrid learning in performing arts such as creative art, theatre art and music, remains insufficient. This study fills the research gap.
venue: Education and Information Technologies : Official Journal of the IFIP technical committee on Education

title: Machine Learning and Prediction in Medicine - Beyond the Peak of Inflated Expectations.
abstract: Machine learning and predictive analytics are heralded as transformative tools in medicine, promising to revolutionize clinical decision-making through the analysis of vast and diverse health data. However, this enthusiasm often overlooks critical limitations inherent in real-world data sources, including bias, confounding, and the rapid obsolescence of historical information. While machine learning can enhance risk stratification and diagnostic accuracy beyond traditional models, its predictive power is constrained by the quality and relevance of available data, as well as the inherent unpredictability of complex biological and social systems. Moreover, accurate prediction does not equate to actionable intervention, as many models identify associations rather than causal relationships amenable to change. The integration of machine learning with clinical expertise holds potential for improved resource allocation and patient outcomes, but expectations must be tempered by a realistic understanding of both the technology’s capabilities and its boundaries. Moving beyond inflated expectations requires a nuanced approach that leverages machine learning as a complement to human judgment, aiming for incremental improvements in care rather than unattainable perfection.

title: QM/MM: what have we learned, where are we, and where do we go from here?
abstract: This article reviews the development, current status, and future directions of combined quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) methods, which have become essential for modeling large, complex systems where both electronic structure changes and environmental effects are important. The paper examines the strengths and limitations of popular QM/MM approaches, with particular attention to boundary treatments such as link-atom methods and the handling of electrostatic interactions at the QM/MM interface. A detailed comparison is made between mechanical embedding, which treats inter-region interactions at the MM level, and electrostatic embedding, which incorporates the environment’s electrostatic influence directly into the QM Hamiltonian. The applicability of QM/MM methods across diverse fields—including organic, organometallic, biochemical, and solid-state chemistry—is discussed, along with recent benchmarking studies and available computational software. The review highlights ongoing challenges such as accurate boundary treatment and efficient coupling schemes, and suggests that future research should focus on more seamless integration of QM and MM descriptions to improve accuracy and broaden applicability.

title: The Condensed matter physics of QCD
abstract: Important progress in understanding the behavior of hadronic matter at high density has been achieved recently, by adapting the techniques of condensed matter theory. At asymptotic densities, the combination of asymptotic freedom and BCS theory make a rigorous analysis possible. New phases of matter with remarkable properties are predicted. They provide a theoretical laboratory within which chiral symmetry breaking and confinement can be studied at weak coupling. They may also play a role in the description of neutron star interiors. We discuss the phase diagram of QCD as a function of temperature and density, and close with a look at possible astrophysical signatures.

title: A procedure for evaluating environmental impact
abstract: Man cannot survive on this planet without utilizing its natural resources prudently. Every human action affects the world around us in some degree and the full effect is difficult to assess because of complex relations among living and nonliving things. Under the circumstances one can neither expect to restore the entire past nor preserve the entire present for future generations. However all can and should strive for proper balance between resource development and maintenance of pleasant surroundings. The Environmental Policy Act of 1969 and the reports on environmental assessment that i t requires are aimed at insuping such a balanced approach. To be effective we must provide a system for relating large numbers of actions and environmental factors and for placing value judgments on impacts which are difficult to quantify. A t my request the Geological Survey has developed an information matrix system that is described and modeled in this Circular. It is published with the thought that it will serve as a useful guide for environmental impact reporting and as a systematic reference. Those who share with us the desire to retain or improve the quality of our environment will recognize that this report is a sincere but still preliminary effort to fill an interim need. We hope that suggestions from others will improve this framework. PREAMBLE In a recent article in ' Science ' discussing the Environmental Policy Act of 1969, Gillette (1971) states ' The law's instructions for preparing an impact report apparently are not specific enough to insure that an agency will fully o r even usefully, examine the environmental effects of the projects i t plans. ' This report contains a procedure that may assist in developing uniform environmental impact statements. The Department of the Interior and the Council on Environmental Quality will appreciate comments on the procedure here proposed. The heart of the system is a matrix which is general enough to be used as a reference checklist o r a reminder of the full range of actions and impacts on the environment that may relate to proposed actions. The marked matrix also serves as a n abstract of the text of the environmental assessment to enable the many reviewers of impact reports to determine quickly what are considered to be the significant impacts and their relative importance a s evaluated by the origina. tors of the impact report. title: 2D materials for future heterogeneous electronics
abstract: Graphene and two-dimensional materials (2DM) remain an active field of research in science and engineering over 15 years after the first reports of 2DM. The vast amount of available data and the high performance of device demonstrators leave little doubt about the potential of 2DM for applications in electronics, photonics and sensing. So where are the integrated chips and enabled products? We try to answer this by summarizing the main challenges and opportunities that have thus far prevented 2DM applications. Graphene and related two-dimensional (2D) materials have remained an active field of research in science and engineering for over fifteen years. Here, the authors investigate why the transition from laboratories to fabrication plants appears to lag behind expectations, and summarize the main challenges and opportunities that have thus far prevented the commercialisation of these materials.

title: Engineering complex tissues.
abstract: Engineering complex tissues represents a significant challenge in tissue engineering, requiring the integration of biomaterial scaffolds, growth factors, and cell populations to restore native architecture and function. This paper summarizes key perspectives from leading researchers on strategies for regenerating complex oral, craniofacial, osseous, cartilage, and cardiovascular tissues. Advances discussed include the design of injectable scaffolds with appropriate mechanical and degradation properties, the importance of pre-vascularization for bone engineering, stem cell-based approaches for stratified cartilage, and novel solutions for tissue interfaces critical to tendon, ligament, and joint repair. The need for biomaterials that support selective cell adhesion and controlled growth factor delivery is emphasized, as is the development of biopreservation techniques to extend the viability of engineered grafts. Clinical considerations highlight the translation of these technologies into functional regenerative therapies. The article concludes that overcoming challenges related to vascularization, interface engineering, scaffold design, and preservation will be essential for the next generation of tissue engineering solutions targeting complex tissue structures.

title: Magnetars: the physics behind observations. A review
abstract: Magnetars are the strongest magnets in the present universe and the combination of extreme magnetic field, gravity and density makes them unique laboratories to probe current physical theories (from quantum electrodynamics to general relativity) in the strong field limit. Magnetars are observed as peculiar, burst–active x-ray pulsars, the anomalous x-ray pulsars (AXPs) and the soft gamma repeaters (SGRs); the latter emitted also three ‘giant flares’, extremely powerful events during which luminosities can reach up to 1047erg s−1 for about one second. The last five years have witnessed an explosion in magnetar research which has led, among other things, to the discovery of transient, or ‘outbursting’, and ‘low-field’ magnetars. Substantial progress has been made also on the theoretical side. Quite detailed models for explaining the magnetars’ persistent x-ray emission, the properties of the bursts, the flux evolution in transient sources have been developed and confronted with observations. New insight on neutron star asteroseismology has been gained through improved models of magnetar oscillations. The long-debated issue of magnetic field decay in neutron stars has been addressed, and its importance recognized in relation to the evolution of magnetars and to the links among magnetars and other families of isolated neutron stars. The aim of this paper is to present a comprehensive overview in which the observational results are discussed in the light of the most up-to-date theoretical models and their implications. This addresses not only the particular case of magnetar sources, but the more fundamental issue of how physics in strong magnetic fields can be constrained by the observations of these unique sources.
venue: Reports on progress in physics. Physical Society

title: Trans-Planckian problem of inflationary cosmology
abstract: The trans-Planckian problem in inflationary cosmology arises because, in standard inflationary models, modes corresponding to present-day cosmological structures originate with physical wavelengths smaller than the Planck length, where conventional field theory and general relativity are expected to break down. This paper investigates the sensitivity of inflationary predictions for the spectrum of cosmological fluctuations to assumptions about unknown super-Planckian physics by introducing modified dispersion relations for a scalar field in a de Sitter background. For dispersion relations of the type proposed by Unruh, the usual scale-invariant spectrum is preserved when the initial state minimizes energy density. However, for more radical modifications akin to those of Corley and Jacobson, significant deviations from scale invariance—including spectral tilt, exponential factors, and oscillatory features—can emerge. These results demonstrate that standard predictions of inflation are not robust against changes in trans-Planckian physics, highlighting the need for a deeper understanding of high-energy physics in early universe cosmology and raising important questions for attempts to unify fundamental interactions with cosmological models.

title: A Primer on Sediment-Trace Element Chemistry
abstract: This primer provides a comprehensive overview of the principles and methodologies underlying sediment-trace element chemistry, emphasizing the critical role of sediments in the transport, partitioning, and historical record of trace elements in aquatic environments. It details the physical and chemical factors influencing trace element associations with sediments, including grain size, surface area, mineralogy, and organic content, and discusses analytical approaches such as chemical partitioning and data normalization. The guide also addresses practical aspects of sediment sampling for both suspended and bed materials, highlighting considerations for spatial and temporal variability. By integrating foundational concepts with practical techniques, this resource serves as a self-teaching tool for environmental scientists seeking to understand sediment-associated trace element dynamics and their implications for water quality assessment and environmental monitoring.

title: Clinical practice parameters for hemodynamic support of pediatric and neonatal patients in septic shock*
abstract: The Institute of Medicine has called for the development of clinical guidelines and practice parameters to develop “best practice” and potentially improve patient outcome. ObjectiveTo provide American College of Critical Care Medicine clinical guidelines for hemodynamic support of neonates and children with septic shock. SettingIndividual members of the Society of Critical Care Medicine with special interest in neonatal and pediatric septic shock were identified from literature review and general solicitation at Society of Critical Care Medicine Educational and Scientific Symposia (1998–2001). MethodsThe MEDLINE literature database was searched with the following age-specific keywords: sepsis, septicemia, septic shock, endotoxemia, persistent pulmonary hypertension, nitric oxide, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. More than 30 experts graded literature and drafted specific recommendations by using a modified Delphi method. More than 30 more experts then reviewed the compiled recommendations. The task-force chairman modified the document until <10% of experts disagreed with the recommendations. ResultsOnly four randomized controlled trials in children with septic shock could be identified. None of these randomized trials led to a change in practice. Clinical practice has been based, for the most part, on physiologic experiments, case series, and cohort studies. Despite relatively low American College of Critical Care Medicine–graded evidence in the pediatric literature, outcomes in children have improved from 97% mortality in the 1960s to 60% in the 1980s and 9% mortality in 1999. U.S. hospital survival was three-fold better in children compared with adults (9% vs. 27% mortality) in 1999. Shock pathophysiology and response to therapies is age specific. For example, cardiac failure is a predominant cause of death in neonates and children, but vascular failure is a predominant cause of death in adults. Inotropes, vasodilators (children), inhaled nitric oxide (neonates), and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation can be more important contributors to survival in the pediatric populations, whereas vasopressors can be more important contributors to adult survival. ConclusionAmerican College of Critical Care Medicine adult guidelines for hemodynamic support of septic shock have little application to the management of pediatric or neonatal septic shock. Studies are required to determine whether American College of Critical Care Medicine guidelines for hemodynamic support of pediatric and neonatal septic shock will be implemented and associated with improved outcome.

title: QCD and strongly coupled gauge theories: challenges and perspectives
abstract: This review provides a comprehensive overview of the current status, recent progress, and ongoing challenges in Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and strongly coupled gauge theories, emphasizing their central role in understanding the strong interaction across a wide range of physical phenomena. The paper discusses the theoretical foundations of QCD, advances in experimental techniques, and the interplay between light and heavy quark dynamics, including hadron structure, spectroscopy, chiral dynamics, and precision observables. It explores the impact of QCD on searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model through precision measurements and computations, addresses the mapping of the QCD phase diagram and properties of deconfined matter such as the quark-gluon plasma, and highlights connections to broader fields including astrophysics, cosmology, and condensed matter physics. The review identifies key open questions in both theory and experiment, outlines methodological developments such as lattice QCD and effective field theories, and offers perspectives on future research directions that will further elucidate the complexities of strongly coupled gauge theories.
venue: European Physical Journal C: Particles and Fields

title: Information overload in the information age: a review of the literature from business administration, business psychology, and related disciplines with a bibliometric approach and framework development
abstract: In the light of the information age, information overload research in new areas (e.g., social media, virtual collaboration) rises rapidly in many fields of research in business administration with a variety of methods and subjects. This review article analyzes the development of information overload literature in business administration and related interdisciplinary fields and provides a comprehensive and overarching overview using a bibliometric literature analysis combined with a snowball sampling approach. For the last decade, this article reveals research directions and bridges of literature in a wide range of fields of business administration (e.g., accounting, finance, health management, human resources, innovation management, international management, information systems, marketing, manufacturing, or organizational science). This review article identifies the major papers of various research streams to capture the pulse of the information overload-related research and suggest new questions that could be addressed in the future and identifies concrete open gaps for further research. Furthermore, this article presents a new framework for structuring information overload issues which extends our understanding of influence factors and effects of information overload in the decision-making process.

title: New parton distributions for collider physics
abstract: We present new parton distribution functions (PDFs) for the proton, derived from a global analysis of hard scattering data within the general-mass framework of perturbative quantum chromodynamics. Incorporating recent theoretical improvements and the latest collider data—including deep-inelastic scattering, vector boson production, and single-inclusive jet production—we address tensions between high-precision DØ Run-II W lepton asymmetry data and certain fixed-target DIS measurements by providing two PDF sets: CT10, which excludes, and CT10W, which includes these asymmetry data with increased weight. Enhanced treatment of systematic uncertainties and more flexible PDF parametrizations improve both the fit quality and uncertainty estimates. We assess the impact of new experimental inputs, particularly the combined HERA-1 data, and evaluate the consistency of constraints from diverse experiments. The resulting PDFs are applied to predict key processes at the Fermilab Tevatron and CERN Large Hadron Collider, providing updated theoretical predictions and uncertainty estimates for collider phenomenology.

title: QM/MM: what have we learned, where are we, and where do we go from here?
abstract: This paper briefly reviews the current status of the most popular methods for combined quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) calculations, including their advantages and disadvantages. There is a special emphasis on very general link-atom methods and various ways to treat the charge near the boundary. Mechanical and electric embedding are contrasted. We consider methods applicable to gas-phase organic chemistry, liquid-phase organic and organometallic chemistry, biochemistry, and solid-state chemistry. Then we review some recent tests of QM/MM methods and summarize what we learn about QM/MM from these studies. We also discuss some available software. Finally, we present a few comments about future directions of research in this exciting area, where we focus on more intimate blends of QM with MM.

title: Pedagogies of embodiment in physical education – a literature review
