These observations constitute a demonstration of strain engineering the band structure in the emergent class of two-dimensional crystals, transition-metal dichalcogenides.

title: Year in review in Intensive Care Medicine 2012: III. Noninvasive ventilation, monitoring and patient–ventilator interactions, acute respiratory distress syndrome, sedation, paediatrics and miscellanea
abstract: This review summarizes key advances in intensive care medicine published in 2012, focusing on noninvasive ventilation (NIV), monitoring, patient–ventilator interactions, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), sedation, paediatrics, and related topics. Studies highlighted the predictors of NIV success and failure in acute respiratory failure, the benefits of neurally adjusted ventilatory assist for patient–ventilator synchrony, and the feasibility of early extubation followed by NIV in selected hypoxaemic patients. Research on pediatric NIV interfaces emphasized the importance of individualized mask selection based on age and disease. Bench studies addressed the need for standardized evaluation criteria for NIV equipment. Biomarker studies identified NT-proBNP as a predictor of post-extubation respiratory distress, supporting its role in guiding prophylactic NIV use. Advances in monitoring included ultrasonographic assessment of diaphragmatic function, noninvasive work of breathing prediction using neural networks, and validation of automated algorithms for detecting ineffective respiratory efforts. Technological innovations such as adaptive support ventilation and speaking valves were evaluated for safety and their impact on patient outcomes. Overall, these developments reflect ongoing efforts to optimize respiratory support, monitoring, and patient care strategies in the intensive care setting.

title: Parton physics on a Euclidean lattice.
abstract: I show that the parton physics related to correlations of quarks and gluons on the light cone can be studied through the matrix elements of frame-dependent, equal-time correlators in the large momentum limit. This observation allows practical calculations of parton properties on a Euclidean lattice. As an example, I demonstrate how to recover the leading-twist quark distribution by boosting an equal-time correlator to a large momentum.

title: Understanding leadership in the environmental sciences
abstract: Leadership is often assumed, intuitively, to be an important driver of sustainable development. To understand how leadership is conceptualized and analyzed in the environmental sciences and to discover what this research says about leadership outcomes, we conducted a review of environmental leadership research over the last 10 years. We found that much of the environmental leadership literature focuses on a few key individuals and desirable leadership competencies. The literature also reports that leadership is one of the most important of a number of factors contributing to effective environmental governance. Only a subset of the literature highlights interacting sources of leadership, disaggregates leadership outcomes, or evaluates leadership processes in detail. We argue that the literature on environmental leadership is highly normative. Leadership is typically depicted as an unequivocal good, and its importance is often asserted rather than tested. We trace how leadership studies in the management sciences are evolving and argue that, taking into account the state of the art in environmental leadership research, more critical approaches to leadership research in environmental science can be developed.

title: Multiferroic materials and magnetoelectric physics: symmetry, entanglement, excitation, and topology
abstract: This review provides a comprehensive and updated overview of multiferroic materials and magnetoelectric physics, emphasizing recent advances in the understanding of symmetry, entanglement, excitation, and topology. The article begins with a historical perspective and classification of multiferroics, highlighting representative materials such as BiFeO3 and TbMnO3. It systematically examines phenomenological approaches based on time-reversal and space-inversion symmetries, as well as the underlying mechanisms of magnetoelectric coupling in both single-phase materials and heterostructures. Key topics include spin-orbit and spin-lattice interactions, electromagnon excitations, domain structure dynamics, and interfacial effects in thin films. The review further explores emergent phenomena such as magnetic skyrmions, monopoles, and topological structures associated with magnetoelectricity. By integrating recent experimental and theoretical developments from the past six years, this work offers critical insights into the physical mechanisms driving multiferroicity and discusses future directions for novel materials discovery, new microscopic mechanisms, and potential device applications.

title: Higgs Boson studies at future particle colliders
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive assessment of the capabilities of proposed future particle colliders to advance Higgs boson studies beyond the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) program. Building on input from collider proponents for the European Strategy Update, the analysis systematically compares the projected performance of several collider concepts—including HE-LHC, FCC-ee, FCC-hh, CEPC, ILC, CLIC, and LHeC—using uniform methodologies. Key aspects examined include precision measurements of Higgs couplings to fermions and vector bosons within both the kappa framework and effective field theory approaches, sensitivity to rare and invisible Higgs decays, determination of the Higgs self-coupling, CP properties, mass, and total width. The study also considers theoretical uncertainties and explores the prospects for further improvements with advanced facilities such as muon colliders and multi-TeV electron-positron colliders. The results demonstrate that future colliders can significantly enhance our understanding of the Higgs sector, providing stringent tests of Standard Model predictions and offering powerful probes for new physics scenarios.

title: History of cannabis as a medicine: a review.
abstract: Cannabis has a long history of medicinal use, originating in Asia before the Christian era, particularly in India, where it was integral to both medical and religious practices. Its introduction into Western medicine occurred in the mid-19th century, reaching peak usage by the late 1800s through extracts and tinctures. However, medical use declined in the early 20th century due to inconsistent potency in plant material and challenges in standardization. Scientific interest was renewed after the identification of cannabis’ chemical constituents in 1965 and further intensified in the 1990s with the discovery of cannabinoid receptors and the endogenous cannabinoid system in the brain. These advances have led to a new era of research and more consistent therapeutic applications, as efficacy and safety of cannabis derivatives are increasingly supported by scientific evidence. This review traces the historical trajectory of cannabis as a medicine, highlighting its shifting roles across cultures and time periods, and underscores the recent resurgence of interest based on modern pharmacological discoveries.

title: Dipolar physics: a review of experiments with magnetic quantum gases
abstract: This review provides a comprehensive overview of experimental advances in the field of dipolar physics with magnetic quantum gases, focusing on ultracold atomic systems possessing large magnetic dipole moments. Since the realization of quantum degeneracy in chromium gases, highly magnetic atoms have enabled the exploration of novel phenomena arising from long-range and anisotropic dipole-dipole interactions. The unique electronic structure and strong magnetic moments of these atoms facilitate precise control over interatomic interactions via Feshbach resonances, enabling the study of both few- and many-body dipolar effects. Key experimental achievements include the observation of anisotropic scattering, stability and dynamics of fully polarized Bose and Fermi gases, the emergence of quantum-stabilized states such as self-bound droplets and supersolids, and the interplay between spin and motional degrees of freedom. The review also discusses the impact of dipolar interactions on spinor physics, low-dimensional systems, and lattice-confined gases, highlighting phenomena such as extended Hubbard and XYZ spin models. By surveying the rich landscape of experimental results, this work underscores the versatility of magnetic quantum gases as a platform for investigating strongly correlated matter, exotic quantum phases, and quantum simulation applications.
venue: Reports on progress in physics. Physical Society

title: Leverage points for improving global food security and the environment
abstract: How to optimize global food production Keeping societies stable and managing Earth's resources sustainably depend on doing a good, steady job producing and distributing food. West et al. asked what combinations of crops and regions offer the best chance of progress. Their analysis focused on reducing greenhouse gas emissions, nutrient pollution, water use, and food waste. They identify regions that are likely to yield the best balance between applying fertilizer to increase crop yields versus the resulting environmental impact. Science, this issue p. 325 A limited set of interventions could disproportionately improve crop production and environmental sustainability. Achieving sustainable global food security is one of humanity’s contemporary challenges. Here we present an analysis identifying key “global leverage points” that offer the best opportunities to improve both global food security and environmental sustainability. We find that a relatively small set of places and actions could provide enough new calories to meet the basic needs for more than 3 billion people, address many environmental impacts with global consequences, and focus food waste reduction on the commodities with the greatest impact on food security. These leverage points in the global food system can help guide how nongovernmental organizations, foundations, governments, citizens’ groups, and businesses prioritize actions.

title: Participatory medicine: a driving force for revolutionizing healthcare
abstract: Healthcare is undergoing a profound revolution as a consequence of three contemporary thrusts: systems medicine [1-4], big data and patient involvement in their own health through social networks. This convergence is leading to a medicine that is predictive, preventive, personalized and participatory (P4) [4-7]. The first three Ps, predictive, preventive and personalized, were delineated in the early 2000s [1,2], whereas the fourth P, participatory, was added later. To achieve a participatory healthcare system, major technical and societal challenges will need to be overcome, and this will require close integration with systems medicine and big data. Before commenting further on participatory medicine, let us first delineate the essence of systems medicine and big data and their implications for P4 medicine. Systems medicine, the application of systems biology approaches to disease [3,4,6,8,9], is already changing how healthcare is practiced (Table 1). We predict that in 5 to 10 years each patient will be surrounded by a virtual cloud of billions of data points - molecular, clinical chemistries, cellular, organ, phenotypic, imaging, social networks, and so on. We also predict that we will have the analytical tools to reduce this big data cloud to simple models that will guide improvements in health and minimize disease. This requires addressing two grand challenges: the signal-to-noise issues intrinsic to big data and integration of multi-scale data into predictive models. Table 1 How systems medicine is transforming healthcare In addition, for each individual patient we foresee that we will be able to integrate an individual’s genetic, molecular, cellular, organ and social networks into an overall 'network of networks’ [10]. Disease leads to the perturbation of the network of networks and this alters the information the network manages. The availability of a personal data cloud will allow one to characterize an individual’s network of networks in its normal or disease-perturbed states. This altered, disease-perturbed information will provide deep insights into disease mechanisms, new approaches to diagnostics and therapeutics, and a platform for participatory medicine.

title: Guidelines for conducting and reporting case study research in software engineering
abstract: Case study is a suitable research methodology for software engineering research since it studies contemporary phenomena in its natural context. However, the understanding of what constitutes a case study varies, and hence the quality of the resulting studies. This paper aims at providing an introduction to case study methodology and guidelines for researchers conducting case studies and readers studying reports of such studies. The content is based on the authors’ own experience from conducting and reading case studies. The terminology and guidelines are compiled from different methodology handbooks in other research domains, in particular social science and information systems, and adapted to the needs in software engineering. We present recommended practices for software engineering case studies as well as empirically derived and evaluated checklists for researchers and readers of case study research.

title: Expander Graphs and their Applications
abstract: This survey provides a comprehensive overview of expander graphs, emphasizing their fundamental role across mathematics and computer science. Expander graphs, characterized by their simultaneous sparsity and strong connectivity, are explored through combinatorial, probabilistic, and algebraic perspectives. The paper discusses structural properties, explicit constructions, and algorithmic aspects of expanders, highlighting their significance in diverse areas such as communication networks, error correcting codes, pseudorandomness, metric embeddings, Markov chain mixing, and complexity theory. Key topics include spectral graph theory, random walks, isoperimetric inequalities, extremal problems, explicit constructions like the Margulis and zig-zag products, Cayley graphs, and applications to coding theory and metric embedding. The survey synthesizes decades of research, illustrating the ubiquity and versatility of expander graphs while providing references for further study and outlining open problems in the field.

title: Nanoparticles and their applications in cell and molecular biology.
abstract: Nanoparticles can be engineered with distinctive composition, size, shape, and surface chemistry to enable novel techniques in a wide range of biological applications. The unique properties of nanoparticles and their behavior in biological milieu also enable exciting and integrative approaches to studying fundamental biological questions. This review will provide an overview of various types of nanoparticles and concepts of targeting nanoparticles. We will also discuss the advantages and recent applications of using nanoparticles as tools for drug delivery, imaging, sensing, and for the understanding of basic biological processes.

title: Computational cell biology
abstract: The complexity of biological systems has outpaced the capacity of traditional reductionist approaches in cell biology, necessitating new strategies to understand the interconnected and dynamic nature of cellular processes. This commentary highlights the transformative role of computational methods in cell biology, which now extend beyond supporting experimental tools to become essential for acquiring, analyzing, and interpreting large-scale data. Advances in computational image analysis, modeling, and systems biology are enabling unprecedented quantitative insights into cellular dynamics, interaction networks, and regulatory patterns. The Journal of Cell Biology recognizes this paradigm shift by presenting reviews and research exemplifying interdisciplinary computational approaches, aiming to foster collaboration between cell and computational biologists. Embracing computational cell biology promises to reveal novel concepts of cellular organization and function, broadening the scope of biological inquiry while maintaining molecular detail.

title: The Virtues and Vices of Equilibrium and the Future of Financial Economics
abstract: This paper critically examines the central role of equilibrium models in financial economics, highlighting both their strengths in providing parsimonious, structured explanations of market behavior and their inherent limitations in capturing complex, real-world phenomena. Drawing on perspectives from both economics and physics, the authors discuss the foundational assumptions of equilibrium theory—such as rational expectations, market clearing, and agent optimization—and assess their empirical validity. While equilibrium models have been instrumental in shaping economic thought and practice, especially in contexts like risk management and arbitrage, the paper argues that their predictive power is often constrained by unrealistic assumptions about agent rationality and information. The authors review empirical evidence for and against equilibrium approaches and illustrate cases where non-equilibrium dynamics—such as power laws, market crises, and heterogeneous agent interactions—are more relevant. The paper advocates for a pluralistic approach to financial economics, integrating alternative methodologies including agent-based modeling, behavioral finance, bounded rationality, and insights from biology and complex systems. Ultimately, the authors call for an empirically grounded reassessment of equilibrium’s place in economic theory and encourage the development of models that better reflect the adaptive, evolving nature of real financial markets.

title: Strain engineering of graphene's electronic structure.
abstract: We explore the influence of local strain on the electronic structure of graphene. We show that strain can be easily tailored to generate electron beam collimation, 1D channels, surface states, and confinement. These can be seen as basic elements for all-graphene electronics which, by suitable engineering of local strain profiles, could be integrated on a single graphene sheet. In addition this proposal has the advantage that patterning can be made on substrates rather than on graphene, thereby protecting the integrity of the latter.

title: Environmental DNA for biomonitoring
abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has rapidly transformed biomonitoring by enabling high-resolution, cost-effective biodiversity assessments across diverse ecosystems. Over the past decade, advances in high-throughput sequencing and analytical methods, including machine learning and taxonomy-free approaches, have expanded the scope of eDNA applications from single-species detection to comprehensive community analyses and environmental impact assessments. Despite these technological breakthroughs, routine implementation of eDNA-based biomonitoring remains limited due to challenges in standardization, legislative integration, and reconciling discrepancies with traditional methods. This special issue of Molecular Ecology presents 29 papers that address methodological innovations, particularly in the use of novel bioindicators and analytical tools, with a focus on fish eDNA surveys and the integration of environmental genomics for ecosystem diagnostics. The collection highlights both the strengths and limitations of current eDNA approaches, emphasizing the need for further development in calibration, reference databases, and regulatory frameworks to fully realize the potential of eDNA in routine biomonitoring.

title: Handbook of freshwater fishery biology
abstract: These volumes have, for over 30 years, been the most readily available source listing the scattered articles, theses, bulletins, and research on freshwater fish in the United States and Canada. 'The Handbook of Freshwater Fishery Biology' summarizes the available data on age, growth, length weight, fecundity, reproductive behavior feeding habits, and necessary environment for each freshwater species. The comparison of species is presented in a manner easily used by fishery mangers and biologists.

title: Hadronic molecules
abstract: A large number of experimental discoveries especially in the heavy quarkonium sector that did not at all fit to the expectations of the until then very successful quark model led to a renaissance of hadron spectroscopy. Among various explanations of the internal structure of these excitations, hadronic molecules, being analogues of light nuclei, play a unique role since for those predictions can be made with controlled uncertainty. We review experimental evidences of various candidates of hadronic molecules, and methods of identifying such structures. Nonrelativistic effective field theories are the suitable framework for studying hadronic molecules, and are discussed in both the continuum and finite volumes. Also pertinent lattice QCD results are presented. Further, we discuss the production mechanisms and decays of hadronic molecules, and comment on the reliability of certain assertions often made in the literature.

title: MatSciBERT: A materials domain language model for text mining and information extraction
abstract: We present MatSciBERT, a domain-specific language model designed for materials science text mining and information extraction. Trained on a curated corpus of approximately 150,000 peer-reviewed materials science publications spanning diverse subfields, MatSciBERT leverages domain-adaptive pre-training to capture the unique terminology and context of materials literature. We evaluate MatSciBERT on three key downstream tasks—named entity recognition, relation classification, and abstract classification—demonstrating significant performance improvements over SciBERT and establishing new state-of-the-art results in the domain. By making the pre-trained model and associated resources publicly available, our work addresses the lack of specialized language models for materials science and enables automated knowledge extraction to accelerate research and discovery in the field.

title: Patterns of New Physics in b → sℓ+ℓ− transitions in the light of recent data
abstract: In the Standard Model (SM), the rare transitions where a bottom quark decays into a strange quark and a pair of light leptons exhibit a potential sensitivity to physics beyond the SM. In addition, the SM embeds Lepton Flavour Universality (LFU), leading to almost identical probabilities for muon and electron modes. The LHCb collaboration discovered a set of deviations from the SM expectations in decays to muons and also in ratios assessing LFU. Other experiments (Belle, ATLAS, CMS) found consistent measurements, albeit with large error bars. We perform a global fit to all available b → sℓ+ℓ− data (ℓ = e, μ) in a model-independent way allowing for different patterns of New Physics. For the first time, the NP hypothesis is preferred over the SM by 5 σ in a general case when NP can enter SM-like operators and their chirally-flipped partners. LFU violation is favoured with respect to LFU at the 3-4 σ level. We discuss the impact of LFU-violating New Physics on the observable P5′ from B → K∗μ+μ− and we compare our estimate for long-distance charm contributions with an empirical model recently proposed by a group of LHCb experimentalists. Finally, we discuss NP models able to describe this consistent pattern of deviations.

title: Theory-Guided Machine Learning in Materials Science
abstract: Materials scientists are increasingly adopting the use of machine learning tools to discover hidden trends in data and make predictions. Applying concepts from data science without foreknowledge of their limitations and the unique qualities of materials data, however, could lead to errant conclusions. The differences that exist between various kinds of experimental and calculated data require careful choices of data processing and machine learning methods. Here, we outline potential pitfalls involved in using machine learning without robust protocols. We address some problems of overfitting to training data using decision trees as an example, rational descriptor selection in the field of perovskites, and preserving physical interpretability in the application of dimensionality reducing techniques such as principal component analysis. We show how proceeding without the guidance of domain knowledge can lead to both quantitatively and qualitatively incorrect predictive models.

title: The Evolution of the Corporate Social Performance Model
abstract: This paper examines the historical development and conceptual refinement of the corporate social performance (CSP) model, highlighting its evolution through scholarly debate on corporate social responsibility (CSR). By analyzing three major challenges—economic responsibility, public responsibility, and social responsiveness—the authors demonstrate how the CSP model integrates these perspectives into a multidimensional framework that encompasses principles of responsibility, processes of responsiveness, and policies for managing social issues. The paper argues that this integrative approach addresses critiques of CSR by recognizing both economic imperatives and societal expectations, positioning CSP as a valuable analytical tool for understanding the dynamic relationship between business and society. Ultimately, the CSP model is presented as a foundational paradigm for future research in business and society, reflecting the ongoing negotiation between corporate obligations and evolving societal values.

title: Simulation Modeling and Analysis
abstract: From the Publisher: This second edition of Simulation Modeling and Analysis includes a chapter on 'Simulation in Manufacturing Systems' and examples. The text is designed for a one-term or two-quarter course in simulation offered in departments of industrial engineering,business,computer science and operations research.

title: Blockchain for Supply Chain Traceability: Business Requirements and Critical Success Factors
abstract: We seek to guide operations management (OM) research on the implementation of supply chain traceability systems by identifying business requirements and the factors critical to successful implementation. We first motivate the need for implementing traceability systems in two very different industries—cobalt mining and pharmaceuticals—and present business requirements and critical success factors for implementation. Next, we describe how we carried out thematic analysis of practitioner and scholarly articles on implementing blockchain for supply chain traceability. Finally, we present our results pertaining to the needs of different stakeholders such as suppliers, consumers, and regulators. The business requirements for traceability systems are curbing illegal practices; improving sustainability performance; increasing operational efficiency; enhancing supply‐chain coordination; and sensing market trends. Critical success factors for implementation are companies’ capabilities; collaboration; technology maturity; supply chain practices; leadership; and governance of the traceability efforts. These findings provide a nascent measurement model for empirical work and a foundation for descriptive and normative research on blockchain applications for supply chain traceability.

title: Applying educational theory to develop a framework to support the delivery of experiential entrepreneurship education
abstract: This paper addresses the need for a stronger theoretical foundation in experiential entrepreneurship education by developing a framework that integrates key educational theories and philosophies. Drawing on constructivism, objectivism, Kolb’s experiential learning theory, Schön’s reflection-in-action, and Mezirow’s transformative learning, the authors propose a three-stage framework to guide educators in further and higher education. The framework clarifies the roles of both educators and learners within experiential entrepreneurship education, supporting pedagogical competence and enhancing the quality and legitimacy of educational practice. By bridging the gap between educational theory and pedagogic practice, this research offers practical guidance for educators seeking to maximize the effectiveness of experiential approaches and responds to calls in the literature for closer engagement with foundational educational theory in entrepreneurship education.

title: Simulation Modeling and Analysis
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive examination of simulation modeling and analysis, emphasizing discrete-event simulation and its application to complex systems. It systematically introduces fundamental concepts, including systems, models, time-advance mechanisms, and the organization of simulation models, supported by practical examples such as queueing and inventory systems. The text explores simulation software, comparing general-purpose and specialized languages, and discusses essential statistical foundations relevant to simulation output analysis. Key topics include model validation and verification, selection of input probability distributions, random number and variate generation, and advanced output data analysis techniques for both terminating and steady-state simulations. The work further addresses methods for comparing alternative system configurations, variance-reduction techniques, experimental design, and optimization within simulation studies. Special attention is given to the simulation of manufacturing systems, highlighting software tools, modeling of system randomness, case studies, and practical implementation issues. Through theoretical exposition and illustrative programming examples in multiple languages, the paper serves as a foundational resource for both the methodology and practice of simulation modeling in operations research and management science.

title: Technology and Economic Theory
abstract: This paper explores the complex relationship between technology and economic theory, emphasizing the central role of technological change in shaping economic growth, competition, and the structure of firms. It critically examines how economists conceptualize technology, highlighting the limitations of traditional production function approaches that treat technology as an unexplained constraint or a simple menu of inputs and outputs. Drawing on historical perspectives from Smith, Marshall, and Schumpeter, as well as modern evolutionary economics, the paper argues that technology is inseparable from human agency and organizational structures. It advocates for a broader understanding of technology that encompasses not only codified knowledge and physical artifacts but also the organization and management of production systems. By analyzing the architecture of technological systems and the division of labor, the paper situates its discussion within both classical and contemporary traditions, ultimately calling for a more nuanced integration of technological complexity into economic theory.

title: Sulfur Containing Scaffolds in Drugs: Synthesis and Application in Medicinal Chemistry.
abstract: Sulfur-containing scaffolds are integral to a wide array of pharmaceuticals, with sulfonamides, thioethers, sulfones, and penicillins representing the most prevalent motifs in FDA-approved drugs. This review highlights the historical and contemporary significance of these sulfur-based structures in medicinal chemistry, emphasizing their diverse biological activities and therapeutic applications. Recent advances in synthetic methodologies are discussed, including traditional and emerging approaches such as flow chemistry, metal-catalyzed couplings, sulfur dioxide fixation using DABSO, and green protocols that enhance efficiency and substrate scope. The synthesis of sulfonamides has particularly benefited from innovations enabling milder conditions, broader functional group tolerance, and scalability. Thioether formation has also evolved through the development of palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions. Collectively, these advances not only facilitate the construction of sulfur-containing drug candidates but also support ongoing drug discovery and development efforts by providing practical, sustainable, and versatile synthetic routes.

title: Fat-Tailed Uncertainty in the Economics of Catastrophic Climate Change
abstract: This paper examines the profound implications of fat-tailed uncertainty for the economics of catastrophic climate change, arguing that deep structural uncertainty and the potential for extreme, low-probability, high-impact events fundamentally challenge standard benefit-cost analyses. Through intuitive empirical examples and theoretical discussion, the paper demonstrates that conventional economic models often underestimate or inadequately represent the risks associated with unprecedented increases in greenhouse gases and uncertain climate sensitivity. The analysis highlights how standard approaches may fail to capture the full scope of potential damages, particularly in the tails of probability distributions where catastrophic outcomes reside. The author contends that these uncertainties necessitate a more robust integration of fat-tailed risk into climate policy analysis, as ignoring them can lead to dangerously incomplete or misleading conclusions about optimal climate action.
venue: Review of Environmental Economics and Policy

title: Modelling Asymmetric Exchange Rate Dependence
abstract: This paper investigates the presence of asymmetric dependence between the Deutsche mark–U.S. dollar and Japanese yen–U.S. dollar exchange rates, focusing on whether their correlation differs during joint appreciations versus joint depreciations against the U.S. dollar. Extending copula theory to incorporate conditioning variables, the study develops flexible models for the conditional dependence structure of these exchange rates using daily data from 1991 to 2001. The results reveal that the mark–dollar and yen–dollar rates are more strongly correlated during joint depreciations than appreciations, consistent with theories of asymmetric central bank intervention and portfolio rebalancing. The analysis also identifies a significant structural break in dependence following the introduction of the euro in 1999, with a notable decline in correlation and a reversal in asymmetry. The paper demonstrates that conditional copulas provide a powerful framework for modeling time-varying, asymmetric dependence in exchange rates, offering important implications for risk management and financial modeling.

title: Scientific collaboration networks. II. Shortest paths, weighted networks, and centrality.
abstract: This paper presents a quantitative analysis of scientific collaboration networks constructed from large-scale bibliographic databases in physics, biomedical research, and computer science. By modeling scientists as nodes and coauthorships as links, we examine key structural properties including the distribution of collaborators, typical shortest paths between scientists, and measures of centrality such as closeness and betweenness. Recognizing that traditional unweighted network representations fail to capture the varying strengths of collaborative ties, we introduce a weighted approach based on the number of coauthored papers and shared collaborators. Our results reveal that scientific collaboration networks are characterized by short average path lengths and highly connected individuals, with significant variation across disciplines. We discuss methods for identifying the most central or best-connected scientists and highlight the implications of network structure for information flow and scientific influence within research communities.
venue: Physical review. E, Statistical, nonlinear, and soft matter physics

title: A dynamic capabilities-based entrepreneurial theory of the multinational enterprise
abstract: This paper develops a dynamic capabilities-based theory of the multinational enterprise (MNE). It first reviews scholarship on the MNE, with a focus on what has come to be known as “internalization” theory. One prong of this theory develops contractual/transaction cost-informed governance perspectives; and another develops technology transfer and capabilities perspectives. In this paper, it is suggested that the latter has been somewhat neglected. However, if fully integrated as part of a more complete approach, it can buttress transaction cost/governance issues and expand the range of phenomena that can be explained. In this more integrated framework, dynamic capabilities coupled with good strategy are seen as necessary to sustain superior enterprise performance, especially in fast-moving global environments. Entrepreneurial management and transformational leadership are incorporated into a capabilities theory of the MNE. The framework is then used to explain how strategy and dynamic capabilities together determine firm-level sustained competitive advantage in global environments. It is suggested that this framework complements contract-based perspectives on the MNE and can help integrate international management and international business perspectives.

title: Boundary crossing pedagogy in STEM education
abstract: This commentary aims to discuss an overarching boundary crossing framework under which integrated STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics) pedagogy can be conceptualized. Four potential learning dialogical processes for boundary crossing are presented and used as the main theoretical construct for the discussion. A proposal of an interactive pedagogical framework is put forward accompanied by a provisional statement to relate the connective factors that are critical in the formation of a boundary crossing STEM pedagogy. These factors are situated learning, communities of practices, problem solving, learning dialogical processes, and boundary objects. A Hong Kong school STEM case is employed to illustrate the applicability of this framework. The commentary ends with a reflective remark on boundary crossing STEM pedagogy.

title: Freshwater crayfish :: biology, management and exploitation
abstract: This comprehensive volume provides an in-depth examination of freshwater crayfish, encompassing their biology, management, and exploitation. The book is organized into two main sections: general biology and species of economic importance. The first section addresses key aspects of crayfish morphology, distribution, evolution, growth, reproduction, ecology, feeding habits, disease, and immune mechanisms. The second section focuses on economically significant genera and species across North America, Europe, and Australia, detailing their production methods, distribution patterns, and associated challenges. Contributions from leading experts offer insights into adaptive radiation, interspecies interactions, and the impact of introduced species on native populations. By integrating fundamental biological knowledge with practical management strategies, this work serves as a valuable resource for researchers, aquaculturists, and policymakers involved in the conservation and sustainable use of freshwater crayfish.

title: Finding communities in linear time: a physics approach
abstract: We introduce a novel physics-inspired algorithm for community detection in large graphs that operates in linear time with respect to the number of nodes and edges. By modeling the network as an electrical circuit and applying voltage drops between selected nodes, our method identifies communities based on the resulting voltage distribution, circumventing the need for computationally expensive edge-cutting or matrix inversion techniques. This approach enables efficient identification of both global community structures and local communities surrounding specific nodes without full graph partitioning. We demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of our algorithm on benchmark datasets, including social and communication networks, and discuss its advantages over traditional methods in terms of speed, accuracy, and applicability to weighted graphs.

title: Search for New Physics with Atoms and Molecules
abstract: Advances in atomic physics, such as cooling and trapping of atoms and molecules and developments in frequency metrology, have added orders of magnitude to the precision of atom-based clocks and sensors. Applications extend beyond atomic physics and this article reviews using these new techniques to address important challenges in physics and to look for variations in the fundamental constants, search for interactions beyond the standard model of particle physics, and test the principles of general relativity.

title: Exploring transparency: a new framework for responsible business management
abstract: This paper critically examines the concept of transparency in business management by conducting a systematic literature review to address inconsistencies and ambiguities in existing definitions. The authors synthesize prior research to propose a comprehensive definition of transparency as the extent to which stakeholders perceive an organization provides learning opportunities about itself. Building on this definition, the study introduces a new conceptual framework that identifies when transparency is most critical, outlines organizational strategies for enhancing transparency, and highlights its potential benefits, particularly in fostering trust and ethical decision making. The framework serves as both a practical guide for organizations seeking to embed transparency as a core value and a foundation for developing universal codes of conduct. Additionally, the paper contributes methodological insights for evaluating construct definitions, thereby advancing empirical research on transparency and responsible business management.

title: Quantum computational advantage using photons
abstract: We report the experimental demonstration of quantum computational advantage using Gaussian boson sampling with photons. By generating 50 high-purity, highly indistinguishable single-mode squeezed states and injecting them into a 100-mode ultralow-loss, fully connected interferometer, we achieve sampling with up to 76 detected photon clicks. The system is phase-locked to maintain coherence across all photon number superpositions and utilizes 100 high-efficiency single-photon detectors. The resulting output state space reaches a dimension of approximately 10^30, and the sampling rate exceeds that of the best known classical simulation strategies and supercomputers by a factor of about 10^14. Rigorous validation against alternative hypotheses—including thermal states, distinguishable photons, and uniform distributions—confirms the quantum nature of the sampling process. Our results establish a clear quantum computational advantage in photonic systems and provide strong evidence against the Extended Church-Turing thesis by demonstrating a task intractable for classical computation with current technology.

title: Emotion, rationality, and decision-making: how to link affective and social neuroscience with social theory
abstract: This paper advocates for a deeper integration between affective and social neuroscience and social theory, arguing that each field can significantly enhance the other. The authors review key findings from neuroscience that challenge core assumptions in influential social theories such as rational choice theory, behavioral economics, and post-structuralism, highlighting inconsistencies regarding human cognition, emotion, and decision-making. In contrast, plural rationality theory is shown to align more closely with neuroscientific evidence. The paper also demonstrates how social theories can refine neuroscientific models by providing precise definitions of social phenomena, raising awareness of cultural biases, and generating new hypotheses. Using plural rationality theory and the somatic marker hypothesis as an example, the authors illustrate how interdisciplinary collaboration can yield more comprehensive models of social evaluation in the brain. The review concludes by emphasizing the mutual benefits of merging social theory with affective and social neuroscience to advance understanding of emotion, rationality, and decision-making.

title: A History of Archaeological Thought
abstract: A History of Archaeological Thought is an intermediate level course intended to introduce students to the development of archaeological theory from the early 19 th century realization that the remote past could be reconstructed solely on the basis of the archaeological record to later developments, such as attempts to identify ethnic/linguistic groups exclusively from material remains. It will trace the emergence of archaeology as a sub-field within anthropology and its continuing close interaction with broader developments in anthropological theory. The course contrasts perspectives that emphasize internal social evolution and adaptation to local environmental settings with post-modern responses that stress multiple perspectives on a contingent past. Students will be introduced to different theoretical approaches to interpreting the archaeological record, such as cultural ecology and neo-evolutionary processual archaeology, archaeologies of identity and place and landscape, Marxist historical materialism and world systems theory, and so-called symbolic/cognitive archaeology. This course reviews different theoretical approaches for explaining the past, emphasizing the positive interaction between accumulating archaeological discoveries and their interpretation and analysis. Social theories, originally formulated in sociology and social anthropology, are evaluated for their adequacy in understanding the material culture record of archaeology. The suitability of these theoretical approaches for interpreting the archaeological record will be critically examined.

title: Bladder cancer, a review of the environmental risk factors
abstract: This review systematically examines the environmental risk factors associated with bladder cancer, focusing on epidemiological evidence from studies published between 1998 and 2010. The analysis identifies cigarette smoking as the primary risk factor, with current smokers exhibiting a threefold increased risk compared to non-smokers, and highlights additional risks from other forms of tobacco use, including cigars, pipes, and environmental tobacco smoke. Occupational exposure to aromatic amines—such as 2-naphthylamine, 4-aminobiphenyl, benzidine, and 4,4’-methylenebis(2-chloroaniline)—commonly found in chemical, dye, and rubber industries, as well as in hair dyes and other products, is strongly linked to bladder cancer. Exposure to arsenic in drinking water at concentrations above 300 µg/l is also associated with elevated risk, with some evidence suggesting synergistic effects with smoking and nutritional factors even at lower concentrations. The review underscores the multifactorial nature of bladder cancer etiology and emphasizes the importance of reducing exposure to these environmental carcinogens to mitigate disease incidence.

title: Review of collagen I hydrogels for bioengineered tissue microenvironments: characterization of mechanics, structure, and transport.
abstract: Type I collagen hydrogels are widely used as three-dimensional scaffolds in tissue engineering due to their biocompatibility and structural similarity to native extracellular matrix; however, variability in fabrication protocols and characterization methods has led to inconsistent data across studies, limiting their utility as standardized tissue mimics. This review systematically examines the parameter space of collagen I hydrogel fabrication—including source, solubilization method, polymerization conditions, and concentration—and correlates these with key hydrogel properties such as mechanics, structure, and transport. By surveying over 50 research articles, the review highlights significant gaps in the literature, particularly regarding comprehensive multidimensional characterization and standardization of protocols. The discussion emphasizes how fabrication parameters influence hydrogel properties relevant to cellular behavior and tissue function, identifies the most commonly used methods and their limitations, and proposes future directions for more effective characterization. Ultimately, this review serves as a resource for researchers seeking to optimize collagen I hydrogels for bioengineered tissue microenvironments by guiding the selection of fabrication parameters and characterization methodologies.

title: The Cosmopolitan Imagination: The Renewal of Critical Social Theory
abstract: Gerard Delanty provides a comprehensive assessment of the idea of cosmopolitanism in social and political thought which links cosmopolitan theory with critical social theory. He argues that cosmopolitanism has a critical dimension which offers a solution to one of the weaknesses in the critical theory tradition: failure to respond to the challenges of globalization and intercultural communication. Critical cosmopolitanism, he proposes, is an approach that is not only relevant to social scientific analysis but also normatively grounded in a critical attitude. Delanty's argument for a critical, sociologically oriented cosmopolitanism aims to avoid, on the one hand, purely normative conceptions of cosmopolitanism and, on the other, approaches that reduce cosmopolitanism to the empirical expression of diversity. He attempts to take cosmopolitan theory beyond the largely Western context with which it has generally been associated, claiming that cosmopolitan analysis must now take into account non-Western expressions of cosmopolitanism.

title: Deep materials informatics: Applications of deep learning in materials science
abstract: The growing application of data-driven analytics in materials science has led to the rise of materials informatics. Within the arena of data analytics, deep learning has emerged as a game-changing technique in the last few years, enabling numerous real-world applications, such as self-driving cars. In this paper, the authors present an overview of deep learning, its advantages, challenges, and recent applications on different types of materials data. The increasingly availability of materials databases and big data in general, along with groundbreaking advances in deep learning offers a lot of promise to accelerate the discovery, design, and deployment of next-generation materials.

title: The role of digitalization in business and management: a systematic literature review
abstract: This paper presents a systematic literature review of digitalization in business and management, focusing on the mature functional areas of management, marketing, and finance and accounting. Analyzing 119 review articles published between 2018 and April 2022, the study identifies key trends such as the impact of digital technologies on consumer behavior analysis, the integration of digitalization with green innovation, and the application of blockchain in financial services. The review synthesizes current knowledge within an integrated framework, clarifies the complexity of digitalization, and establishes connections with established literature in core business disciplines. By highlighting research gaps and future agendas, this work offers a comprehensive and up-to-date perspective on digitalization’s transformative role in organizations, providing valuable insights for scholars and practitioners seeking to navigate ongoing digital transformation.

title: Black hole chemistry: thermodynamics with Lambda
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive review of black hole thermodynamics in extended phase space, where the cosmological constant is treated as a thermodynamic pressure and its conjugate variable as a thermodynamic volume. By reinterpreting the black hole mass as enthalpy rather than internal energy, an enriched thermodynamic framework emerges, leading to new insights such as the reverse isoperimetric inequality and the identification of novel phase transitions analogous to those in conventional chemistry, including Van der Waals fluids, reentrant phase transitions, and triple points. The review also discusses the extension of the AdS/CFT correspondence in this context, connections with horizon thermodynamics, applications to Lifshitz spacetimes, and possible future directions. This approach, termed black hole chemistry, reveals deep analogies between black holes and everyday thermodynamic systems and opens new avenues for understanding gravity, quantum theory, and holography.

title: From telecollaboration to virtual exchange: state-of-the‑art and the role of UNICollaboration in moving forward
abstract: This article examines the evolution of telecollaboration, now increasingly termed virtual exchange, as a pedagogically structured approach to online intercultural interaction and collaboration in education. It provides a comprehensive overview of the diverse models and terminologies that have emerged across disciplines, highlighting both the adaptability and challenges resulting from this heterogeneity. The paper traces the historical development of virtual exchange, analyzes key trends and barriers to broader implementation, and discusses the need for unified terminology to facilitate understanding and dissemination among educators and policymakers. The role of the UNICollaboration organization is explored as a cross-disciplinary platform aimed at consolidating research, fostering collaboration, and advancing the field of virtual exchange in higher education. The article concludes by emphasizing the importance of interdisciplinary approaches and coordinated efforts to address ongoing challenges and maximize the educational benefits of virtual exchange initiatives.

title: Components of Environmental Literacy in Elementary Science Education Curriculum in Bulgaria and Turkey.
abstract: The purpose of this study was to analyze the extent to which science education objectives in elementary schools addressed to the six basic components of environmental literacy (EL), and how this attention differed from Bulgaria to Turkey. The main method in the study involved comparative content analysis of these objectives. The courses sampled for Bulgaria include “The Human Being and Nature”, “Biology and Health Education”, “Chemistry and Environmental Protection” and “Physics and Astronomy”. The course sampled for Turkey is “Science and Technology Education”. Content analysis of these objectives reveals that all components of environmental literacy did not receive the same attention. For example in both countries most attention was given to knowledge, less to skills and attitudes, and little to environmentally responsible behavior (ERB).

title: CellProfiler 3.0: Next-generation image processing for biology
abstract: CellProfiler has enabled the scientific research community to create flexible, modular image analysis pipelines since its release in 2005. Here, we describe CellProfiler 3.0, a new version of the software supporting both whole-volume and plane-wise analysis of three-dimensional (3D) image stacks, increasingly common in biomedical research. CellProfiler’s infrastructure is greatly improved, and we provide a protocol for cloud-based, large-scale image processing. New plugins enable running pretrained deep learning models on images. Designed by and for biologists, CellProfiler equips researchers with powerful computational tools via a well-documented user interface, empowering biologists in all fields to create quantitative, reproducible image analysis workflows.

title: Definition of Health 2.0 and Medicine 2.0: A Systematic Review
abstract: During the last decade, the Internet has become increasingly popular and is now an important part of our daily life. When new “Web 2.0” technologies are used in health care, the terms “Health 2.0' or 'Medicine 2.0” may be used. Objective The objective was to identify unique definitions of Health 2.0/Medicine 2.0 and recurrent topics within the definitions. Methods A systematic literature review of electronic databases (PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL) and gray literature on the Internet using the search engines Google, Bing, and Yahoo was performed to find unique definitions of Health 2.0/Medicine 2.0. We assessed all literature, extracted unique definitions, and selected recurrent topics by using the constant comparison method. Results We found a total of 1937 articles, 533 in scientific databases and 1404 in the gray literature. We selected 46 unique definitions for further analysis and identified 7 main topics. Conclusions Health 2.0/Medicine 2.0 are still developing areas. Many articles concerning this subject were found, primarily on the Internet. However, there is still no general consensus regarding the definition of Health 2.0/Medicine 2.0. We hope that this study will contribute to building the concept of Health 2.0/Medicine 2.0 and facilitate discussion and further research.

title: The One Health Concept: 10 Years Old and a Long Road Ahead
abstract: Over the past decade, the One Health concept has emerged as a holistic, transdisciplinary approach to address the growing complexity of global health challenges at the human–animal–ecosystem interface. This review examines the evolution and current limitations of One Health, highlighting its initial focus on zoonotic diseases and the relative neglect of ecosystem health and non-communicable diseases. The increasing incidence of infectious outbreaks, antimicrobial resistance, environmental pollution, and chronic multifactorial diseases underscores the need for integrative strategies that encompass ecological, evolutionary, and environmental sciences. We argue that effective implementation of One Health requires breaking down disciplinary barriers between human and veterinary medicine and the ecological sciences, developing shared indicators for ecosystem health, and fostering systemic approaches to disease emergence and control. The review identifies key obstacles to integration and outlines ambitions for advancing One Health as a global framework capable of informing public policy and promoting sustainable health for humans, animals, plants, and ecosystems alike.

title: Experimental observation of topological Fermi arcs in type-II Weyl semimetal MoTe2
abstract: Weyl semimetals represent a novel quantum state characterized by topologically protected surface states known as Fermi arcs. While type-I Weyl semimetals have been extensively studied, the experimental realization of type-II Weyl semimetals, distinguished by tilted Weyl cones and the coexistence of electron and hole pockets, has remained elusive. Here, we present direct experimental evidence for topological Fermi arcs in orthorhombic MoTe2, a predicted type-II Weyl semimetal. Using a combination of angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and scanning tunneling microscopy (STM), we resolve the surface states and quasi-particle interference patterns associated with the Fermi arcs at the boundary between electron and hole pockets in the Td phase of MoTe2. Our results are supported by first-principles band structure calculations and detailed sample characterization, confirming the high quality and appropriate crystal structure necessary for the emergence of Weyl fermions. The observed Fermi arcs are absent in the centrosymmetric 1T' phase, further corroborating their topological origin. This work establishes MoTe2 as the first experimental realization of a type-II Weyl semimetal and opens new avenues for investigating exotic quantum phenomena in this class of materials.

title: Effects and treatment methods of acupuncture and herbal medicine for premenstrual syndrome/premenstrual dysphoric disorder: systematic review
abstract: During their reproductive years about 10% of women experience some kind of symptoms before menstruation (PMS) in a degree that affects their quality of life (QOL). Acupuncture and herbal medicine has been a recent favorable therapeutic approach. Thus we aimed to review the effects of acupuncture and herbal medicine in the past decade as a preceding research in order to further investigate the most effective Korean Medicine treatment for PMS/PMDD.MethodsA systematic literature search was conducted using electronic databases on studies published between 2002 and 2012. Our review included randomized controlled clinical trials (RCTs) of acupuncture and herbal medicine for PMS/PMDD. Interventions include acupuncture or herbal medicine. Clinical information including statistical tests was extracted from the articles and summarized in tabular form or in the text. Study outcomes were presented as the rate of improvement (%) and/or end-of-treatment scores.ResultsThe search yielded 19 studies. In screening the RCTs, 8 studies in acupuncture and 11 studies in herbal medicine that matched the criteria were identified. Different acupuncture techniques including traditional acupuncture, hand acupuncture and moxibustion, and traditional acupuncture technique with auricular points, have been selected for analysis. In herbal medicine, studies on Vitex Agnus castus, Hypericum perforatum, Xiao yao san, Elsholtzia splendens, Cirsium japonicum, and Gingko biloba L. were identified. Experimental groups with Acupuncture and herbal medicine treatment (all herbal medicine except Cirsium japonicum) had significantly improved results regarding PMS/PMDD.ConclusionsLimited evidence supports the efficacy of alternative medicinal interventions such as acupuncture and herbal medicine in controlling premenstrual syndrome and premenstrual dysphoric disorder. Acupuncture and herbal medicine treatments for premenstrual syndrome and premenstrual dysphoric disorder showed a 50% or better reduction of symptoms compared to the initial state. In both acupuncture and herbal medical interventions, there have been no serious adverse events reported, proving the safety of the interventions while most of the interventions provided over 50% relief of symptoms associated with PMS/PMDD. Stricter diagnostic criteria may have excluded many participants from some studies. Also, depending on the severity of symptoms, the rate of improvement in the outcomes of the studies may have greatly differed.

title: Theory-Guided Machine Learning in Materials Science
abstract: The integration of machine learning into materials science offers significant potential for accelerating discovery and understanding of material properties, yet the unique characteristics of materials data necessitate careful methodological choices. This paper examines the challenges and best practices in applying machine learning to materials informatics, emphasizing the importance of theory-guided approaches. We discuss common pitfalls such as overfitting, particularly in data-scarce environments, and highlight the need for robust validation strategies like cross-validation and Bayesian error estimation. The issue of underrepresented classes in classification tasks is addressed, with recommendations for balancing datasets and penalizing misclassification of minority classes. Using decision trees as a case study, we demonstrate how algorithmic choices and feature selection can yield qualitatively different models, underscoring the necessity of incorporating domain knowledge to ensure physical interpretability and meaningful predictions. The paper advocates for rational descriptor selection and simple, interpretable models, providing a workflow that integrates theoretical understanding with data-driven techniques to enhance reliability and insight in materials research.

title: Developing Difference: Social Organization and the Rise of the Auto Industries of South Korea, Taiwan, Spain, and Argentina
abstract: This paper examines the divergent development trajectories of the automobile industries in South Korea, Taiwan, Spain, and Argentina through a comparative institutional analysis. By focusing on the role of social organization, the study demonstrates how differences in state intervention, industrial policy, labor relations, and business networks shaped each country's path to industrialization and integration into the global automotive sector. The findings reveal that while all four countries faced similar challenges as late industrializers, their unique configurations of social and institutional arrangements led to distinct outcomes in terms of industry structure, competitiveness, and internationalization. The analysis underscores the importance of understanding local social dynamics and institutional contexts in explaining variations in economic development and highlights the limitations of universal models of industrial growth.

title: Kondo physics in carbon nanotubes
abstract: The connection of electrical leads to wire-like molecules is a logical step in the development of molecular electronics, but also allows studies of fundamental physics. For example, metallic carbon nanotubes are quantum wires that have been found to act as one-dimensional quantum dots, Luttinger liquids, proximity-induced superconductors and ballistic and diffusive one-dimensional metals. Here we report that electrically contacted single-walled carbon nanotubes can serve as powerful probes of Kondo physics, demonstrating the universality of the Kondo effect. Arising in the prototypical case from the interaction between a localized impurity magnetic moment and delocalized electrons in a metallic host, the Kondo effect has been used to explain enhanced low-temperature scattering from magnetic impurities in metals, and also occurs in transport through semiconductor quantum dots. The far greater tunability of dots (in our case, nanotubes) compared with atomic impurities renders new classes of Kondo-like effects accessible. Our nanotube devices differ from previous systems in which Kondo effects have been observed, in that they are one-dimensional quantum dots with three-dimensional metal (gold) reservoirs. This allows us to observe Kondo resonances for very large electron numbers (N) in the dot, and approaching the unitary limit (where the transmission reaches its maximum possible value). Moreover, we detect a previously unobserved Kondo effect, occurring for even values of N in a magnetic field.

title: Synthetic biology: applications come of age
abstract: Synthetic biology has rapidly evolved from its conceptual origins, inspired by the analogy between biological and electronic circuits, to a robust engineering discipline capable of designing and constructing novel biomolecular components, genetic circuits, and synthetic pathways. Early successes in building synthetic gene networks such as toggle switches and oscillators demonstrated the feasibility of rationally engineering cellular behavior using modular, model-driven approaches. Over the past decade, advances in genomic tools and genetic engineering have enabled the development of increasingly sophisticated biological devices, including memory elements, pulse generators, logic gates, filters, and communication modules. These engineered systems are now transitioning from proof-of-concept demonstrations to practical applications addressing complex societal challenges. This review highlights the emerging real-world impact of synthetic biology in biosensing, therapeutics, biofuel production, pharmaceuticals, and novel biomaterials. The versatility of synthetic biology platforms lies in their ability to integrate sensing and response modules at multiple regulatory levels, enabling precise control over cellular functions. As synthetic biology matures, its multivalent applicability promises transformative solutions across diverse fields, marking a coming-of-age for the discipline.

title: Handbook of Accelerator Physics and Engineering
abstract: Concerned with the design and operation of modern accelerators including linacs, synchrotrons and storage rings, this text includes both theoretical and practical matters. Chapters on beam dynamics and electromagnetic and nuclear interactions deals with linear and nonlinear single particle and collective effects including spin motion, beam-environment, beam-beam and intrabeam interactions. The impedance concept and calculations are covered along with the instabilities associated with the various interactions mentioned. A chapter on operational considerations deals with orbit error assessment and correction. Chapters on mechanical and electrical considerations present material data and aspects of component design including heat transfer and refrigeration. Hardware systems for particle sources, feedback systems, confinement and acceleration (both normal conduction and superconducting) receive detailed treatment in a subsystems chapter, which also covers beam measurement techniques and apparatus. The closing chapter gives data and methods for radiation protection computations as well as much data on radiation damage to various materials and devices.

title: Unpacking “Participation” in the Adaptive Management of Social–ecological Systems: a Critical Review
abstract: This paper critically reviews the concept of stakeholder participation within the adaptive management of social–ecological systems, drawing on three case studies at varying scales. Through an examination of when and how different stakeholders are engaged across the adaptive management cycle, the study highlights the diversity of participatory mechanisms and their roles in fostering social learning and more democratic environmental governance. The analysis underscores that while participation is widely advocated for its potential to enhance decision-making, legitimacy, and inclusivity, its implementation remains complex due to varying stakeholder interests, power dynamics, and contextual factors. The findings call for more nuanced reflection on participatory processes in adaptive management, emphasizing the need to address both practical and normative challenges while unpacking the interconnections between science, institutions, knowledge, and power to achieve more equitable and effective outcomes.

title: What do people really think of generic medicines? A systematic review and critical appraisal of literature on stakeholder perceptions of generic drugs
abstract: This systematic review critically appraises literature published between 2003 and 2014 on stakeholder perceptions of generic medicines, focusing on physicians, pharmacists, and patients. Searches in PubMed and Scopus identified 16 studies on physician opinions, 11 on pharmacists, and 31 on patient or consumer perspectives, with quantitative surveys predominating. The findings indicate that while acceptance of generic medicines has generally improved across all groups, persistent mistrust remains, particularly among patients who often equate lower cost with reduced quality. Higher educational attainment is associated with greater acceptance of generics, whereas lower socioeconomic status correlates with increased skepticism. The review highlights the importance of targeted education and information dissemination to address misconceptions about equivalency and regulation of generics. Additionally, as patient trust in physicians can override personal doubts about generics, enhancing healthcare professionals’ confidence in these medicines is crucial for broader acceptance and utilization. These insights inform policy strategies aimed at increasing the use of generic medicines to achieve healthcare cost savings.

title: Van der Waals heterostructures
abstract: Research on graphene and other two-dimensional atomic crystals is intense and is likely to remain one of the leading topics in condensed matter physics and materials science for many years. Looking beyond this field, isolated atomic planes can also be reassembled into designer heterostructures made layer by layer in a precisely chosen sequence. The first, already remarkably complex, such heterostructures (often referred to as ‘van der Waals’) have recently been fabricated and investigated, revealing unusual properties and new phenomena. Here we review this emerging research area and identify possible future directions. With steady improvement in fabrication techniques and using graphene’s springboard, van der Waals heterostructures should develop into a large field of their own.

title: Developing Difference: Social Organization and the Rise of the Auto Industries of South Korea, Taiwan, Spain, and Argentina
abstract: Theories of economic development as diverse as modernization, dependency, world-system, and market reform take a “critical factor” view. Proponents of each theory argue that countries fail to develop because of an obstacle to economic growth. We argue instead that neither a critical factor nor a single path leads to economic development; viable paths vary. Economic growth depends on linking a country's historically developed patterns of social organization to the opportunities of global markets. We formulate a sociological theory of cross-national comparative advantage including not only economic factor endowments but also institutionalized patterns of authority and organization. Such patterns legitimize certain actors and certain relationships among those actors, which facilitate development success in some activities but not in others. We illustrate this approach to understanding development outcomes with a comparative analysis of the difficult rise of the automobile assembly and components industries in South Korea, Taiwan, Spain, and Argentina.

title: Understanding the signature pedagogy of the design studio and the opportunities for its technological enhancement
abstract: This paper analyzes the design studio as the signature pedagogy of design education, drawing on theoretical frameworks such as signature pedagogies, conversational models, and pedagogical patterns to examine its unique qualities, strengths, and limitations. Focusing primarily on the architectural studio, the study explores how the studio environment integrates knowledge acquisition, skill development, and professional identity formation through experiential and project-based learning. The analysis highlights the studio’s alignment with deep learning approaches and constructivist principles but also critiques its reliance on traditional hierarchical relationships and the persistence of a hidden curriculum. The paper identifies opportunities for technological enhancement by mapping the core dimensions of studio pedagogy against various delivery modes and media forms, proposing a structured framework for future research and experimentation aimed at enriching the studio experience while addressing its shortcomings.

title: Discontinuity Analysis for Rock Engineering
abstract: Introduction to discontinuities. Measurement of discontinuity characteristics. Discontinuity orientation. Discontinuity frequency. Discontinuity spacing. Discontinuity size. Stresses on discontinuities. Analysis of rigid blocks. Discontinuities and rock strength. Discontinuities and rock deformability. Fluid flow in discontinuities.

title: Modern control engineering
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive overview of modern control engineering, covering fundamental concepts, mathematical modeling, and analytical techniques essential for the design and analysis of control systems. It introduces control system types, contrasts open-loop and closed-loop configurations, and explores Laplace transform methods for solving linear differential equations. The work details the modeling of dynamic systems—including mechanical, electrical, fluid, and thermal domains—using both transfer function and state-space approaches, with practical applications demonstrated through MATLAB. Key topics include transient and steady-state response analyses, stability criteria such as Routh's and Nyquist's methods, root-locus and frequency-response techniques, and compensation strategies for system performance enhancement. Advanced subjects address PID controller design, tuning methodologies, two-degrees-of-freedom control systems, and optimal state-space control including pole placement and observer design. The paper emphasizes computational tools for analysis and synthesis, providing a foundational resource for students and practitioners in modern automatic control engineering.

title: Conducting Polymers for Tissue Engineering.
abstract: Conducting polymers such as polyaniline, polypyrrole, and polythiophene, along with their derivatives, have emerged as promising biomaterials for tissue engineering due to their unique combination of electrical conductivity and biocompatibility. These materials enable electrical stimulation of cells, which can enhance cellular activities such as adhesion, proliferation, and differentiation, making them particularly valuable for engineering electrically responsive tissues including nerve, muscle, cardiac, and bone. However, the inherent brittleness and limited processability of pure conducting polymers have prompted the development of composite biomaterials that integrate conducting polymers with biodegradable natural or synthetic polymers to improve mechanical properties and processability. This review summarizes the fabrication methods and properties of various conductive biomaterials—including films, nanofibers, hydrogels, and scaffolds—produced through techniques such as electrospinning, in situ polymerization, and surface coating. The applications of these materials in tissue engineering are discussed in detail, highlighting advances in bone regeneration, muscle repair, neural interfaces, cardiac tissue engineering, and wound healing. Overall, conducting polymer-based biomaterials represent a versatile platform for developing bioactive scaffolds that support tissue regeneration through both structural and electrical cues.

title: Does the Hubble constant tension call for new physics?
abstract: The tension between local and Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB)-inferred measurements of the Hubble constant (H0) presents a significant challenge to the ΛCDM cosmological model. We assess whether this discrepancy necessitates new physics by exploring modifications to the standard model, including late-time and early dark energy scenarios. Using a Bayesian framework and a comprehensive set of cosmological data—local distance ladder, gravitational lensing, CMB, Type Ia supernovae, baryon acoustic oscillations, and big bang nucleosynthesis—we find that late-time dark energy explanations are mildly disfavored, while models introducing an additional pre-CMB decoupling energy component show marginally positive Bayesian evidence. The equation of state for this early dark energy is constrained to w = 0.086+0.04−0.03, deviating from the value expected for dark radiation but not strongly excluding it. Our results indicate that while current data do not decisively favor new physics, persistent tension and future high-precision H0 measurements could provide critical tests for these extensions to ΛCDM.
venue: Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics

title: Overview of natural hydrogels for regenerative medicine applications
