title: The Impact of Entrepreneurship Education in Higher Education: A Systematic Review and Research Agenda
abstract: Using a teaching model framework, we systematically review empirical evidence on the impact of entrepreneurship education (EE) in higher education on a range of learning outcomes, analysing 159 published articles from 2004-2016. The teaching model framework allows us for the first time to start rigorously examining relationships between pedagogical methods and specific outcomes. Re-confirming past reviews and meta-analyses, we find that EE impact research still predominantly focuses on short-term and subjective outcome measures and tends to severely under-describe the actual pedagogies being tested. Moreover, we use our review to provide an up-to-date and empirically rooted call for less obvious, yet greatly promising, new or underemphasised directions for future research on the impact of university-based entrepreneurship education. This includes, for example, the use of novel impact indicators related to emotion and mindset, focus on the impact indicators related to the intention-to-behaviour transition, and explore the reasons for some of the contradictory findings in impact studies including person-, context- and pedagogical model-specific moderators.

title: Surface chemistry influences implant biocompatibility.
abstract: Implantable medical devices are increasingly important in the practice of modern medicine. Unfortunately, almost all medical devices suffer to a different extent from adverse reactions, including inflammation, fibrosis, thrombosis and infection. To improve the safety and function of many types of medical implants, a major need exists for development of materials that evoked desired tissue responses. Because implant-associated protein adsorption and conformational changes thereafter have been shown to promote immune reactions, rigorous research efforts have been emphasized on the engineering of surface property (physical and chemical characteristics) to reduce protein adsorption and cell interactions and subsequently improve implant biocompatibility. This brief review is aimed to summarize the past efforts and our recent knowledge about the influence of surface functionality on protein:cell:biomaterial interactions. It is our belief that detailed understandings of bioactivity of surface functionality provide an easy, economic, and specific approach for the future rational design of implantable medical devices with desired tissue reactivity and, hopefully, wound healing capability.

title: A Short History of Sociological Thought
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the development of sociological thought from its origins in eighteenth-century social philosophy to contemporary theoretical perspectives. It traces the emergence of sociology as a distinct discipline, examining foundational figures such as Vico, Montesquieu, and the thinkers of the Scottish Enlightenment, and explores the rise of positivism and empiricism in the nineteenth century through the works of Comte, Saint-Simon, Mill, and Spencer. The analysis highlights Marxism’s contributions to understanding capitalist development, class formation, and historical determinism. The paper then examines classical sociology’s critique of positivism through Durkheim’s functionalism and Weber’s interpretive sociology, as well as theories of social action and domination. It further considers the evolution of Marxist thought after Marx, including the ideas of Lukacs and Gramsci. In its discussion of modern sociology, the paper reviews key developments in functionalism, action theory, symbolic interactionism, phenomenology, structuralism, and the sociology of knowledge and culture. The conclusion addresses ongoing debates concerning democracy, industrialization, legitimation, and the future trajectory of sociological theory. Through this historical survey, the paper elucidates how sociological thought has responded to changing social conditions and intellectual currents over time.

title: Projected Marine Heatwaves in the 21st Century and the Potential for Ecological Impact
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are increasingly frequent and intense extreme events with profound ecological and socioeconomic consequences. Using daily sea surface temperature outputs from six CMIP5 global climate models, this study projects changes in MHW characteristics under two greenhouse gas emission scenarios (RCP4.5 and RCP8.5) through 2100. Results indicate a significant acceleration in both the intensity and annual count of MHW days, with many ocean regions projected to experience near-permanent MHW conditions by the late 21st century, particularly under high emissions. The emergence of these trends from natural variability is evident within the first half of the century, underscoring the strong influence of anthropogenic forcing. The projected escalation in MHW exposure is expected to cause widespread, persistent, and potentially irreversible impacts on marine ecosystems, threatening biodiversity, foundational habitats, and ecosystem services globally. These findings highlight the urgent need for mitigation and adaptation strategies to address the escalating risks posed by marine heatwaves in a warming world.

title: The microphysics of collisionless shock waves
abstract: Collisionless shock waves, governed by electromagnetic interactions rather than particle collisions, are fundamental to a wide range of astrophysical and space environments, including supernova remnants, pulsar winds, gamma-ray bursts, and galaxy clusters. This review synthesizes recent advances in the understanding of the microphysical processes underlying collisionless shock formation, dynamics, and particle acceleration. Emphasis is placed on the multi-scale, nonlinear nature of these shocks and the critical roles played by background magnetic field strength, orientation, and shock velocity in shaping instabilities and particle energization. The interplay between high-energy cosmic rays and shock structure is explored through a combination of observational data, analytical theory, and numerical simulations. Key instabilities—driven by resonant particle-wave interactions, return currents, and energetic particle gradients—are examined for their impact on magnetic field amplification and diffusive shock acceleration efficiency. The review also highlights recent progress in laboratory plasma experiments that probe shock microphysics, offering new perspectives on processes relevant to both space and astrophysical shocks.
venue: Reports on progress in physics. Physical Society

title: THE APPLICATIONS OF INTERNATIONAL CLASSIFICATION OF FUNCTIONING, DISABILITY AND HEALTH (ICF) BY WORLD HEALTH ORGANIZATION(WHO) IN REHABILITATION MEDICINE PRACTICE
abstract: The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) by the World Health Organization provides a comprehensive framework for understanding and assessing health, functioning, and disability. This paper explores the practical applications of ICF in rehabilitation medicine at the University of Malaya Medical Centre, Kuala Lumpur. It discusses how ICF’s multidimensional model—encompassing body functions, structures, activities, participation, and environmental factors—aligns with the holistic goals of rehabilitation medicine. The paper highlights the adaptation of ICF through the use of Core Sets tailored for specific health conditions to enhance feasibility in clinical practice, research, and education. Ongoing initiatives include the validation of existing Core Sets and the development of new ones for conditions prevalent in rehabilitation settings. The integration of ICF fosters improved communication among healthcare professionals, patients, and stakeholders by providing a standardized language for describing health and disability. Ultimately, the adoption of ICF enhances patient-centered care, supports interdisciplinary collaboration, and contributes to better health outcomes in rehabilitation medicine.

title: Social Relationships and Health Behavior Across Life Course.
abstract: Sociological theory and research point to the importance of social relationships in affecting health behavior. This work tends to focus on specific stages of the life course, with a division between research on childhood/adolescent and adult populations. Yet recent advances demonstrate that early life course experiences shape health outcomes well into adulthood. We synthesize disparate bodies of research on social ties and health behavior throughout the life course, with attention to explaining how various social ties influence health behaviors at different life stages and how these processes accumulate and reverberate throughout the life course.

title: Hadronic molecules
abstract: The study of hadronic molecules has gained renewed interest following numerous experimental discoveries, particularly in the heavy quarkonium sector, that challenge the traditional quark model. This review systematically examines the concept of hadronic molecules—loosely bound states of hadrons analogous to light nuclei—by surveying experimental evidence across light mesons, open heavy-flavor mesons, heavy quarkonium-like states, and baryons. Methods for identifying hadronic molecules are discussed, including S-matrix properties, compositeness criteria, and characteristic line shapes. Theoretical frameworks such as nonrelativistic effective field theories and lattice QCD are explored for their roles in modeling these states and extracting their properties. The review also addresses production and decay mechanisms, highlighting both long- and short-distance processes as well as the implications of heavy quark symmetries. By critically evaluating the reliability of various claims in the literature and summarizing current phenomenological manifestations, this work provides a comprehensive overview of the status and future directions in the study of hadronic molecules within hadron spectroscopy.

title: Nanotechnology and its Applications in Medicine
abstract: Nanotechnologyis the study of extremely small structures, having size of 0.1 to 100 nm. Nano medicine is a relatively new field of science and technology. Brief explanation of various types of pharmaceutical nano systems is given. Classification of nano materials based on their dimensions is given. An application of Nanotechnology in various fields such as health and medicine, electronics, energy and environment, is discussed in detail. Applications of nano particles in drug delivery, protein and peptide delivery, cancer are explained. Applications of various nano systems in cancer therapy such as carbon nano tube, dendrimers, nano crystal, nano wire, nano shells etc. are given. The advancement in nano technology helps in the treatment of neuro degenerative disorders such as Parkinson’s disease and Alzheimer’s disease. Applications of nano technology in tuberculosis treatment, the clinical application of nanotechnology in operative dentistry, in ophthalmology, in surgery, visualization, tissue engineering, antibiotic resistance, immune response are discussed in this article. Nano pharmaceuticals can be used to detect diseases at much earlier stages.

title: Feminist Praxis: Research, Theory and Epistemology in Feminist Sociology
abstract: This collection critically examines the intersections of research, theory, and epistemology within feminist sociology, foregrounding feminist praxis as both a methodological and political project. Through diverse contributions, it interrogates the academic production of knowledge, challenges traditional divides between quantitative and qualitative methods, and highlights the significance of auto/biographical approaches in feminist research. The volume explores the complexities of defining research topics, negotiating personal and professional identities, and analytically utilizing lived experience to produce situated knowledge. By engaging with written and visual texts, contributors demonstrate how feminist epistemologies disrupt conventional sociological paradigms and offer transformative insights into gender, class, ethnicity, and professional practice. This work advances feminist sociology by illuminating the reflexive processes underpinning feminist inquiry and advocating for methodologies that center women's experiences and challenge dominant power structures in knowledge production.

title: Economic Theory and Experimental Economics
abstract: This paper explores the questions of how economic theory can be used to design and interpret experiments and how experimental results can be used to construct and interpret economic theories. The relationship between economic theory and experiments is modeled and illustrated with examples from both theoretical and experimental work. The emphasis is on combing theory and experiment to the benefit of both.

title: Entropy and area.
abstract: The entropy associated with a free, massless scalar quantum field in its ground state is calculated by tracing over the field degrees of freedom inside an imaginary sphere of radius R, yielding a reduced density matrix for the exterior region. Contrary to the expectation that entropy is extensive and scales with volume, the analysis shows that the resulting entropy is proportional to the surface area of the sphere, S ∝ A, where A is the boundary area. This result is established through explicit computation using coupled harmonic oscillators and then extended to quantum fields with appropriate ultraviolet and infrared cutoffs. The finding parallels the Bekenstein-Hawking formula for black hole entropy, suggesting a more general connection between entropy and area in quantum field theory, independent of gravitational dynamics or special properties of horizons. The implications for black hole thermodynamics and the nature of quantum information in field theory are discussed.

title: Tumor engineering: the other face of tissue engineering.
abstract: Tumor engineering, as the counterpart to traditional tissue engineering, leverages biomimetic strategies to construct complex in vitro models that recapitulate the architecture and function of the in vivo tumor microenvironment. This approach addresses critical limitations of conventional two-dimensional cultures and animal models, enabling more physiologically relevant studies of tumor development, progression, and therapeutic response. By integrating advances in patterning techniques, materials science, and imaging modalities, tumor engineering facilitates the investigation of dynamic interactions among tumor cells, stromal components, extracellular matrix, and vasculature. Such models allow researchers to dissect fundamental questions regarding angiogenesis, invasion, metastasis, and microenvironmental heterogeneity—questions that are difficult to answer using existing in vivo or in vitro systems. The commentary highlights recent progress in engineering perfused microvasculature within hydrogels and combinatorial microenvironment arrays to study spatial and temporal aspects of tumor biology. Ultimately, the authors advocate for increased collaboration between physical and life scientists to further develop tumor engineering as a discipline, not only to advance regenerative medicine but also to unravel the complexity of cancer biology and improve therapeutic strategies.

title: A Holistic Approach to Marine Eco-Systems Biology
abstract: Marine ecosystems play a critical role in regulating Earth’s biogeochemical cycles and climate, yet their complexity and dynamics remain insufficiently understood. This paper presents the Tara Oceans project, a global, multidisciplinary initiative that integrates optical and genomic methods to systematically sample and analyze viruses, bacteria, archaea, protists, and metazoans across diverse oceanic environments and depths. By combining traditional and innovative sampling techniques with high-throughput sequencing, quantitative imaging, and advanced bioinformatics, the project generates comprehensive open-access datasets linking organismal diversity to physico-chemical parameters. This holistic approach enables unprecedented insights into the morphological, genetic, and functional biodiversity of planktonic communities, their ecological interactions, and their roles in global biogeochemical processes. The Tara Oceans consortium’s coordinated efforts aim to inform ecosystem modeling, improve predictions of climate impacts and fish stock distributions, and uncover novel bioactive compounds, ultimately advancing our understanding and stewardship of marine ecosystems.

title: The Evolutionary synthesis : perspectives on the unification of biology
abstract: It is common knowledge that the theories proposed by Darwin in his Origin encountered massive resistance. But there were considerable differences in the degree of acceptance of his various theories, particularly among the biological disciplines. The naturalists (taxonomists), for instance, favored evolutionary theories different from those of the experimental zoologists. The paleontologists, again, had preferences somewhat different from those of the students of living organisms. The result was one controversy after another, until finally, in the years 1937 to 1947, a general consensus was reached, now referred to as the evolutionary synthesis. In order to understand why such a synthesis was necessary and how it was accomplished, one must review the entire history of the Darwinian controversies after 1859. Within this period a number of shorter periods can be distinguised, each of which became the background for the ensuing period.

title: The rise of graphene.
abstract: Graphene is a rapidly rising star on the horizon of materials science and condensed-matter physics. This strictly two-dimensional material exhibits exceptionally high crystal and electronic quality, and, despite its short history, has already revealed a cornucopia of new physics and potential applications, which are briefly discussed here. Whereas one can be certain of the realness of applications only when commercial products appear, graphene no longer requires any further proof of its importance in terms of fundamental physics. Owing to its unusual electronic spectrum, graphene has led to the emergence of a new paradigm of 'relativistic' condensed-matter physics, where quantum relativistic phenomena, some of which are unobservable in high-energy physics, can now be mimicked and tested in table-top experiments. More generally, graphene represents a conceptually new class of materials that are only one atom thick, and, on this basis, offers new inroads into low-dimensional physics that has never ceased to surprise and continues to provide a fertile ground for applications.

title: Cell encapsulation in biodegradable hydrogels for tissue engineering applications.
abstract: Encapsulating cells in biodegradable hydrogels offers numerous attractive features for tissue engineering, including ease of handling, a highly hydrated tissue-like environment for cell and tissue growth, and the ability to form in vivo. Many properties important to the design of a hydrogel scaffold, such as swelling, mechanical properties, degradation, and diffusion, are closely linked to the crosslinked structure of the hydrogel, which is controlled through a variety of different processing conditions. Degradation may be tuned by incorporating hydrolytically or enzymatically labile segments into the hydrogel or by using natural biopolymers that are susceptible to enzymatic degradation. Because cells are present during the gelation process, the number of suitable chemistries and formulations are limited. In this review, we describe important considerations for designing biodegradable hydrogels for cell encapsulation and highlight recent advances in material design and their applications in tissue engineering.

title: The Condensed matter physics of QCD
abstract: This paper explores the behavior of quantum chromodynamics (QCD) at high baryon density and low temperature, applying concepts and methods from condensed matter physics to analyze the emergence of novel phases such as color superconductivity. The authors demonstrate that, at asymptotically high densities, the combination of asymptotic freedom and BCS theory allows for a controlled theoretical treatment, revealing the formation of diquark condensates analogous to Cooper pairs in conventional superconductors. The phenomenon of color-flavor locking is identified as a particularly robust and symmetric ground state in three-flavor QCD, leading to spontaneous breaking of color and chiral symmetries, the generation of energy gaps for colored excitations, and the appearance of new collective modes. The study systematically examines variants with different numbers of quark flavors and colors, discusses calculational techniques including renormalization group methods and variational approaches, and constructs a tentative phase diagram for QCD as a function of temperature and density. Potential astrophysical implications are addressed, especially regarding the properties of neutron star interiors and observable signatures such as cooling rates and magnetic field evolution. The work highlights both the theoretical advances made possible by condensed matter analogies and the open challenges in understanding dense QCD matter.

title: The Three R's: How Community Based Participatory Research Strengthens the Rigor, Relevance and Reach of Science.
abstract: In the last few decades, community based participatory research (CBPR) has emerged as an important approach that links environmental health and justice advocates with research institutions to understand and address environmental health problems. CBPR has generally been evaluated for its impact on policy, regulation, and its support of community science. However, there has been less emphasis on assessing the ways in which CBPR (re)shapes and potentially improves the scientific enterprise itself. This commentary focuses on this under-emphasized aspect of CBPR-how it can strengthen science. Using two case studies of environmental health CBPR research-the Northern California Exposure Study, and the San Joaquin Valley Drinking Water Study-we posit that CBPR helps improve the '3 R's'of science-rigor, relevance and reach-and in so doing benefits the scientific enterprise itself.

title: Ten Chemical Innovations That Will Change Our World: IUPAC identifies emerging technologies in Chemistry with potential to make our planet more sustainable
abstract: This paper presents the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry’s (IUPAC) initiative to identify ten emerging chemical technologies with the potential to significantly advance global sustainability. Marking the centennial of IUPAC and the 150th anniversary of Mendeleev’s Periodic Table, the study highlights how chemistry continues to shape society and address pressing challenges. Through a rigorous selection process involving global experts, IUPAC has spotlighted innovations such as nanopesticides, enantio-selective organocatalysis, solid-state batteries, flow chemistry, and reactive extrusion. These technologies promise to enhance agricultural productivity with reduced environmental impact, enable greener and more efficient synthesis of chemicals and pharmaceuticals, improve energy storage safety and performance, and minimize hazardous waste through solvent-free processes. The paper discusses both the scientific breakthroughs and the practical hurdles facing these innovations as they transition from laboratory research to industrial application. By showcasing these advances, IUPAC aims to inspire further research, foster interdisciplinary collaboration, and accelerate the adoption of sustainable chemical solutions worldwide.

title: Molecular transport junctions: vibrational effects
abstract: Transport of electrons in a single molecule junction is the simplest problem in the general subject area of molecular electronics. In the past few years, this area has been extended to probe beyond the simple tunnelling associated with large energy gaps between electrode Fermi level and molecular levels, to deal with smaller gaps, with near-resonance tunnelling and, particularly, with effects due to interaction of electronic and vibrational degrees of freedom. This overview is devoted to the theoretical and computational approaches that have been taken to understanding transport in molecular junctions when these vibronic interactions are involved. After a short experimental overview, and discussion of different test beds and measurements, we define a particular microscopic model Hamiltonian. That overall Hamiltonian can be used to discuss all of the phenomena dealt with subsequently. These include transition from coherent to incoherent transport as electron/vibration interaction increases in strength, inelastic electron tunnelling spectroscopy and its interpretation and measurement, affects of interelectronic repulsion treated at the Hubbard level, noise in molecular transport junctions, non-linear conductance phenomena, heating and heat conduction in molecular transport junctions and current-induced chemical reactions. In each of these areas, we use the same simple model Hamiltonian to analyse energetics and dynamics. While this overview does not attempt survey the literature exhaustively, it does provide appropriate references to the current literature (both experimental and theoretical). We also attempt to point out directions in which further research is required to answer cardinal questions concerning the behaviour and understanding of vibrational effects in molecular transport junctions.

title: Authentic Assessment and Pedagogical Strategies in Higher Education
abstract: This study investigates the implementation of authentic assessment and its alignment with pedagogical strategies in higher education in Malaysia. Employing a qualitative research design, data were collected through interviews, document analysis, and classroom observations involving two lecturers and twenty students from a postgraduate course. The findings reveal that various forms of authentic assessment, when integrated with suitable pedagogical approaches, enhance student engagement, promote deeper learning, and are generally preferred over traditional standardized assessments. The study underscores the importance of aligning assessment methods with instructional practices and recommends that authentic assessment be embedded as a formative process within the instructional cycle. Providing timely feedback from both lecturers and peers is highlighted as essential for supporting students’ self-assessment, identifying learning needs, and fostering continuous improvement. The results suggest that adopting authentic assessment practices can better prepare students for real-world challenges and lifelong learning.

title: Peptide and protein sequence analysis by electron transfer dissociation mass spectrometry.
abstract: Peptide sequence analysis using a combination of gas-phase ion/ion chemistry and tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) is demonstrated. Singly charged anthracene anions transfer an electron to multiply protonated peptides in a radio frequency quadrupole linear ion trap (QLT) and induce fragmentation of the peptide backbone along pathways that are analogous to those observed in electron capture dissociation. Modifications to the QLT that enable this ion/ion chemistry are presented, and automated acquisition of high-quality, single-scan electron transfer dissociation MS/MS spectra of phosphopeptides separated by nanoflow HPLC is described.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Defect Engineering: Tuning the Porosity and Composition of the Metal–Organic Framework UiO-66 via Modulated Synthesis
abstract: Presented in this paper is a deep investigation into the defect chemistry of UiO-66 when synthesized in the presence of monocarboxylic acid modulators under the most commonly employed conditions. We unequivocally demonstrate that missing cluster defects are the predominant defect and that their concentration (and thus the porosity and composition of the material) can be tuned to a remarkable extent by altering the concentration and/or acidity of the modulator. Finally, we attempt to rationalize these observations by speculating on the underlying solution chemistry.

title: What Is (Business) Management? Laying the Ground for a Philosophy of Management
abstract: In this article, we philosophically reflect on the nature of business management. We move beyond the political paradigm of the conceptualization of management in order to lay the ground for a philosophy of business management. First, we open-up the self-evident conceptualization of business management in contemporary management practices by comparing ancient and contemporary definitions of management. Second, we develop a framework with six dimensions of the nature of business management that can guide future philosophical and empirical work on the nature of business management: management control, people management, asset management and entrepreneurial action, management as participation, management as responsive action and management as constituting meaning.

title: Development cycle 2 of the Modular Earth Submodel System (MESSy2)
abstract: The second development cycle of the Modular Earth Submodel System (MESSy2) advances the framework for constructing comprehensive Earth System Models (ESMs) by introducing significant infrastructural enhancements and new submodels. MESSy2 features a redesigned, basemodel-independent memory and meta-data management interface (CHANNEL), enabling flexible coupling of process submodels across diverse basemodels and improving data handling and export capabilities. Additional generic submodels, such as TIMER and QTIMER, optimize time control and resource management. The system is further extended with new diagnostic and process submodels, as well as updates to the atmospheric chemistry setup, supporting more robust model evaluation against observational data. These developments establish a foundation for expanding from Chemistry Climate Models toward fully integrated ESMs, with an emphasis on modularity, flexibility, and continuous re-evaluation to accommodate ongoing scientific and technical advancements.

title: The Development of Local Wisdom-Based Natural Science Module to Improve Science Literation of Students
abstract: This study aims to develop a natural science module based on local wisdom to enhance students’ science literacy, particularly in disaster-prone areas near Mount Kelud. Employing a Research and Development (R&D) approach with the ASSURE instructional design model, the module integrates local knowledge and cultural practices related to volcanic eruptions into science learning materials. Theoretical validation by experts showed high feasibility across material, presentation, language, local wisdom integration, and science literacy components, each scoring above 87% in the “very good” category. Empirical testing with students demonstrated improvements in science literacy, with N-gain values ranging from low to medium categories (0.2–0.4). These results indicate that the developed module is both theoretically sound and empirically effective in fostering students’ understanding of scientific concepts through the context of their local environment and experiences, supporting the integration of local wisdom as a valuable resource in science education.

title: Noise stability of functions with low influences: Invariance and optimality
abstract: In this paper, we study functions with low influences on product probability spaces. The analysis of Boolean functions f {-1, 1}/sup n/ /spl rarr/ {-1, 1} with low influences has become a central problem in discrete Fourier analysis. It is motivated by fundamental questions arising from the construction of probabilistically checkable proofs in theoretical computer science and from problems in the theory of social choice in economics. We prove an invariance principle for multilinear polynomials with low influences and bounded degree; it shows that under mild conditions the distribution of such polynomials is essentially invariant for all product spaces. Ours is one of the very few known non-linear invariance principles. It has the advantage that its proof is simple and that the error bounds are explicit. We also show that the assumption of bounded degree can be eliminated if the polynomials are slightly 'smoothed'; this extension is essential for our applications to 'noise stability '-type problems. In particular; as applications of the invariance principle we prove two conjectures: the 'Majority Is Stablest' conjecture [29] from theoretical computer science, which was the original motivation for this work, and the 'It Ain't Over Till It's Over' conjecture [27] from social choice theory. The 'Majority Is Stablest' conjecture and its generalizations proven here, in conjunction with the 'Unique Games Conjecture' and its variants, imply a number of (optimal) inapproximability results for graph problems.
venue: IEEE Annual Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science

title: The role of representative design in an ecological approach to cognition.
abstract: This paper examines the significance of representative design within an ecological approach to cognition, drawing on Egon Brunswik’s theoretical and methodological contributions. Representative design, which involves sampling or constructing experimental stimuli that preserve the statistical properties of the natural environment, contrasts with traditional systematic design that prioritizes internal validity at the expense of ecological realism. The authors review the historical development and theoretical foundations of representative design, analyze its limited adoption in contemporary cognitive psychology—particularly in judgment and decision-making research—and demonstrate how experimental outcomes can be shaped by design choices. They argue that representative design enhances the external validity and generalizability of psychological findings by aligning experimental conditions with real-world organism–environment relations. The paper also discusses practical challenges to implementing representative design and suggests that advances in technology may help overcome these barriers. Ultimately, the authors contend that representative design is essential for a truly ecological approach to cognition and advocate for its broader integration into psychological research methodology.

title: Topic Modeling in Management Research: Rendering New Theory from Textual Data
abstract: This paper reviews the emergence and application of topic modeling as a methodological innovation in management research, highlighting its capacity to generate new theoretical constructs and conceptual relationships from large-scale textual data. By positioning topic modeling as a rendering process that bridges qualitative and quantitative approaches, the authors distinguish it from related techniques such as content analysis, grounded theorizing, and general natural language processing. The review outlines the steps involved in rendering with topic modeling and analyzes its contributions to five key areas of management theory: detecting novelty and emergence, developing inductive classification systems, understanding online audiences and products, analyzing frames and social movements, and exploring cultural dynamics. The authors further discuss recent trends in topic modeling and emphasize the continued importance of researcher interpretation alongside computational analysis. Ultimately, the paper demonstrates how topic modeling can advance theory building in management by enabling scholars to systematically extract meaning from complex textual corpora while maintaining interpretive rigor.

title: Avogadro: an advanced semantic chemical editor, visualization, and analysis platform
abstract: BackgroundThe Avogadro project has developed an advanced molecule editor and visualizer designed for cross-platform use in computational chemistry, molecular modeling, bioinformatics, materials science, and related areas. It offers flexible, high quality rendering, and a powerful plugin architecture. Typical uses include building molecular structures, formatting input files, and analyzing output of a wide variety of computational chemistry packages. By using the CML file format as its native document type, Avogadro seeks to enhance the semantic accessibility of chemical data types.ResultsThe work presented here details the Avogadro library, which is a framework providing a code library and application programming interface (API) with three-dimensional visualization capabilities; and has direct applications to research and education in the fields of chemistry, physics, materials science, and biology. The Avogadro application provides a rich graphical interface using dynamically loaded plugins through the library itself. The application and library can each be extended by implementing a plugin module in C++ or Python to explore different visualization techniques, build/manipulate molecular structures, and interact with other programs. We describe some example extensions, one which uses a genetic algorithm to find stable crystal structures, and one which interfaces with the PackMol program to create packed, solvated structures for molecular dynamics simulations. The 1.0 release series of Avogadro is the main focus of the results discussed here.ConclusionsAvogadro offers a semantic chemical builder and platform for visualization and analysis. For users, it offers an easy-to-use builder, integrated support for downloading from common databases such as PubChem and the Protein Data Bank, extracting chemical data from a wide variety of formats, including computational chemistry output, and native, semantic support for the CML file format. For developers, it can be easily extended via a powerful plugin mechanism to support new features in organic chemistry, inorganic complexes, drug design, materials, biomolecules, and simulations. Avogadro is freely available under an open-source license from http://avogadro.openmolecules.net.

title: An invitation to loop quantum gravity
abstract: We describe the basic assumptions and key results of loop quantum gravity, which is a background independent approach to quantum gravity. The emphasis is on the basic physical principles and how one deduces predictions from them, at a level suitable for physicsts in other areas such as string theory, cosmology, particle physics, astrophysics and condensed matter physics. No details are given, but references are provided to guide the interested reader to the literature. The present state of knowledge is summarized in a list of 35 key results on topics including the hamiltonian and path integral quantizations, coupling to matter, extensions to supergravity and higher dimensional theories, as well as applications to black holes, cosmology and Plank scale phenomenology. We describe the near term prospects for observational tests of quantum theories of gravity and the expectations that loop quantum gravity may provide predictions for their outcomes. Finally, we provide answers to frequently asked questions and a list of key open problems.
